title: tests/Main.hs still threads Proxy tokens through six law-helper functions
description:
Left over from sized-grid-all (2026-08-11), deliberately.

tests/Test/Utils.hs exports six helpers that all take a 'Proxy' as a type token:

    semigroupLaws, monoidLaws, additiveGroupLaws, affineSpaceLaws, aesonLaws,
    isCoordLaws

and tests/Main.hs calls them in groups sharing one binding:

    let p = Proxy @(Periodic 10)
    in [ semigroupLaws p, monoidLaws p, ..., isCoordLaws p ]

sized-grid-all removed Proxy from the *library* API but left these alone. The
reason: converting one of six siblings would have been worse than converting
none, since they share the 'p' binding at every call site, and converting all
six is a separate refactor with its own churn.

These are also a different use of Proxy from the one that issue was about. They
carry a *type* to test, not a size, and the visible-forall form is awkward for
types whose constructors share their name -- 'twoDimensionalCoordTests (type
(Coord '[HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]))' needs the 'type' keyword because 'Coord'
is also a data constructor. The natural fix here is AllowAmbiguousTypes plus a
type application ('isCoordLaws @Periodic @10'), not a required type argument.
acceptance_criteria: The six helpers take their type by application rather than by Proxy, tests/Main.hs no longer binds 'p', and the suite still passes with no new warnings.
close_reason: Converted all nine law helpers (semigroupLaws, monoidLaws, additiveGroupLaws, affineSpaceLaws, aesonLaws, isCoordLaws, comonadLaws, representableLaws, distributiveLaws) from Proxy args to AllowAmbiguousTypes + type application. tests/Main.hs no longer binds 'p'; testAllCoordOrdered/testCoordLayout/eq1Laws/functorLaws etc keep taking Proxy since they were out of scope. cabal build clean (no warnings), cabal test: all 485 tests pass.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text: Scope grew on 2026-08-12 (sized-grid-ryy): Test.Utils now has NINE Proxy-threaded law helpers, not six. The three new ones -- comonadLaws, representableLaws, distributiveLaws -- were deliberately written in the existing Proxy style rather than the type-application style this issue proposes, so that the conversion is one uniform change instead of leaving the module in two styles at once. Nothing here is harder as a result; there is just more of it.

title: Extract SeamTable as atlas-topology's core: the gluing combinatorics, not the chart contents
description:
## Decision

Supersedes sized-grid-jtt. The criterion for extracting isn't "does an outside consumer exist yet" -- it's "is there a self-contained abstraction here with plausible growth." There is: the seam/gluing table (chart id + boundary label + involution) is already payload-agnostic in cubeSeam's actual shape and already checked as such by tests that never mention Grid. Target: a future `atlas-topology` package holding this core. Not building it yet -- this issue records the intended shape so extraction is a mechanical lift when it happens, not a redesign.

## Rationale

Re-examining Data.Grid.Atlas.CubeMap against the "does this need Grid" question sized-grid-ts4 asked, one layer resolves cleanly and one doesn't:

**Already payload-agnostic, evidenced by the existing tests (not a guess):**
- `Face`, `Axis`, `Extremum`, `Heading` -- plain enums, no Grid/coordinate reference.
- `cubeSeam :: Face -> Axis -> Extremum -> (Face, Axis, Extremum, Bool)` is a fixed-point-free involution over `(chart, boundary-label)` pairs -- exactly a manifold atlas's transition functions, discretized, generalized only by parameterizing the chart-id type (was Face) and boundary-label type (was (Axis, Extremum)).
- Its correctness property, `cubeSeamPairsUp` (every half-edge pairs with exactly one other, pointing back), is a property of *any* seam table: crossing a seam and crossing back lands exactly where you started with the same orientation bit. Nothing about that law mentions squares or cells.

**Still one data point, left alone:**
- `cubeStep`'s coordinate arithmetic -- detecting a boundary crossing within a chart and applying the landing coordinate -- is tied to `Ordinal n x Ordinal n` grid stepping. Generalizing "what a chart is and how it detects its own boundary" (a typeclass like `HasBoundary chart pos boundary`) would still be fixing an API against a single example (is a chart always coordinate-shaped? could it be a bare graph node, per sized-grid-ts4's original "pathfinding" aside?). That question stays open, tracked separately, not designed here.

## Generalized shape (design only, not yet built)

    -- | A single half-edge: which chart, and which boundary feature of it.
    type HalfEdge chart boundary = (chart, boundary)

    -- | The gluing table: crossing a named boundary of a chart lands on
    -- another chart at another named boundary, plus whether the
    -- along-the-seam direction is preserved or reversed. 'cubeSeam'
    -- generalized by parameterizing Face -> chart, (Axis, Extremum) ->
    -- boundary.
    newtype SeamTable chart boundary = SeamTable
      { crossSeam :: chart -> boundary -> (chart, boundary, Bool) }

    -- | The one law every seam table must satisfy -- 'cubeSeamPairsUp'
    -- generalized. Checkable purely combinatorially via Bounded/Enum
    -- enumeration, no chart contents involved.
    seamIsInvolution ::
         (Eq chart, Eq boundary)
      => SeamTable chart boundary -> chart -> boundary -> Bool
    seamIsInvolution (SeamTable cross) c b =
      let (c', b', flip1) = cross c b
          (c'', b'', flip2) = cross c' b'
      in (c'', b'', flip2) == (c, b, flip1)

CubeMap's `cubeSeam` becomes `SeamTable Face (Axis, Extremum)`; `cubeSeamPairsUp` becomes `seamIsInvolution` applied over all `(Face, Axis, Extremum)`. `cubeStepBeltCloses` (the belt-closure property) stays put -- it exercises the coordinate-stepping half, not the seam table alone.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Gate on an external consumer showing up first (sized-grid-jtt's original call)**: rejected on reflection -- the seam-table half isn't a guess about what a future consumer wants, it's a description of what cubeSeam already does structurally, with its own tests as evidence. Waiting for outside pull conflates "no consumer" with "no design basis," which is wrong here.
- **Extract the whole chart/seam/coordinate-stepping layer together (original sized-grid-ts4 framing)**: rejected -- would drag the one-data-point coordinate-arithmetic layer along with the well-evidenced seam-table layer, which is exactly the speculative half.
- **Design AND build atlas-topology now**: deferred at the user's request -- this issue captures the shape so the eventual build is a lift, not a design session.

## Affects

- sized-grid-jtt (superseded by this decision)
- sized-grid-ts4 (the original question)
- sized-grid-fh2, sized-grid-68j (the two atlases the design is drawn from)
close_reason: Decision recorded: SeamTable/HalfEdge design captured for future atlas-topology extraction; not building yet per sized-grid-b15's explicit go-ahead gate.

title: Space-group framing: every boundary policy is a quotient Z^n/G
description:
The organising idea behind the whole boundary-policy catalogue, worth recording
because it turns an ad-hoc list into a classification.

    grid space  =  Z^n / G

An infinite integer lattice, quotiented by a discrete group G of rigid
transformations of that lattice. Every boundary policy is a choice of G. Every
step is then two moves:

    1. add the displacement in Z^n, ignoring edges entirely
    2. reduce the result to its canonical representative under G

  G                                       policy
  ---------------------------------------------------------------
  trivial                                 infinite / unbounded
  pure translations (x+w, y+h)            torus
  translation + one-axis reflection       Mobius
  translation + alternating reflections   Klein bottle
  antipodal identification                projective plane
  reflections (a Coxeter group)           billiard / mirror
  octahedral rotations                    cube map

WHY IT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN DECORATIVE

  * It says what the complete catalogue IS. The policies are not an open-ended
    wishlist; they are the discrete subgroups of the isometries of Z^n, and in
    2D that is the 17 wallpaper groups. That is a finite target.
  * The reduction step is where the frame transform comes from, for free: an
    element of G is an affine map `T(x) = Ax + b` with A a unimodular integer
    matrix, and A IS the seam rule's `Needle -> Needle`. So the seam-rule issue
    and this one are the same fact stated at different altitudes, and the
    matrix form suggests the representation: signed permutations of n axes, a
    finite enumerable group, no closures.
  * It explains cleanly why Clamped and Ordinal are NOT in this table.
    Quotienting is information-preserving up to the group action; clamping
    destroys information and ordinal refuses. They are not quotients of Z^n,
    they are a bounded fundamental domain with the outside deleted. That is the
    real reason they have no lawful PseudoAffine instance, and it is a better
    reason than "the laws happen not to hold".

CAVEAT

Do not turn the library into this. The value is as a classification that says
which policies exist and where each one's frame transform comes from; it is not
a proposal to represent coordinates as group cosets at run time. The per-axis
`IsCoord` representation stays.
close_reason: Documented as a Haddock note on the IsCoord class (src/Data/Grid/Sized/Coord/Class.hs): the grid space = Z^n/G framing, the two-move step (add in Z^n, reduce to canonical representative under G), the A x + b matrix tying to axisFrameFlipsIsCoord's Bool at one axis, the rank-1 G -> instance table (Periodic = translation, Reflective/Reflect101 = reflection), why per-axis products are exactly the separable policies (sized-grid-3u1) and why Mobius/Klein/projective/cube-map are not (block-diagonal vs off-diagonal G, needing the atlas layer sized-grid-fh2), and why Ordinal/Clamped are excluded (not quotients -- refused or destroyed, not identified). Ends with the caveat: classification only, per-axis IsCoord representation unchanged. Builds, haddocks, and all 415 tests pass.

title: Mobius seam table's Straight entries are placeholders, not gluings
description:
mobiusSeam is a SeamTable () (Axis, Extremum), and SeamTable is total, so it has to answer for the Straight edges even though nothing is glued there. It answers with the identity: crossing the straight edge lands on the same edge of the same chart, non-reversing. That satisfies seamIsInvolution and is checked by mobiusSeamPairsUp, so the test passes on an entry that describes no gluing at all.

Since sized-grid-4wn the real answer is given elsewhere: mobiusStep's 'glued' lookup returns Nothing for (Straight, _) before consulting the table, which is what rectStep's Applicative parameter is for. So the table's Straight rows are now visibly dead as gluings while still being covered by the involution test.

Data.Atlas.Topology.Seam's own haddock names the fix: a caller wanting partial seams instantiates chart or boundary with a Maybe-ish type of its own. Options are to make the boundary label say which edges can be glued (SeamTable () Extremum, describing only the wrapped seam, with mobiusStep adapting), or to leave it. Either way mobiusSeamPairsUp's enumeration changes to match, which is the real work.

Not urgent: nothing is wrong at runtime, and the placeholder is 2 of 4 entries in one small table.

title: toJSON pays a vector conversion at the axis-list recursion boundary
description:
toJSON (and parseJSON) recurse down the axis list at a concrete boxed vector, and the generic instance converts at the boundary with VG.convert -- for a boxed grid, a copy between a type and itself. Costs toJSON about 19%.

collapseGrid and gridFromList (originally also named in this issue) are FIXED: see the RULES added in Data.Grid.Sized.Internal.Grid (collapseGrid/boxed, gridFromList/boxed) and bd memory sized-grid-2g0-collapsegrid-gridfromlist-fixed-via-rules. That technique does not reach toJSON/parseJSON: they are class methods, so a RULE only sees the opaque ToJSON/FromJSON dictionary, not the AllSizedKnown cs / ToJSON a pieces the recursion needs, and RULES pragmas do not accept their own class context.

The only remaining angle is an internal v-to-boxed-conversion class (V.Vector -> id, VG.Vector v a -> VG.convert, overlappable) dispatched from inside the ToJSON/FromJSON instances. That constraint would sit in the instance context, which would break any function written polymorphically over v that calls toJSON internally (the same style collapseGrid itself uses) unless it also picks up the new constraint. Considered not worth it unless someone actually needs the 19% back -- these remain boundary operations nobody reaches for either representation to speed up.
notes:
RESOLVED (partially): collapseGrid and gridFromList fixed via RULES at v ~ V.Vector, bypassing VG.convert entirely with zero public API change. toJSON/parseJSON left as documented residual cost -- see full writeup in the memory below and the updated $recursion doc comment in Data.Grid.Sized.Internal.Grid.
WONTFIX for the toJSON/parseJSON residual: nobody has asked for the 19% back, and the only fix (an internal v-to-boxed-conversion class dispatched from the ToJSON/FromJSON instances) would leak a constraint into those instance contexts, breaking any polymorphic-over-v function that calls toJSON internally. Closing rather than filing a separate low-priority follow-up -- this issues description already has the full angle and reasoning if it needs picking up later.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
REVERTING TO OPTION 2 IS A LEGITIMATE RESOLUTION OF THIS ISSUE, and should be weighed before
engineering around the conversion.

This regression exists only because up6 chose option 1 (parameterise Grid over its vector). Option 2
-- a separate hand-written unboxed module -- touches no existing code, so collapseGrid and toJSON
would be bit-for-bit the boxed originals and this issue would not exist.

That option was re-examined empirically after up6 shipped. It was built as a working prototype
against pre-change master and it compiles: 25 functions, ~246 lines, including a second
ShrinkableUGrid class. Unboxed performance is a wash -- within noise of option 1 on every workload,
~5-9% ahead on tabulate and transpose. Full details in bd memories (search 'option 1' or
'option 2').

So the real choice for this issue is three-way, not two-way:
  a. Engineer around VG.convert while keeping option 1 (the angles listed in the description).
  b. Give the BOXED grid its own monomorphic collapseGrid/gridFromList/toJSON/parseJSON and let the
     generic ones serve only other vector types. Cheap and certain to work -- but it is
     re-introducing option 2's duplication at exactly the four functions where option 1's
     'one implementation' thesis is weakest, so it should be recognised as a partial retreat rather
     than a fix.
  c. Revert up6 to option 2 wholesale.

(b) is probably the pragmatic answer if the 19% ever matters. (c) is only worth it if the option-1
complexity -- AllowAmbiguousTypes, the four recursion helpers, the gridFromList annotation, worse
type errors -- turns out to cost more in practice than the duplication would have. Nothing observed
so far says it does.

Weighing against all of these: nobody has reported that 19% mattering. These are boundary
operations. Leaving it alone remains defensible.

title: takeGrid and splitHigherDim have unsound type signatures (no n <= m; z unconstrained)
description:
CONFIRMED empirically.

1) takeGrid -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:197-198

    takeGrid :: KnownNat n => Proxy n -> Grid '[c m] x -> Grid '[c n] x
    takeGrid p (Grid v) = Grid $ V.take (fromIntegral $ natVal p) v

Missing 'n <= m'. Probe:
    takeGrid (Proxy @9) (gridFromList [1,2,3] :: Grid '[Ordinal 3] Int) :: Grid '[Ordinal 9] Int
    => unGrid length 3, while the type claims 9. Invariant broken, silently.

2) splitHigherDim -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:200-219

    splitHigherDim :: forall c as x y z a. (KnownNat x, KnownNat y, y <= x, ...)
      => Grid (c x ': as) a -> (Grid (c y ': as) a, Grid (c z ': as) a)

'z' is a completely free type variable in the result. The caller picks any z they
like and the second component's type is a lie unless they happen to pick x - y.
tests/Main.hs:136-138 only passes because it annotates z correctly by hand.

3) dropGrid -- src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:190-195 has the same shape of problem;
   'm - n' is stuck rather than checked when n > m.

Fix: add 'n <= m' to takeGrid/dropGrid and fix splitHigherDim's result to
'Grid (c (x - y) ': as) a'. This is a breaking API change but restores the
core guarantee the library exists to provide.

Related: this class of hole is exactly what ghc-typelits-natnormalise +
ghc-typelits-knownnat make cheap to state and discharge.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. takeGrid and dropGrid now require 'n <= m'; splitHigherDim's remainder is 'c (x - y)' instead of a free variable.

The stricter signatures immediately caught a fourth bug: ShrinkableGrid's window constraint had x and y transposed. Filed and fixed as sized-grid-px9.

Consequence for the tests: the two cases that used to fail at RUNTIME are now compile errors ('Cannot satisfy: 9 <= 3'), so they cannot be runtime assertions any more. They are documented in tests/Test/Invariant.hs and a compile-fail harness is filed as sized-grid-cti. The positive half (sizes promised == sizes held) is still asserted.

No impact on ../aoc: it uses none of takeGrid/dropGrid/splitHigherDim/shrinkGrid.

title: Boundaryless: the marker class that makes path fusion sound, and turns walkPath total
description:
Follows the sketch in the sized-grid-gyn comment, with one correction and one
addition, both verified by building them (GHC 9.12.3).

== Correction to the sketch recorded on sized-grid-gyn

That comment proposes

    class IsCoord c => Boundaryless c
    instance Boundaryless Periodic

and then `All Boundaryless cs` on a fusion-dependent signature. That does not
typecheck. IsCoord is indexed by the container (kind Nat -> Type), but the
axis list cs :: [Type] holds Periodic 10, not Periodic. GHC 9.12.3 rejects it:

    Couldn't match kind 'Nat -> *' with '*'
    Expected kind '[*]', but 'cs' has kind '[Nat -> *]'

The class has to be at kind Type, mirroring the existing IsCoord /
IsCoordLifted split. A marker class has no methods with n quantified, so it
needs no container-level twin -- one lifted class is enough.

== Proposed

    -- | An axis with no walls: the translation action is total and associative.
    class (IsCoordLifted x, AffineSpace x, Diff x ~ Int, Group x) => Boundaryless x
    instance (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Boundaryless (Periodic n)

Laws (none checkable by GHC; all stated in the Haddock and tested):

  1. axisBoundary x         == Nothing              -- no value is at an end
  2. offsetIsCoord x d      == Just (x .+^ d)       -- the action is total
  3. (p .+^ u) .+^ v        == p .+^ (u + v)        -- and associative
  4. p <> q                 == p .+^ (q .-. zeroPosition)
                                                    -- the group op IS translation

Law 4 is what earns Group as a superclass rather than leaving the two markers
overlapping: a boundaryless axis is a Z-torsor, and IsCoord already supplies
the origin (zeroPosition) that turns a torsor into a group. Measured 49/49 on
Periodic 7. If that superclass is judged too strong an obligation on future
axis authors, drop it and keep laws 1-3 -- the rest of this issue is unchanged.

== The payoff: it is not documentation, it changes a type

    walkPathTotal ::
           ( All Boundaryless cs
           , AffineCoordList cs
           , All AdditiveGroup (MapDiff cs)
           )
        => Coord cs -> Path cs -> Coord cs
    walkPathTotal c p = c .+^ pathOffset p

Coord cs, not Maybe (Coord cs). Today walkPath (Coord.hs:390) returns Maybe
because a step can leave the grid; on a boundaryless axis it never can, and
the caller is left holding a Maybe they cannot discharge. This compiles as
written. Note that `Diff x ~ Int` in the superclass supplies what
AllDiffSame Int cs supplies elsewhere, so that constraint is not needed here.

Alongside it, the equation that justifies the name:

    walkPath c p == Just (walkPathTotal c p)

Checked at '[Periodic 5, Periodic 7] over 35 points x 96 three-leg paths:
3360/3360.

== Discrimination is correct and the error is legible

    fuse :: All Boundaryless cs => Coord cs -> Coord cs

  '[Periodic 5, Periodic 7]  accepted
  '[Periodic 5, Clamped 5]   rejected: "No instance for Boundaryless (Clamped 5)"

== Why not hang this off Group instead (see sized-grid-4il)

With the instances proposed there, All Group cs already selects exactly the
all-Periodic lists, so it would "work". Do not do it. Group states that
positions form a group under <>; Boundaryless states that .+^ is a total
associative action. Nothing in Group's laws forces .+^ to be the group's
translation -- a future axis could satisfy one and not the other -- so
soundness of fusion would rest on a coincidence of today's instance set.
Boundaryless names the property the fusion actually needs.

== Relationships

- sized-grid-zrk wants a property test for the interior-only action law and a
  note that the unrestricted one is deliberately absent. Boundaryless gives
  that note a type: the unrestricted law is a Boundaryless law, tested for
  every Boundaryless instance; the interior-only version covers the rest.
- sized-grid-gyn's TorusAxes satisfies All Boundaryless by construction, and
  CylinderAxes does not. That is the sharpest thing those aliases could mean.
- sized-grid-8nz's group-theoretic account (translations descend to Z^n/G only
  when G commutes with them) is why no other axis type can ever join.
close_reason: Implemented: Boundaryless class in Coord/Class.hs, Group+Boundaryless instances for Periodic in Coord/Periodic.hs, walkPathTotal in Coord.hs, property test in Test.Path, and a compile-fail discrimination test. All 525 tests pass under nix devShell (ghc-9.12.3).

title: onBoundary/coordDistance sweeps still allocate ~166 B per call after fusing
description:
sized-grid-adr.3 removed the intermediate list from onBoundary, isCorner, coordDistance and coordManhattan. The 360,000-call bench sweeps dropped from 123/135 MB to 60 MB, but 60 MB is still 166 B per call, against 32 B/call for the (.+^) corner-read sweep which builds the same Coord the same way.

So the residual is not the fold and not (.+^): it is that the sweep's Coord survives as a boxed NP across the call to onBoundary/coordDistance, where the corner-read sweep's is consumed by index and unboxed. Adding INLINE to the four wrappers in Data.Grid.Sized.Coord was tried and changed allocation not at all (still 60 MB), so the fix is not a pragma on the wrapper.

Worth a Core read before any more guessing: -ddump-simpl on bench/Main.hs around onBoundarySweep, to see what keeps the Coord boxed.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-19. The -ddump-simpl read this issue asked for was done (GHC 9.12.3, library at -O2 -fexpose-all-unfoldings -fspecialise-aggressively, bench at default -O1) and it settles the question the other way from how the issue frames it: there is no residual cost in onBoundary, coordDistance or offsetCoord. All three already compile to the same unrolled, fully-unboxed comparisons cornerReads reaches. The 102 B/call (36.7 MB / 360,000) is the BENCHMARK's own artifact, not the library's.

The tell in the Core: cornerReads compiles to a single joinrec over allCoord -- GHC's zero-allocation loop form, no closures. onBoundarySweep compiles to a letrec-bound (not join) worker $wc :: Coord ... -> (Int -> Int) -> Int# -> Int that takes the next arm as an explicit continuation -- a real heap closure, built four times per cell. checkedCornerReads and axisDistanceSweep show the identical shape.

Root cause is how the benchmarks are written, not the library. cornerReads sums four separately-written 'index g (c .+^ lit)' expressions -- one generator (c <- allCoord), no second generator over displacements. checkedCornerReads/onBoundarySweep/axisDistanceSweep instead use a second generator, d <- [d0,d1,d2,d3], over a 4-element runtime list (kept runtime deliberately so full laziness can't float it out as a CAF). GHC's list-fusion rewrite for a two-generator comprehension over a short runtime list comes out CPS'd rather than as a join point, and building each continuation is the allocation.

Confirmed empirically: added checkedCornerReadsFlat/onBoundarySweepFlat/axisDistanceSweepFlat to bench/Main.hs, identical displacements, k still a runtime argument, written as four flat arithmetic arms instead of a second generator (as cornerReads already is). Allocation drops ~99.8% and each runs 2.4-3.7x faster:
  offsetCoord (checked)  36.7 MB -> 82 B    6.88 ms -> 1.81 ms
  onBoundary             36.7 MB -> 152 B   7.10 ms -> 2.90 ms
  coordDistance          36.7 MB -> 82 B    8.73 ms -> 2.61 ms

Closes the loop adr.3 opened: the fold has no intermediate list left to remove. What remains is a caller-side cost (a closure per per-cell, per-offset check) that shows up only when offsets are driven off a multi-arm runtime list, a fact about GHC's fusion of multi-generator list comprehensions, not about this library's folds.

Landed as sized-grid-2xv: the three *Flat benchmarks are permanent additions (the fair reading of offsetCoord/onBoundary/coordDistance in isolation); the original three are kept and re-documented (the list-driven shape is closer to how a caller sweeping a runtime list of offsets would write the loop) -- both measure different, real things. Baseline CSV re-recorded with the three new rows. No src/ changes: nothing in the library needed fixing.
close_reason: Closed

title: tranposeCoord is misspelled in the public export list
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey.

  tranposeCoord

is misspelled -- "tranpose", missing the 's'. It is in the public export list
of Data.Grid.Sized.Coord (Coord.hs:56) and is used by `transposeGrid`
(Internal/Grid.hs:527), which is spelled correctly.

Rename to `transposeCoord`. Pre-1.0 and not yet released under the
`grid-sized` name, so a deprecated alias is probably unnecessary -- but check
`../aoc` for call sites before deciding, since it is the one real consumer.

Small on its own; filed because the optics work touches this function
(`_Transposed` and `permuted` both want a coord-level transpose Iso to build
on) and renaming it in that pass is free, whereas renaming it later is not.

While there: consider whether `transposeCoord` should itself be exported as
an `Iso' (Coord '[w x, h y]) (Coord '[h y, w x])` rather than a function. It
is its own inverse for the same reason `transposeGrid` is, and `permuted`
(companion issue) takes an `Iso'` as its argument, so the Iso form is what
that combinator actually needs.
close_reason: Renamed the public coordinate transpose function to transposeCoord and updated all repository references; Cabal tests pass.

title: Optics survey: which from/to pairs and structural operations should be lens optics
description:
Companion to sized-grid-90f (instances). Same principle, different axis: judge
each candidate on whether the optic is LAWFUL and what it lets an unknown
consumer express, not on whether ../aoc wants it today.

The library is already half-committed to lens -- `lens >=5.2 && <5.4` is a
direct dependency of the library, the tests and the benchmarks (grid-sized.cabal:244,
284, 321, 343) -- so this is about finishing a decision already made, not
taking a new one. What exists today:

  _WrappedCoord  :: IsCoordList cs => Iso' (Coord cs) (NP I cs)   Coord.hs:233
  _WrappedDelta  :: Iso' (Delta ds) (NP I ds)                     Delta.hs:113
  _Ordinal       :: (KnownNat n, Integral a) => Prism' a (Ordinal n)  Ordinal.hs:205
  asOrdinal      :: Iso' (c n) (Ordinal n)                        Coord/Class.hs:49
  coordHead/coordTail :: Lens ...                                 Coord.hs:315,327
  deltaHead/deltaTail :: Lens ...                                 Delta.hs:192,195
  Field1/Field2/... for Coord and Delta                           Coord.hs:351, Delta.hs:212
  gridIndex :: Coord cs -> Lens' (grid a) a                       Class.hs:16
  asGrid / asFocusedGrid :: Lens'                                 Class.hs:17,18
  FunctorWithIndex / FoldableWithIndex / TraversableWithIndex for Grid

So the pattern is established and the gaps are the odd ones out, not a new
direction.

== CORRECTION to the premise this survey started from

"npToPosition <-> npFromPosition can just be represented as a lens Iso" is
half right and the half that is wrong matters.

  * At `Coord`, the Iso ALREADY EXISTS: `_WrappedCoord = iso unCoord (Coord .
    npToPosition)` (Coord.hs:233-234). Nothing to do.
  * At the class methods themselves it is NOT an Iso. `npFromPosition :: Int
    -> NP I cs` (Coord/Class.hs:343) is unchecked -- an out-of-range Int is
    decoded through `unsafeFromAxisIndex` (Coord/Class.hs:441) and forges an
    out-of-range axis value. `Int` is strictly bigger than the coordinate
    space, so the honest optic is a PRISM, and the checked half already
    exists: `coordFromPosition :: Int -> Maybe (Coord cs)` (Coord.hs:498).

That is the general shape of this survey. Most from/to pairs in the tree are
Prisms, not Isos, and the ones that really are Isos are mostly the
STRUCTURAL operations (split/combine, transpose, cons/uncons) rather than the
conversions.

== Verdict by tier

Tier A -- genuine Isos (total both ways, mutually inverse):
  _CoordTuple / _DeltaTuple      coordFromTuple+coordToTuple, delta ditto
  _CoordCons / _DeltaCons        coordSplit+appendCoord, deltaSplit+appendDelta
  _SplitGrid                     splitGrid+combineGrid
  _SplitHigherDim                splitHigherDim+combineHigherDim (needs y <= x)
  _Transposed                    transposeGrid is its own inverse
  permuted                       a coord bijection lifts to a grid bijection
  _FocusedGrid                   FocusedGrid cs a ~ (Grid cs a, Coord cs)

Tier B -- genuine Prisms (partial one way, and the check already exists):
  _Position          coordPosition + coordFromPosition
  _GridVector        gridVector + gridFromVector
  _CollapsedGrid     collapseGrid + gridFromList
  _Weakened          strengthenCoord + weakenCoord (and the Ordinal/axis versions)

Tier C -- Traversals / Folds / Setters (these ADD capability, they are not
repackaging):
  mapLowerDim is ALREADY a Traversal, wearing another name
  gridTiles is a lawful Traversal'; gridWindows is a Fold and CANNOT be a
    Traversal (overlapping foci)
  sliceGrid/takeGrid/dropGrid as Lens' -- write-back into a window, new
  mapAxis as a Setter today, Traversal alongside adr.5
  translated -- the torsor structure of a boundaryless Coord as an Iso

Tier D -- hygiene and one real bug:
  asFocusedGrid for Grid violates the lens put-get law (Class.hs:36)
  _WrappedCoord's name has lied since adr.16
  tranposeCoord is misspelled in the public export list
  law tests for all of the above
  where the optics live (module organisation)

== REJECTED, with reasons

  * lens's `Cons`/`Snoc` for Coord and Delta. Wrong shape: `Cons s t a b`
    requires the tail to have the same type as the whole (`_Cons :: Prism s t
    (a, s) (b, t)`), and a `Coord (c ': cs)`'s tail is `Coord cs`, a
    different type. Writing a bespoke Iso instead is not a workaround, it is
    strictly stronger -- `Cons` gives a Prism because a list can be empty,
    and `Coord (c ': cs)` never is.
  * `At` for Grid. Already rejected in sized-grid-90f for the same reason:
    it implies insert and delete, and a fixed shape has neither.
  * `Wrapped` for Coord. See the naming issue: after adr.16 a Coord is an
    Int, not an `NP I cs`, so an `Unwrapped (Coord cs) = NP I cs` instance
    would be a lawful Iso under a class whose whole convention is that it is
    a coerce. Delta, Path and Ordinal are real newtypes and are fair game.
  * Migrating to the `optics` package. Not on the table: `lens` is already a
    direct dependency in four components, and `optics` would be a second
    optic vocabulary in one API for no gain here.
  * `Reversing`. No caller, no obvious meaning on a multi-axis grid, and
    unlike everything above it does not fall out of an operation that
    already exists.
design:
Survey complete: every signature quoted was read out of the tree, and every law claim was checked by hand against the lens/prism/traversal laws rather than assumed. 20 issues filed.

Three findings that were not in the original brainstorm and are the reason this was worth doing as a survey rather than a batch of small tasks:

1. sized-grid-3au is a REAL BUG in shipped code. asFocusedGrid at the Grid instance (Class.hs:36) violates put-get: write a FocusedGrid through it, read it back, and the focus has silently moved to zeroCoord. FocusedGrid's Eq is on both fields by explicit design (Focused.hs:31) so this is a genuine inequality. It cannot be fixed in place -- a Grid has no focus to store, so no lawful Lens' (Grid cs a) (FocusedGrid cs a) exists.

2. gridTiles and gridWindows have the SAME TYPE and cannot have the same optic (sized-grid-r2b). Tiles are disjoint (Mod ~ 0), so a lawful Traversal'. Windows overlap by construction -- the Haddock says so at Internal/Grid.hs:904 -- so a Traversal is unlawful and only a Fold is available. Shipping them as Traversal'/Fold puts that difference in the types instead of in prose.

3. mapLowerDim (Internal/Grid.hs:660) IS a Traversal already, exactly, van Laarhoven and all (sized-grid-aq7). Zero implementation, a type synonym. Its 12-line Haddock warning about f ~ [] is really the standard "don't traverse with []" in a vocabulary the reader does not have yet.

The premise the survey started from was half wrong and the wrong half mattered: npToPosition/npFromPosition IS an Iso at Coord and already exists as _WrappedCoord (Coord.hs:233), but at Int it is a PRISM, because npFromPosition is unchecked and forges out-of-range coordinates (Coord/Class.hs:343 via unsafeFromAxisIndex at :441). That generalised: most from/to pairs here are Prisms, and the genuine Isos are mostly the STRUCTURAL operations (split/combine, transpose, cons) rather than the conversions.

Take sized-grid-01d (naming and module placement) before working the implementation issues -- it is cheap now and expensive after 20 more names exist.
close_reason: Survey complete. 20 issues filed, one per accepted line, plus the rejected list with reasons in the description. Verdict is in the design field.

title: Rejected: one class-polymorphic (:|) for both Coord and Delta
description:
Considered during sized-grid-adr.16 and rejected. Recorded so it is not
re-derived, not because it is queued work.

THE IDEA. adr.16 split displacements out of Coord, so positions are written
with (:|)/EmptyCoord and displacements with (:^)/NoDelta. Option C at the time
was to keep one spelling for both, via a class with an associated constraint
family:

    class HasCons (f :: [Type] -> Type) where
      type ConsCtx f (c :: Type) (cs :: [Type]) :: Constraint
      hcons   :: ConsCtx f c cs => c -> f cs -> f (c ': cs)
      huncons :: ConsCtx f c cs => f (c ': cs) -> (c, f cs)

    pattern (:|) :: (HasCons f, ConsCtx f c cs) => c -> f cs -> f (c ': cs)

It does not remove the type split -- there are still two types either way. All
it buys is source compatibility for the (:|)/EmptyCoord spelling on
displacements.

WHY NOT, in order of weight.

1. The port measured the exact hazard this would deepen. (:|) is the first
   version of that operator to carry a required context, and a pattern synonym
   with a required context compiles to a matcher taking dictionaries that GHC
   does not inline on its own. Left alone it cost 9.20 ms and 36 MB against
   1.13 ms and 4.8 MB on a tabulate whose rule destructures its coordinate --
   400 bytes a cell for a match that should be a quotRem. An INLINE pragma
   fixed it, and there is now a benchmark (tabulate 300x300 [rule destructures
   the coord]) guarding it.

   That was with two ordinary class constraints. Option C makes the constraint
   a type family APPLICATION, which GHC must reduce at every use site before it
   can even see the dictionaries. Whether the same INLINE rescues that is
   unknown, and the failure mode is a silent 8x on the hottest path in the
   library. Buying syntax with that risk is a bad trade.

2. The migration it would have saved is already done, and was trivial. Across
   the library, tests, benchmarks, README, four example programs and two atlas
   packages, the displacement sites came to four test helpers (d2 x3, sevenD),
   one regex over bench/Main.hs, six lines of README and two in examples. ../aoc
   adds eight more (sized-grid-3xw). Every one was caught by the type checker;
   no silent behaviour change was possible.

3. Two spellings turn out to be a feature. 'c .+^ (1 :^ 1 :^ NoDelta)' says in
   its syntax that the argument is a displacement, which '1 :| 1 :| EmptyCoord'
   did not. Option C gives that distinction back up.

4. Inference gets worse. 'EmptyCoord :: f '[]' is ambiguous standalone, so any
   unannotated local helper that ends a chain would need a signature it does
   not need today. COMPLETE pragmas on a class-polymorphic synonym are also
   subtle in a way the current ones are not.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT. Essentially only GHC gaining real INLINE support for
pattern synonym matchers, so that (1) stops being a live risk. Wanting one
spelling back is not on its own a reason; see (3).
close_reason: Decision record, not work. Rejected on merit during the adr.16 port: it deepens the constrained-pattern-synonym inlining hazard the port measured at 8x on the destructuring path, and the migration it would have saved was ~50 mechanical type-checked lines that are already done.

title: asFocusedGrid for Grid violates the lens put-get law and silently moves the focus
description:
Found during the sized-grid-31z optics survey. This is a real law violation
in shipped code, not a proposal.

  class IsGrid cs grid | grid -> cs where
    asFocusedGrid :: Lens' (grid a) (FocusedGrid cs a)      Class.hs:18

  instance ... IsGrid cs (Grid cs) where
    asFocusedGrid = lens (`FocusedGrid` zeroCoord) (const focusedGrid)   Class.hs:36

Desugared: getter `\g -> FocusedGrid g zeroCoord`, setter `\_ fg -> focusedGrid fg`.

== The violation

put-get (`view l (set l v s) == v`) fails.

  set asFocusedGrid v s              = focusedGrid v
  view asFocusedGrid (focusedGrid v) = FocusedGrid (focusedGrid v) zeroCoord

For `v = FocusedGrid g p` with `p /= zeroCoord`, that is `FocusedGrid g
zeroCoord`, which is not `v`. `FocusedGrid`'s Eq is on BOTH fields -- stated
explicitly at Focused.hs:31, "two grids with the same cells but different
focus are distinct" -- so this is a genuine inequality, not a representation
detail.

Concretely: write a focused grid through the lens, read it back, and the
focus has silently moved to the origin.

get-put holds (`set l (view l s) s = focusedGrid (FocusedGrid s zeroCoord) = s`),
which is why this has gone unnoticed: the round trip that starts from a
`Grid` is fine. Only the one that starts from a `FocusedGrid` loses data.

The other three method implementations are fine:
  * `asGrid = id` at Grid -- lawful.
  * `asGrid = lens focusedGrid (\(FocusedGrid _ p) g -> FocusedGrid g p)` at
    FocusedGrid (Class.hs:41) -- lawful, it preserves the focus.
  * `asFocusedGrid = id` at FocusedGrid -- lawful.

So the bug is exactly one method at exactly one instance.

== Why it cannot be fixed in place

A `Grid` does not have a focus. There is nowhere for the setter to put `p`.
No implementation of `Lens' (Grid cs a) (FocusedGrid cs a)` can be lawful,
because the lens type is the claim that a `Grid` CONTAINS a `FocusedGrid`,
and it does not -- it contains half of one.

== Options

  1. Weaken the method to `Getter`/`Setter`, or split it into two. Honest,
     small, and breaks any consumer using it as a Lens -- which, given the
     law failure, is a consumer already getting wrong answers.
  2. Change the class so the conversion is stated where it is true: keep
     `asGrid :: Lens' (grid a) (Grid cs a)` (lawful at both instances) and
     replace `asFocusedGrid` with the Iso from the companion issue,
     `_FocusedGrid :: Iso' (FocusedGrid cs a) (Grid cs a, Coord cs)`, plus a
     `focus` Lens. The conversion Grid -> FocusedGrid then needs a coord
     supplied, which is the truth.
  3. Keep the signature and document the violation. Rejected -- a Lens that
     loses data on put-get is the exact failure mode this library's design
     thesis is organised against, and "nothing clamps silently" is in the
     package synopsis.

Prefer (2), which is why this is filed alongside the _FocusedGrid Iso rather
than on its own.

Whatever the fix, add the law properties -- see the optic law-test issue.
This would have been caught by a two-line QuickCheck property.
close_reason: Fixed together: dropped the unlawful asFocusedGrid Lens from IsGrid, added _FocusedGrid/focus/unfocused to FocusedGrid, wired law tests. See commit c0bc2df.

title: ci.yml has no concurrency group, so pushes queue rather than cancel
description: Observed 2026-08-19/20: 5 CI runs stacked up simultaneously on master, one wedged ~5 hours (a cabal matrix job whose steps rendered as simultaneously in-progress, suggesting a disconnected runner never marked failed -- ci.yml sets no timeout-minutes, default is 6h). No concurrency group means every push to master queues a full new run instead of cancelling the superseded one, so a burst of pushes (several worktree merges in a short window) backs up the runner queue for hours. Fix: add a top-level concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true to ci.yml. Cancelled the 4 stale runs by hand this time; this issue tracks the workflow fix so it doesn't recur.
close_reason: Closed

title: Editing pass on src/ Haddock: apply ASD-STE100 and cut change-history narration
description:
The Haddock in src/ has grown to roughly half the source. `find src -name '*.hs' | xargs cat | wc -l` is 2,693 lines, of which 1,364 begin with `--`. Much of it is good, but it was written incrementally across many refactor sessions and now carries three defects that a single editing pass can fix.

**1. Change history is documented as if it were the API.** 34 lines in src/ contain "used to", "This was", "formerly", or "previously". Examples:

- src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:9 — "This used to be a GADT carrying the value at the type level:"
- src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:26 — "This used to be a method of `IsCoord` taking a @Proxy (c n)@."
- src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:82 — "This was @asSizeProxy@, whose continuation took a @Proxy m@."
- src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:354, :451, :604 — "The fold this used to carry as a @where@ helper is now ..." (same sentence, three times)

A reader coming to the docs for the first time does not have the old code and cannot use this. The rationale worth keeping is the *reason the current shape is right* ("the size is now given visibly", "@1 <= n@ is required because a @c 0@ has no inhabitants"); the reason worth dropping is what the previous shape was. Where the history genuinely matters, it belongs in ChangeLog.md or the beads issue that made the change, not in the reference docs of every call site.

**2. The prose is not written to be parsed quickly.** Long compound sentences, `---` asides nested inside already-long clauses, and hedges. This is the library's public documentation and its main audience is somebody skimming Hackage for whether a function does what they need.

**3. Duplication.** The `where`-helper sentence appears three times verbatim; several `IsCoord` method docs restate the same "a type argument is visible when inference cannot recover it" rule that is already stated once, well, at src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:33.

## Scope

Apply the `asd-ste100` skill to Haddock and comments across src/. ASD-STE100 is the controlled-English standard: one topic per sentence, active voice, approved simple verbs, no ambiguous participles, short sentences (about 20 words in descriptive text). This suits reference documentation exactly.

Do, in one pass per file:

- Rewrite each Haddock block to STE100.
- Delete change-history narration; keep the design rationale, restated in the present tense as a property of the current code.
- Collapse the repeated sentences to one statement in the most-visible place, and cross-reference it from the others.
- Keep every `@...@`, `'...'`, and `> ...` markup form working; the doc examples in `> ` blocks are load-bearing for readers, so verify they are still correct.
- Leave README.lhs alone unless it is trivially affected; it is a literate-Haskell file that compiles, and it deserves its own pass.

## Out of scope

No behaviour change, no signature change, no export-list change. If the pass turns up a real defect in the code, file it separately rather than fixing it here, so the diff stays reviewable as prose-only.

## Verification

`cabal build` and `cabal haddock` both clean, and `git diff --stat` shows changes to comment lines only. A diff that touches a line of code means the scope leaked.
notes:
Sequencing: if sized-grid-85n (rename the package, re-own the metadata) lands first, do this pass after it. That rename rewrites module and identifier names that appear inside the prose, so running the prose pass first means editing the same sentences twice. Not a hard blocker — it is only a rework cost.

Suggested order, largest comment blocks first, since they carry the most history:
  Coord.hs (424 comment lines / 838), Coord/Class.hs (401 / 572),
  Internal/Grid.hs (237 / 567), Ordinal.hs (87 / 231),
  Internal/Type.hs (55 / 78), Coord/Clamped.hs (43), Coord/Periodic.hs (37),
  Grid/Unsafe.hs (31), Grid/Grid.hs (25), Grid/Focused.hs (16),
  Grid/Class.hs (6), SizedGrid.hs (2)

This is safely splittable per file if the diff gets too large to review at once.

title: Missing API: sliding windows over a grid (stride 1), distinct from gridTiles
description:
gridTiles (renamed from gridWindows in sized-grid-61o) cuts a grid into DISJOINT tiles: an Ordinal 9 axis tiled by Ordinal 3 gives 3 tiles. The name it used to have promised the other operation -- a sliding window of size 3 at each of the 7 offsets -- and that operation still does not exist.

The primitive is already there: shrinkGrid (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs) extracts a sub-grid at a coordinate offset, and the ShrinkableGrid constraint 'x + z <= y + 1' already states exactly 'a window of z taken at any of the x offsets fits inside a source of y'. A sliding-window function is shrinkGrid mapped over all offsets.

Wanted:
    gridWindows :: ... => Grid (big ': rest) a -> [Grid (small ': rest) a]
      -- CoordNat big - CoordNat small + 1 results, stride 1, overlapping

Consumers: summed-area / convolution style problems. ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs builds 3x3 and NxN sums by hand over a prefix-sum grid, which is what this would replace.

Left out of sized-grid-61o deliberately: that issue was the P0 hang, and adding a new operation is not needed to fix it.
acceptance_criteria: gridWindows returns CoordNat big - CoordNat small + 1 overlapping sub-grids at stride 1; a size larger than the source is a type error; property test that every window equals the corresponding shrinkGrid at that offset.
close_reason: Implemented gridWindows in Internal/Grid.hs, exported from Data.Grid.Sized. Property tests in tests/Test/Windows.hs verify agreement with shrinkGrid at every offset (1D and 2D-with-fixed-axis cases), plus a slice-equivalence check. Confirmed a window larger than the source is a type error. All 420 tests pass, hlint clean.

title: The per-axis coord design expresses exactly the separable boundary policies
description:
The library's boundary policy lives per axis, in the coordinate type. That is a
deliberate decision (see the `boundary policy placement` memory) and it is the
right one, but it has an exact limit that has never been written down:

    THE PER-AXIS COORD DESIGN EXPRESSES EXACTLY THE SEPARABLE POLICIES.

A policy is separable when axis i's edge behaviour is a function of axis i
alone. Non-separable means crossing the edge of axis i transforms axis j.

The limit is structural, not a gap in the instances. Every operation that can
leave the space is per-axis by construction:

  * `offsetIsCoord :: c n -> Int -> Maybe (c n)`  (Coord/Class.hs:123)
        one axis, one Int. It cannot see, let alone alter, another axis.
  * `npOffset` (Coord/Class.hs:549) folds `offsetIsCoord` down the NP
        independently per axis, `<*>`-ing the results.
  * `npStepsWithin` (Coord/Class.hs:553) is a cartesian product of per-axis
        `axisSteps`.
  * `npAdd`/`npSub` on AffineCoordList (Coord.hs:321) — same shape.

WHAT IS SEPARABLE (fits today, no new machinery)
  Ordinal, Clamped, Periodic          — implemented
  Reflective (billiard bounce)         — see the sibling issue, a drop-in
  Reflect101 (mirror, no edge dup)     — drop-in
  Constant / padding                   — needs a value, not just a coord

  And every mixed product for free: `'[Periodic 10, Clamped 5]` is a cylinder,
  `'[Periodic w, Periodic h]` a torus. This is the payoff of the per-axis
  choice and it is why the design should NOT move to a single grid-level policy
  parameter, which cannot say "cylinder" at all.

WHAT IS NOT SEPARABLE (needs something genuinely new)
  Mobius strip    — wrapping axis 0 flips axis 1
  Klein bottle    — same, with axis 1 also wrapping
  Projective plane— leaving any edge inverts all axes
  Glide reflection in 3D — leaving Z rotates the XY plane
  Cube map / atlas— leaving a face changes which grid you are in, and rotates
                    the frame

WHY THIS MATTERS

The non-separable policies are exactly the ones that motivated the
atlas/mosaic direction. This issue is the precise statement of why they cannot
be added as another `IsCoord` instance: there is no `c n` whose `offsetIsCoord`
can reach the neighbouring axis. Anything that wants them needs a new
coordinate layer above `Coord cs`, not a fourth axis type.

That is a scoping fact, and it means the atlas work does not threaten anything
that exists. `Coord cs` stays the separable case and stays fast.
close_reason: Written down: haddock section on IsCoordList (src/Data/Grid/Sized/Coord/Class.hs, 'Why this is exactly the separable boundary policies') states the structural ceiling and cross-references sized-grid-o1n/sized-grid-ghj for where non-separable policies would need to go. AffineCoordList (Coord.hs) gets a short pointer to the same argument. Commit a5dc864.

title: Vertex cycles in atlas-topology: the law seamIsInvolution does not catch
description:
atlas-topology checks one law: every half-edge names a partner that names it back. That law is necessary and not sufficient. It is a statement about EDGES, and a surface's corners can still be wrong when every edge is right.

WHAT IS MISSING

Walk around a corner of a chart by alternating 'turn to the next boundary
at this corner' with 'cross that seam'. You come back to where you started
after some number of steps, and that number is the vertex's cycle length --
the discrete cone angle. It is pure combinatorics, computable from a
SeamTable and a corner enumeration alone, with no coordinate, no cell and
no Grid in sight. Exactly the split b15 drew.

WHAT IT WOULD SAY ABOUT THE SURFACES WE HAVE

    torus / Klein     4 squares per vertex   angle 2*pi   flat
    cube (68j)        3 squares per vertex   angle 3*pi/2  cone point
    projective (4nl)  2 squares per vertex   angle pi      cone point

So the cube already has non-flat vertices and nobody wrote that down;
cubeStepBeltCloses walks equators, which never pass through a corner, so
the test suite has never touched the phenomenon. sized-grid-4nl is where it
starts to matter, because a projective-plane walker cannot take a diagonal
step at a corner without an arbitrary choice, and the involution law will
report the table as perfectly healthy.

WHY IT IS WORTH HAVING AS A LAW AND NOT A COMMENT

A cycle length of 4 everywhere is the checkable statement 'this seam table
describes a flat surface', which is precisely the class of surface where a
square-lattice walker is unambiguous. A table that pairs up but has a
vertex of cycle length 1 describes no surface at all, and today nothing
would catch it. This gives atlas-topology a second law with real
discriminating power and gives 4nl its headline property test.

Needs a corner enumeration the way seamViolations needs a half-edge
enumeration -- passed in as a list for the same reason (a corner label is a
product, and base gives tuples Bounded but not Enum).

title: Migrate ../aoc to the Delta displacement type (adr.16 fallout)
description:
sized-grid-adr.16 split displacements out of Coord: Diff (Coord cs) is now
Delta (MapDiff cs), built with (:^)/NoDelta and deltaFromTuple rather than
(:|)/EmptyCoord and coordFromTuple. ../aoc is the consumer adr.16 named as the
one real cost of the change, and this is that cost, itemised.

It is entirely mechanical and entirely caught by the type checker -- no silent
behaviour change is possible. Every coordFromTuple call in ../aoc is building a
displacement, so all of them become deltaFromTuple:

  src/2016/02.hs:13   delta :: Move -> Coord '[Int, Int]  ->  Delta '[Int, Int]
  src/2016/02.hs:5    import list: coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple, add Delta
  src/2016/02.hs:15-18, 53, 68   coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple
  src/2017/19.hs:37, 57          coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple
  src/2018/06.hs:27              coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple
  src/2018/11.hs:41              coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple
  src/2024/04.hs:14   import list: coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple
  src/2024/04.hs:58, 77          coordFromTuple -> deltaFromTuple

Note 2016/02's delta is shape-polymorphic on purpose -- it is used at both
'[Clamped 3, Clamped 3] and '[Clamped 5, Clamped 5] through a solve that is
polymorphic in n. Delta '[Int, Int] keeps that working unchanged, which is the
reason adr.16 indexed Delta by the diff list rather than the axis list; do not
'fix' it by naming a shape.

POSITIONS NEED NO CHANGE. (:|) and EmptyCoord are still the interface for
coordinates and still COMPLETE, so 2018/18.hs:72-73, 2018/06.hs:51-52 and
2018/11.hs:12,35 compile as they are. (:|) gained an
(IsCoordLifted c, IsCoordList cs) context, which every one of those call sites
already has in scope.

NOT VERIFIED BY A BUILD, and that is why this is filed rather than done: ../aoc
does not build in this environment at all, before or after adr.16 -- hmatrix
0.20.2 fails to configure for want of blas and lapack, identically against
unmodified master. The list above is by inspection. Someone with a working
hmatrix should build it and confirm nothing else moved.

Expect a speedup for free once it builds: the grid puzzles are index- and
neighbour-heavy, which is where adr.16 measured 2.3x-2.6x.
close_reason: i fixed it

title: stencilFoldGrid x100 unboxed allocates 149 MB, not the ~48 MB the single-pass figure predicts
description: Found while closing sized-grid-adr.13. stencilFoldGrid, table already built, 50x50, unboxed grid, single pass: 479 KB. Naively that predicts iterate (stencilFoldGrid ...) g !! 100 at roughly 100x that, ~48 MB. Measured: 149 MB (bench "stencilFoldStep x100, 50x50, unboxed" in bench/Main.hs). Not chased further -- flagging in case the gap points at something real (a fusion break specific to the unboxed VG.generate path under iterate, GC accounting, or just the single-pass figure being warmed differently than a cold iterate loop). Not blocking anything; low priority.

title: Speculative: coord + heading (FibreBundle/ParallelTransporting)
description:
Inspiration: `Data.Manifold.FibreBundle` in the `manifolds` package.

    data FibreBundle b f = FibreBundle { baseSpace :: b, fibreSpace :: f }
    type TangentBundle m = FibreBundle m (Needle m)

A tangent bundle is a point paired with a direction at that point, and the associated
`ParallelTransporting` class answers the question "as I move along the space, what happens
to my heading?"

sized-grid has half of this already. `FocusedGrid cs a` (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Focused.hs:18)
is a grid paired with a position --- a pointed structure. What is missing is the heading.

Consumers hand-roll it:

    ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:71   type State n = (FocusedGrid '[HardWrap n, HardWrap n] Cell, Dir)
    ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:63   shift :: Dir -> Coord ... -> Coord ...
    ../aoc/src/2017/19.hs      the same pattern again, on a hand-rolled Map-based grid

WHAT THE ANALOGY BUYS

The interesting content is not the pair --- anyone can write a pair --- it is
`ParallelTransporting`: the boundary policy should decide what happens to the heading
when a walker meets an edge. On a `Periodic` axis the heading is unchanged and the walker
wraps. On a `HardWrap` axis there is a genuine choice the library could name: stop,
reflect, or turn. Today every consumer re-decides that inline, and ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs
gets it right only by ACCIDENT --- it relies on `HardWrap`'s `(.+^)` clamping so that
walking off the keypad edge silently returns the walker to where it was:

    move fg c = let next = seeks (.+^ delta c) fg
                in if isNothing $ extract next then fg else next -- It's a "wall", stay put

That works, but nothing in the types says it should, and the clamp is documented
elsewhere in this library as the behaviour callers must not rely on.

STATUS: SPECULATIVE, FILED FOR THE RECORD

This is the weakest-justified item in the set and is deliberately backlogged. Two real
consumers is not a strong enough signal to add a type, and the design question --- is a
heading a `Needle`, a unit step, or a per-axis sign? --- is unresolved.

DO NOT START THIS before the Needle issue lands. A heading is most naturally
`Needle (Coord cs)` restricted to unit steps, so the representation question is
downstream of how needles are represented at all.

Revisit if a third consumer wants it, or if the boundary-policy work makes
"what happens to a heading at an edge" a question the library is already answering.
design: Deliberately backlogged. The valuable part is not the pair but ParallelTransporting: letting the axis's boundary policy decide what a heading does at an edge (Periodic wraps unchanged; HardWrap must choose stop/reflect/turn). Blocked on the Needle representation, since a heading is most naturally a unit Needle.
acceptance_criteria: Not scheduled. Revisit if a third consumer wants it or if the boundary work makes edge-heading semantics a question the library already answers.
close_reason:
Implemented, real code: Walker cs a (Data.Grid.Sized.Focused) pairs FocusedGrid with a heading (Diff (Coord cs), reusing the needle per sized-grid-iet, not a new type); stepWalker takes one step in the walker's own heading through the new transportCoord (Data.Grid.Sized.Coord), which is total (uses .+^, not the checked offsetCoord) and folds axisFrameFlips per axis to negate the heading's component on any axis a bounce reversed. The per-axis fold needed both AffineSpace and IsCoordLifted at once, neither of which the existing IsCoordList/AffineCoordList classes state together, so it lives in a new small class TransportCoordList (Coord.hs), same shape and precedent as those two. Tests in tests/Test/Focused.hs: agreement with transportCoord on both a Clamped and a Reflective grid, invariance of heading through a Clamped wall, and an explicit bounce example confirming the heading reverses on exactly the axis that flipped. Full suite (407 tests) and all examples/bench build clean.

Scope: only the axis-local seam (a billiard bounce reversing its own axis), which is what axisFrameFlips (sized-grid-o1n) can express. Cross-axis frame transforms (Mobius, Klein, atlas) are still sized-grid-fh2/sized-grid-1bm's territory, unchanged by this. No new ParallelTransporting typeclass was added -- the design question of what such a class's shape should be is still open, and a concrete function (transportCoord) answers the motivating question (sized-grid-o1n's seam rule, made concrete for a walker) without committing to unresolved class design.

title: Modernise sized-grid.cabal: cabal-version 1.10, zero version bounds, missing modules, per-file LANGUAGE noise
description:
Current sized-grid.cabal problems:

  - 'cabal-version: >=1.10' (line 3). Modern baseline is 'cabal-version: 2.4' or 3.0,
    which unlocks common stanzas and the modern module syntax.
  - Library build-depends has NO version bounds at all: 'base,' 'aeson ,' 'lens ,' etc.
    Unacceptable for a Hackage release; also means nothing pins the library away from
    a breaking aeson/lens major bump.
  - SizedGrid.Internal.Type is in neither exposed-modules nor other-modules.
  - Every module repeats 10-20 LANGUAGE pragmas. GHC2021 (default on GHC 9.2+) already
    implies ScopedTypeVariables, TypeApplications, TypeOperators, FlexibleContexts,
    FlexibleInstances, RankNTypes, StandaloneDeriving, GADTs and more. Setting
    'default-language: GHC2021' plus a short 'default-extensions: DataKinds,
    TypeFamilies, UndecidableInstances, PolyKinds' would delete most of the headers.
  - The CPP '#if MIN_VERSION_base(4,11,0)' blocks in SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:25-28,
    SizedGrid/Grid/Class.hs:19-22 and tests/Test/Utils.hs:16-19 exist to support
    base < 4.11 (GHC 8.2). Dead now; delete the CPP and the pragma.
  - src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:1 sets '-Wno-redundant-constraints' for the whole module,
    which hides real problems (e.g. the Monoid/Semigroup constraints on the Comonad

title: Group/Abelian/Cyclic instances for Periodic and Coord: the algebra the types already have
description:
Verified by building it (GHC 9.12.3, groups-0.5.3, base-only dependency).
Every claim below compiled and ran; nothing here is on paper.

== What is missing

Periodic n IS Z/nZ, the finite cyclic group. The library already ships its
Semigroup, Monoid and AdditiveGroup instances (Coord/Periodic.hs:46-60), so
the group structure is present but is only reachable through vector-space's
AdditiveGroup hierarchy, which does not connect to Semigroup/Monoid. A
consumer writing generic code over "a Monoid with inverses" reaches for
Data.Group (groups package), and finds nothing.

== Measured

Exhaustively over Periodic 7 (all 7 elements; 343 triples for associativity):

  invertibility  p <> invert p == mempty, both sides   7/7
  associativity  (a<>b)<>c == a<>(b<>c)                343/343
  commutativity  a<>b == b<>a                          49/49
  pow agrees     pow p k == zeroV .+^ (fromEnum p * k) 63/63  (k in [-4..4])
  action is <>   a <> b == a .+^ fromEnum b            49/49

The last line is the load-bearing one: Periodic's monoid operation IS its
translation action, so a Group instance is not a second, parallel algebra
bolted on -- it names the one already there.

== Proposed instances

  instance (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Group    (Periodic n) where invert = negateV
  instance (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Abelian  (Periodic n)
  instance (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Cyclic   (Periodic n) where generator = toEnum 1

  instance (All Semigroup cs, All Monoid cs, All Group cs) => Group (Coord cs) where
    invert (Coord a) = Coord (hcliftA (Proxy @Group) (fmap invert) a)
  instance (All Semigroup cs, All Monoid cs, All Group cs, All Abelian cs)
    => Abelian (Coord cs)

All five compile against the library as it stands.

== Three things the instance placement says for free

1. Clamped has Monoid but CANNOT have Group: clamping is not invertible. The
   absent instance is the statement.
2. Reflective and Reflect101 have no Semigroup at all, so the question does
   not arise for them.
3. Group therefore picks out exactly Periodic among the four axis types. That
   is a coincidence of the current instance set, NOT a law -- see the
   Boundaryless issue for why fusion soundness must not be hung off it.

== Two things NOT to do

- Do NOT add Cyclic (Coord cs). A product of cyclic groups is cyclic only
  when the orders are pairwise coprime: Z/5 x Z/7 is cyclic, Z/5 x Z/5 is
  not. An All Cyclic cs instance would be wrong at '[Periodic 5, Periodic 5].
- Do NOT expect Group to subsume AdditiveGroup. Displacements are
  Coord (MapDiff cs) = Coord '[Int, ..], and Int has no Monoid, so the
  displacement type gets AdditiveGroup and cannot get Group without Sum
  wrappers at every call site. Both hierarchies stay.

== Cost

groups-0.5.3 depends on base alone and built clean on GHC 9.12.3 here. The
instances add no run-time representation and no methods beyond invert.

== Gotcha for whoever writes the tests

Data.Group's `generated` is INFINITE -- it is the orbit iterated forever, so
`show (generated :: [Periodic 7])` does not terminate (found the hard way:
3.4 GB of output). `generated'` is the Eq-bounded one and returns the 7
elements, starting at the generator: [1,2,3,4,5,6,0].
close_reason: Implemented: Abelian/Cyclic (Periodic n) and pointwise Group/Abelian (Coord cs). Tested via groupLaws/abelianLaws QuickCheck properties and an exhaustive Cyclic check against generated' for Periodic 7. All 600 tests pass.

title: Missing API: boundary detection (Interior/Boundary from manifolds)
description:
Inspiration: `SemimanifoldWithBoundary` in the `manifolds` package, which makes the
boundary a first-class part of the type rather than something callers rediscover:

    type Interior m; type Boundary m
    separateInterior :: m -> Either (Boundary m) (Interior m)

sized-grid has NO API for "is this coordinate on an edge". Not a predicate, not an
enumeration, nothing. Every consumer hand-rolls it against `natVal`:

    ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:59-62
      n = fromEnum (natVal (Proxy @n)) - 1
      isCorner ((fromEnum -> r) :| (fromEnum -> c) :| _) =
        (r == 0 || r == n) && (c == 0 || c == n)

That is the whole of a boundary check written out per call site, and it is wrong the
moment an axis is `Periodic` --- a torus has no corners, but the code above will happily
report some.

PROPOSAL

Add a method to `IsCoord` (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:32), following exactly the shape
`offsetIsCoord` established: a default that does the bounds check, which edgeless coord
types override.

    data Extremum = AtMin | AtMax deriving (Eq, Ord, Show, Enum, Bounded)

    -- in class IsCoord:
    coordBoundary :: (KnownNat n, 1 <= n) => c n -> Maybe Extremum
    coordBoundary c
      | i == 0                 = Just AtMin
      | i == ordinalSize @n - 1 = Just AtMax
      | otherwise              = Nothing
      where i = ordinalToInt (c ^. asOrdinal)

`Periodic` overrides it to `const Nothing`, for the same reason it overrides
`offsetIsCoord` to be total: a torus has no edges. That symmetry is the argument for
putting it in the class rather than writing a free function over `Coord`.

Then over a whole coord:

    coordBoundaries :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Coord cs -> NP (K (Maybe Extremum)) cs
    onBoundary      :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Coord cs -> Bool   -- any axis at an edge
    isCorner        :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Coord cs -> Bool   -- every axis at an edge

`isCorner` on an all-`Periodic` coord is then `False` by construction, which is the
correct answer and the one the hand-rolled version gets wrong.

RELATED, worth doing in the same change

`interiorCoords` / a `Grid` traversal restricted to cells whose full Moore neighbourhood
exists. Cellular automata want exactly this: ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs and gameOfLife both
special-case edge cells, and `mooreNeighbours` (Coord.hs:453) already returns a shorter
list at an edge without saying so.

ACCEPTANCE

../aoc/src/2015/18.hs can delete its `n`/`isCorner` local definitions and call the
library instead, and the result is still correct for `HardWrap` axes.
design: Add coordBoundary as an IsCoord method with a bounds-check default, mirroring exactly how offsetIsCoord is structured: bounded types take the default, Periodic overrides because a torus has no edges. That symmetry is why it belongs in the class rather than being a free function over Coord.
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs deletes its local n/isCorner definitions and calls the library; isCorner on an all-Periodic coord returns False.
notes:
CORRECTION to the note above, on the Grid traversal half.

The earlier note said the traversal 'does not serve the consumers cited' because an
extend-based automaton must produce a value for every cell. That reasoning is about the
CA pipeline and it stands, but it was the wrong answer to the question. The right answer
is that the traversal needs no new API at all:

    interior = itraversed . indices (not . onBoundary)
    boundary = itraversed . indices onBoundary

Grid cs is already TraversableWithIndex (Coord cs) (src/SizedGrid/Internal/Grid.hs:192),
so the index IS the coordinate and Control.Lens.indices does the filtering. Verified: on
a Clamped 5 x Clamped 5, lengthOf interior is 9, its indices are exactly interiorCoords,
'g & interior .~ 9' leaves all 16 boundary cells untouched, and 'indices isCorner' picks
out four cells. On a Periodic 5 x Periodic 5 the interior is all 25.

That composition is strictly better than what a named function would have given, because
it reads AND writes where interiorCoords only enumerates. Naming it would add a signature
and a second way to say the same thing and no capability, so it stays unnamed and is
documented on interiorCoords, in the README, and in the ChangeLog, with six tests in
tests/Test/Boundary.hs pinning it -- a documented composition nothing exercises is a
claim, not a fact.

So the 'RELATED, worth doing in the same change' half of this issue is now fully
addressed: interiorCoords for the enumeration, the optic for read-write, neither of them
requiring the consumer to know what natVal is.
close_reason: Closed

title: Projective plane grid: single-chart atlas with both seams reversed
description:
The gluing sized-grid-aqa originally spelled out, filed under its correct name.

Both edge-pairs self-glued with the OTHER axis reflected:

    walking off the right edge at row y  -> left edge, row (h - 1 - y)
    walking off the bottom edge at col x -> top edge,  col (w - 1 - x)

That is RP^2, not a Klein bottle: the square model (0,y)~(1,1-y) plus
(x,0)~(1-x,1) identifies antipodal boundary points. aqa filed it as Klein
and deferred 'projective' on the belief that projective meant an opposite-
CORNER gluing (sized-grid-o1n's policy table reads 'Projective -> (antipode
c, negate all axes)'); the antipodal identification of a square's BOUNDARY
is exactly the both-edges-reversed table above. Worth re-checking o1n's
table entry against this.

Data.Grid.Atlas.Klein (built in aqa) already drives its coordinate remap
entirely off SeamTable's reversed bit, so the table here is a two-line edit
of crossKleinEdge -- flipping the Rolled entries' False to True.

WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN A COPY

RP^2 is not flat. The four corners of the square fall into two classes of
two, so each corner class is a cone point of total angle pi rather than
2*pi: a walker circling that cell returns to its start after TWO quarter
turns, not four. That is a property no other surface in grid-atlas has, and
the one worth testing -- CubeMap's corners are cone points of angle 3*pi/2
for the same reason (three squares meeting), so cubeStep's machinery has
already met the phenomenon and there may be a shared law here.

Check first whether a step function can even be written totally at those
corners with the current single-chart shape. If a diagonal-ish walk hits an
ambiguity there, that is the finding, and it is the first thing in this
package that SeamTable's involution law does NOT catch -- the law is about
half-edges pairing up, and cone angle is a fact about corners.

title: _SplitGrid: splitGrid/combineGrid is the shape algebra's associativity, stated as two functions
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier A: a genuine Iso, and the one
that most deserves to be one -- this is the shape algebra's associativity
law, currently stated as two functions that happen to be inverse.

  splitGrid   :: (VG.Vector v a, AllSizedKnown cs)
              => GridOf v (c ': cs) a -> Grid '[c] (GridOf v cs a)   Internal/Grid.hs:534
  combineGrid :: VG.Vector v a
              => Grid '[c] (GridOf v cs a) -> GridOf v (c ': cs) a   Internal/Grid.hs:549

Both total, mutually inverse: `splitGrid` chops the row-major vector into
`MaxCoordSize cs`-sized chunks, `combineGrid` concatenates them back in the
same order.

  _SplitGrid :: (VG.Vector v a, AllSizedKnown cs)
             => Iso' (GridOf v (c ': cs) a) (Grid '[c] (GridOf v cs a))
  _SplitGrid = iso splitGrid combineGrid

The Iso takes the union of the two constraint sets, so `AllSizedKnown cs`
comes along even though `combineGrid` does not need it. That is not
avoidable and is not a real cost -- every caller with a concrete shape has it.

What it buys: `over _SplitGrid` is "do something to the grid as a stack of
slices and put it back", which today has to be written as
`combineGrid . f . splitGrid` with the round trip visible. It also composes
with the outer `Grid '[c]`'s own Traversable, so `_SplitGrid . traversed` is
a Traversal over the slices -- see the mapLowerDim issue, which arrives at
the same traversal from the other direction and should be cross-checked
against this one for consistency of order.

Note the asymmetry the splitGrid Haddock already records: the OUTER grid is
always boxed whatever `v` is, because a grid is never an unboxed element.
The Iso inherits that and should repeat the note.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Added and exported _SplitGrid as an Iso' over splitGrid/combineGrid, with focused Iso law coverage; full grid-sized suite passes.

title: aoc/src/2024/04.hs: coordFromTuple/coordRay fails to type-check after the Coord row-major rewrite
description:
Discovered while migrating aoc's asFocusedGrid call sites off the removed
IsGrid method (sized-grid-3au / sized-grid-nbt).

../aoc/src/2024/04.hs (lines 57 and 76) fails to compile:

    [i, j, k] <- [take 3 (coordRay c (coordFromTuple (dy, dx)))]
    -- Cannot satisfy: 1 <= p5 / 1 <= p4

    traverse (offsetCoord c . coordFromTuple) $ ...
    -- Cannot satisfy: 1 <= p3 / 1 <= p1

`dy`/`dx` are runtime Integers from a list comprehension; `coordFromTuple`
used to resolve the tuple's target Coord/Delta type without leaving
unsolved `1 <= n` axis constraints on the result. It no longer does.

This is unrelated to the asFocusedGrid removal (git diff for that fix
touches only import lines and the two `view asFocusedGrid` call sites,
not lines 57/76) and predates this session: aoc/src/2024/04.hs was last
edited 2026-08-16, but sized-grid's row-major Coord rewrite (6ade7e3,
"Represent Coord as its row-major position", sized-grid-adr.16) landed
2026-08-19 -- three days later. That rewrite, or the adr.8 traversal
follow-up the next day (e491670), is the likely cause.

The other three aoc call sites fixed alongside this (2015/18.hs,
2018/18.hs, 2025/04.hs) build and link cleanly against current
sized-grid, so this looks isolated to coordFromTuple/coordRay/Delta's
inference, not the FocusedGrid API change.

Next step: reproduce standalone (a coordFromTuple/coordRay call outside
aoc) to find exactly which type stopped being inferred, then decide
whether the fix belongs in sized-grid's Delta/coordFromTuple signature or
in aoc's call site.

title: Generalize cubeStep's chart-boundary detection, or decide it stays cube-specific
description:
Left open deliberately by sized-grid-1av and untouched by sized-grid-b15, which extracted only the seam-table half into atlas-topology.

The other half of Data.Grid.Atlas.CubeMap's cubeStep -- deciding that a step leaves the current chart, and turning a seam-table answer into a landing coordinate -- is still written against Ordinal n x Ordinal n directly. Generalizing it would mean fixing an API (something like 'HasBoundary chart pos boundary': given a position and a heading, is this a crossing, and which boundary label) against a single example, and the shape of the answer depends on a question nobody has answered yet: is a chart always coordinate-shaped, or could it be a bare graph node with numbered ports (sized-grid-ts4's pathfinding aside)?

Do not build on speculation. The trigger is the same as b15's was: a second concrete chart shape that is not an n x n grid. Until then the honest outcome may be closing this as 'stays in grid-atlas'.
notes:
Done as a generalization, not a close-as-cube-specific. The trigger the issue names -- a second concrete chart shape that is not an n x n grid -- arrived in sized-grid-00v: a Mobius strip is Clamped w x Clamped h with a real edge on one axis, and mobiusStep was written as a near-copy of cubeStep (duplicate Axis, Heading, sideSign, signSide).

Extracted as Data.Grid.Atlas.Rect in grid-atlas, not in atlas-topology: this half knows what a chart is (a rectangle of cells), and Seam.hs's own split says that half stays with whoever knows. rectStep takes exactly what the two callers disagree about -- per-axis sizes, the gluing as a lookup rather than a SeamTable, and how partial that lookup is, as the Applicative it answers in (Identity for the cube, so cubeStep stays total; Maybe for the strip). Positions are raw Int pairs, so Ordinal vs Clamped wrapping stays with the caller.

Deliberately NOT done: no HasBoundary class. Both atlases are rectangular, and a class fitted to two instances of one shape is a guess about the third. The question the issue flags -- is a chart always coordinate-shaped, or a graph node with numbered ports -- is still open and still needs a non-rectangular chart to answer it. What changed is that the answer now has a place to go: everything Rect contributes is separated from the cube- and Mobius-specific tables.

No behaviour change; both belt tests pass unchanged. Follow-up filed as sized-grid-1yn.
close_reason: Closed
