title: AllSizedKnown restates evidence All IsCoordLifted already determines
description:
Inspiration: the witness pattern in the `manifolds` package. `SemimanifoldWitness` and
`PseudoAffineWitness` exist, in Hackage's words, to "reify constraints to avoid requiring
UndecidableSuperclasses" --- inductive evidence packaged as a VALUE in the class, because
a superclass cannot carry it.

sized-grid states the same fact twice, as two separate obligations:

  - `All IsCoordLifted cs` gives, per axis, `KnownNat (CoordNat x)` and
    `x ~ CoordContainer x (CoordNat x)` (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:111-119).
  - `AllSizedKnown cs` (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:487-498) gives
    `Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))`.

The second is DETERMINED by the first: `MaxCoordSize` is the product of the per-axis
nats, and `AllSizedKnown`'s own instance body is nothing but that induction with
`timesNat` at each step. So it is derivable evidence being demanded as a separate class.

SCOPE CORRECTION --- READ THIS BEFORE ESTIMATING THE PAYOFF

This is NOT a consumer-ergonomics win, and an earlier framing of it overstated the case.
sized-grid-qh9 already established that for a CONCRETE `cs` the class is discharged by
instance resolution from `KnownNat n` alone and callers pay nothing. The cost lands only
where `cs` is a type variable, i.e. the library's own signatures and polymorphic helpers:

    src/            19 occurrences (grep -rn AllSizedKnown src/)
    tests/Main.hs:86,154        alongside `All IsCoordLifted cs`
    gameOfLife/src/Main.hs:59,152

and gameOfLife is the clearest case, because it lists BOTH halves of the same fact:

       , KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)
       , AllSizedKnown cs

`AllSizedKnown cs` supplies exactly that `KnownNat` as a `Dict`, so the two lines are
redundant with each other.

PROPOSAL

Replace the class with a function that produces the evidence from the dictionary the
caller already has:

    sizeProof :: forall cs. All IsCoordLifted cs => Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))

by induction on `sList`, `timesNat @(CoordNat x) @(MaxCoordSize xs)` at each step.

PREREQUISITE: `MaxCoordSize` (Coord.hs:256-258) currently matches on the SHAPE `c n`:

    MaxCoordSize ((c n) ': cs) = n GHC.* (MaxCoordSize cs)

which will not reduce for an abstract axis type. Restate it via the projection so it
reduces from `IsCoordLifted` alone:

    MaxCoordSize (c ': cs) = CoordNat c GHC.* MaxCoordSize cs

RISKS

  - Widens some signatures from `AllSizedKnown cs` to `All IsCoordLifted cs`, which
    additionally demands `1 <= n` per axis. Affects the sites that use `AllSizedKnown`
    ALONE today: `gridFromVector` (Internal/Grid.hs:112), `Applicative (Grid cs)`
    (:139), `Arbitrary1` (tests/Test/Arbitrary.hs:38). Probably fine --- a zero-width
    axis makes `MaxCoordSize` zero and the grid empty --- but it must be checked rather
    than assumed.
  - `sizeProof` becomes a per-call induction over `sList`. See the recorded memory
    `sized-grid-slist-from-all-dict`: getting `sList` from an `All c xs` dictionary is
    NOT free, it goes through `cpara_SList`. Here the fold is over DIMENSIONS (at most a
    handful), not cells, and produces a `Dict` GHC can float --- but the benchmark suite
    should confirm `pure`/`tabulate` do not regress, since `Applicative (Grid cs)` calls
    it on every `pure`.

RELATED: sized-grid-qh9 covers the mirror-image problem for `AllGridSizeKnown` (a type
family, so it DOES leak to consumers). These two should be designed together --- qh9's
option 2 proposes converting `AllGridSizeKnown` INTO the shape of `AllSizedKnown`, while
this issue proposes dissolving `AllSizedKnown` into a function. Resolve the disagreement
before either is implemented.
design: Witness pattern from manifolds: derivable inductive evidence should be a value produced from a dictionary the caller already holds, not a separate class the caller must satisfy. Prerequisite is restating MaxCoordSize via CoordNat so it reduces for an abstract axis type. Must be reconciled with sized-grid-qh9, which proposes moving AllGridSizeKnown INTO the shape this issue proposes dissolving.
acceptance_criteria: AllSizedKnown is gone from src/; tests/Main.hs and gameOfLife/src/Main.hs each drop a constraint without gaining one; bench shows no regression in pure/tabulate.

Reconciled AllSizedKnown (Coord.hs) and AllGridSizeKnown (Internal/Grid.hs) into one class rather than dissolving AllSizedKnown into a function as originally proposed -- qh9 and h56 had both reaffirmed 'class, not function' for this exact kind of inductive evidence since this issue was filed, and the concrete redundancy 4xh cited (gameOfLife stating both halves) was already gone. AllSizedKnown now carries KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs) as a superclass plus a SizeProof GADT witness (AllGridSizeKnown's shape); AllGridSizeKnown is deleted. Fixed the real remaining duplication at tests/Main.hs's gridTests (AllSizedKnown cs + AllGridSizeKnown [f x, g y] for the same cs). Verified: full build, both test suites (485+4 checks), and pure/tabulate/collapseGrid/gridFromList/JSON benchmarks against a git-archive HEAD baseline all show unchanged allocations.

title: Universe and Finite (universe-base): universe = allCoord
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey.

  instance IsCoordList cs => Universe (Coord cs) where universe = allCoord
  instance IsCoordList cs => Finite   (Coord cs) where universeF = allCoord

allCoord already exists (Coord.hs:275) and is already documented as
enumerating every value in order. The instances are one line each and the
same holds for Ordinal and the four axis types via allCoordLike
(Coord/Class.hs:371).

The argument for it is that Universe is the ecosystem's standard "this type
is enumerable" interface, and several generic libraries dispatch on it --
which is a different thing from Enum, whose contract is about succ/pred, and
from Bounded, whose contract is about extremes.

The argument against is that a consumer with allCoord in scope gets the same
list without the class, so this only pays off for code that is polymorphic
in the type.

== Cost

universe-base is a genuinely new dependency -- it is not in the current build
plan. It is base-only and well maintained, which makes it a much smaller
commitment than finitary, but it is still a package.

P4 deliberately: this is the lowest-value accepted line in the survey, and it
should be picked up only once the free ones are done.
close_reason: Added Universe and Finite instances for Coord, Ordinal, and all axis policies, with focused tests and universe-base dependency wiring.

title: Semialign and Zip for Grid (and the survey's Align/Semialign conflation, corrected)
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey. Corrects one line of it.

== The correction

The survey said "Zip (semialign), pointwise. But NOT Align: aligning needs a
shape union, and the shape is fixed." The conclusion is right and the reason
is wrong for one of the two classes, and the difference matters because you
cannot have Zip without the class the reason rejects.

semialign's hierarchy is

  class Functor f    => Semialign f  where align, alignWith
  class Semialign f  => Align f      where nil
  class Semialign f  => Zip f        where zip, zipWith
  class Zip f        => Repeat f     where repeat

Semialign is Zip's SUPERCLASS, so Zip (Grid cs) is not reachable without it.
And Semialign is perfectly lawful here: the shapes of two Grid cs values are
equal by type, so

  alignWith f a b = zipWithGrid (\x y -> f (These x y)) a b

is total and simply never produces This or That. Nothing about align needs a
shape union -- that is a property of the list and Map instances, not of the
class.

Align is the one to reject, and the reason is its method: nil :: f a is an
empty structure, and there is no empty grid at a fixed shape. Same argument
that rejects Alternative and MonadPlus.

Repeat is reachable (repeat = pure) but needs AllSizedKnown, unlike Semialign
and Zip which need only IsCoordList. Add it or not on its own merits.

== Accept

  instance IsCoordList cs => Semialign (Grid cs)   -- align never misses
  instance IsCoordList cs => Zip (Grid cs)         -- zipWithGrid

Both at IsCoordList, which is WEAKER than the AllSizedKnown that Applicative
carries. That is the real payoff: a consumer can zip grids in a context that
has no size evidence, which liftA2 cannot do.

== Reject, and record why

  Align (Grid cs)   -- nil has no inhabitant at a fixed shape
  Unalign, Unzip    -- only if a use appears; they are not free

== Cost

None. semialign is already in the build plan, pulled in by aeson.
notes: Follow-up: added three QuickCheck coherence properties. The focused group now passes 5 tests, including 100 randomized cases for each property.
close_reason: Implemented pointwise Semialign and Zip instances for Grid with IsCoordList constraints, added direct semialign/these dependencies, and added regression tests. Ticket-specific tests pass; full suite retains three unrelated pre-existing Coord enum-law failures.

title: Apply the ray rewrite to ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs when sized-grid-dr1 reaches master
description:
sized-grid-dr1 added `coordRay` and `offsetCoordUpTo`, the offset that reports where
it hit the edge. ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs is the call site that asked for them and can
now drop the workaround it was built on.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ISSUE, AND WHEN TO DO IT

Exactly as sized-grid-bij: aoc/cabal.project lists ../sized-grid as a source package,
so aoc builds against the MAIN sized-grid checkout on master, not against any
.claude/worktrees branch. aoc keeps working while dr1 sits on branch
worktree-offset-boundary-report and this patch would not even compile until it lands.
Apply WITH the master merge, not before it.

aoc's working tree also has substantial uncommitted changes, which is why this was
verified out-of-tree rather than applied. Rebase if 2024/04.hs has moved.

WHAT CHANGES, AND WHY THE GRID TYPE CHANGES WITH IT

The day is a bounded word search: XMAS must not wrap round an edge. The grid was
nevertheless `Grid '[Periodic n, Periodic n]`, and the boundedness was simulated ---
strengthen every coordinate into a grid one cell larger, walk there, and let
`weakenCoord` reject anything that landed in the pad. That is what forced
`strengthenCoord`/`weakenCoord`, `mapMaybe (traverse weakenCoord)` and the three
`Dict` entailments (`plusNat`, `leTrans`, `plusMonotone2`).

With a ray that stops at an edge, the simulation is unnecessary: the axes become
`Clamped`, which is what the pad was imitating, and part one becomes
`take 3 (coordRay c d)` with a pattern match that drops the directions without room.
Part two becomes `traverse (offsetCoord c . coordFromTuple)` over the four diagonals.
partTwo's signature loses `KnownNat (n + 1)` and `n <= n + 1`.

VERIFICATION ALREADY DONE (2026-08-12, against the worktree build)

Using the scratch-project workaround in memory `sized-grid-aoc-cannot-be-cabal-built`,
with the extra deps from `sized-grid-aoc-typecheck-extra-deps`:

  - type-checks against the dr1 worktree
  - the module's own documented examples still answer 18 and 9
  - old and new agree on ALL FOUR answers over 300 random 12x12 grids, so the
    rewrite is behaviour-preserving and the real input still answers 2532/1941

The full input (input/2024/04.txt) is NOT in the repo, so 2532/1941 could not be
produced directly. The random-grid equivalence above is the evidence in its place.

THE PATCH

Apply from the aoc repo root with `git apply`.

```diff
--- a/src/2024/04.hs
+++ b/src/2024/04.hs
@@ -17,24 +17,23 @@
 import Control.Comonad (extend, extract)
 import Control.Comonad.Store (experiment)
 import Control.Lens (view)
-import Data.AffineSpace ((.+^))
 import Data.Attoparsec.ByteString.Char8 (Parser, char, choice, endOfLine, many1, parseOnly, sepBy)
 import Data.Bool (bool)
 import Data.ByteString qualified as BS (readFile)
-import Data.Constraint (withDict, (\\))
-import Data.Constraint.Nat (leTrans, plusMonotone2, plusNat)
 import Data.Function (on)
 import Data.Functor.Compose (Compose (..))
 import Data.Functor.Product (Product (Pair))
-import Data.Maybe (fromJust, mapMaybe)
-import GHC.TypeNats (KnownNat, type (+), type (<=))
+import Data.Maybe (fromJust)
+import GHC.TypeNats (KnownNat, type (<=))
 import GHC.TypeNats qualified as GHC
-import SizedGrid (Grid, IsGrid (asFocusedGrid), Periodic, StrengthenCoord (strengthenCoord), WeakenCoord (weakenCoord), gridFromList)
-import SizedGrid.Coord (Coord, coordFromTuple)
+import SizedGrid (Clamped, Grid, IsGrid (asFocusedGrid), gridFromList)
+import SizedGrid.Coord (Coord, coordFromTuple, coordRay, offsetCoord)
 
 data Cell = X | M | A | S deriving (Eq, Show)
 
-type Input n = Grid '[Periodic n, Periodic n] Cell
+-- The word must not wrap round the edge of the puzzle, so the axes are Clamped:
+-- a walk off the end of one stops instead of coming back on the other side.
+type Input n = Grid '[Clamped n, Clamped n] Cell
 
 -- (2532,1941)
 main :: IO ()
@@ -60,24 +59,18 @@
 solve :: forall n. (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Input n -> Int
 solve = sum . fmap occurences . extend (\s -> if extract s == X then experiment applyContext s else mempty) . view asFocusedGrid
   where
-    applyContext :: Coord '[Periodic n, Periodic n] -> Context (Coord '[Periodic n, Periodic n])
+    applyContext :: Coord '[Clamped n, Clamped n] -> Context (Coord '[Clamped n, Clamped n])
     applyContext c =
-      Compose $
-        mapMaybe
-          (traverse weakenCoord)
-          [ Three i j k
-          | dy <- [-1 .. 1],
-            dx <- [-1 .. 1],
-            (dy, dx) /= (0, 0),
-            let d = coordFromTuple (dy, dx),
-            let i, j, k :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)]
-                i = strengthenCoord c .+^ d
-                j = i .+^ d
-                k = j .+^ d
-          ]
-          \\ plusNat @n @1
-          \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1)
-          \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1
+      Compose
+        [ Three i j k
+        | dy <- [-1 .. 1],
+          dx <- [-1 .. 1],
+          (dy, dx) /= (0, 0),
+          -- Three steps that way, or nothing: the ray stops at the edge, so a
+          -- direction without room for a whole word yields fewer than three
+          -- cells and the pattern match drops it.
+          [i, j, k] <- [take 3 (coordRay c (coordFromTuple (dy, dx)))]
+        ]
 
     occurences :: Context Cell -> Int
     occurences = length . filter (== Three M A S) . getCompose
@@ -88,19 +81,17 @@
 
 -- >>> partTwo example
 -- 9
-partTwo :: forall n. (1 <= n, KnownNat n, KnownNat (n + 1), n <= n + 1) => Input n -> Int
+partTwo :: forall n. (1 <= n, KnownNat n) => Input n -> Int
 partTwo = sum . fmap (bool 0 1 . isXmas) . extend (\s -> if extract s == A then experiment applyContext s else Compose Nothing) . view asFocusedGrid
   where
-    applyContext :: Coord '[Periodic n, Periodic n] -> ContextTwo (Coord '[Periodic n, Periodic n])
-    applyContext c' =
-      withDict (plusNat @n @1) . withDict (plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1) $
-        withDict (leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1)) $
-          let c :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)] = strengthenCoord c'
-           in Compose $
-                traverse weakenCoord $
-                  Pair
-                    (Two (c .+^ coordFromTuple (-1, -1)) (c .+^ coordFromTuple (1, 1)))
-                    (Two (c .+^ coordFromTuple (-1, 1)) (c .+^ coordFromTuple (1, -1)))
+    applyContext :: Coord '[Clamped n, Clamped n] -> ContextTwo (Coord '[Clamped n, Clamped n])
+    applyContext c =
+      -- One diagonal step each way, and all four have to land on the grid.
+      Compose $
+        traverse (offsetCoord c . coordFromTuple) $
+          Pair
+            (Two (-1, -1) (1, 1))
+            (Two (-1, 1) (1, -1))
 
     isXmas :: ContextTwo Cell -> Bool
     isXmas (Compose (Just (Pair l r))) = on (&&) (`elem` [Two M S, Two S M]) l r
```

title: sudoko: write the actual solver using rowAtPoint/columAtPoint/squareAtPoint/allValues
description:
sized-grid-dvm wired rowAtPoint, columAtPoint, squareAtPoint and allValues
into sudoko/src/Main.hs's main (a single sample-point demo at (4,4)) purely
to clear -Wunused-top-binds under the repo-wide -Werror it turned on. That

sudoko's own module docstring already says: "'main' validates the board
rather than solving it: the search itself is still to be written." A
sibling comment on the executable's build-depends notes that
recursion-schemes/free/lens used to be dependencies of "an unfinished
Cofree-based search that was never written."

This issue is to actually write that search: a backtracking (or
constraint-propagation) solver over Board using allValues for candidate
generation per cell and rowAtPoint/columAtPoint/squareAtPoint (or

title: quickcheck-classes law bundles the suite could run but does not
description:
quickcheck-classes-0.6.5.0 is already a test dependency and Test.Utils already
has lawsToTest to render a Laws bundle (tests/Test/Utils.hs). Adding a bundle
is mostly a matter of listing it in tests/Main.hs, so the cost per law here is
close to a line.

== What the suite runs today

From quickcheck-classes (tests/Main.hs:32-34): functorLaws, applicativeLaws,
monadLaws, foldableLaws, traversableLaws -- all on Grid only.

Hand-rolled in Test.Utils: eq1Laws, aesonLaws, semigroupLaws, monoidLaws,
additiveGroupLaws, affineSpaceLaws, traversalLaws, isoLaws, isCoordLaws,
comonadLaws, representableLaws, distributiveLaws.

== Gaps, ranked by what they would actually catch

1. ordLaws and eqLaws, on Coord.
   Eq (Coord cs) (Coord.hs:123) and Ord (Coord cs) (Coord.hs:129) are written
   by hand over NP -- hcliftA2 folds, not deriving. Nothing in the suite tests
   transitivity, antisymmetry, or that compare agrees with (==). This is the
   largest hand-written-instance-with-no-law-test surface in the library.

2. jsonLaws, and a ToJSONKey/FromJSONKey property that does not exist at all.
   The hand-rolled aesonLaws (tests/Test/Utils.hs:63) checks exactly one
   thing: decode (encode a) == Just a. quickcheck-classes' jsonLaws also
   checks that toEncoding agrees with toJSON -- the classic aeson divergence
   -- and that parsing the Value round-trips, which is a different code path
   from parsing the ByteString.
   Separately: Ordinal and all four axis types have ToJSONKey and FromJSONKey
   instances, and NOTHING tests them. Key encoding is its own code path. That
   one has to be hand-rolled; quickcheck-classes does not cover it.

3. showLaws.
   Show (Ordinal m) (Ordinal.hs:104) and Show (Coord cs) (Coord.hs:135) are
   hand-written. showLaws checks showsPrec and showList agree with show.

4. commutativeMonoidLaws / commutativeSemigroupLaws.
   Periodic, Clamped and any Coord product of them are commutative, and
   nothing records it. Cheap, and it is a real property a consumer might lean
   on when reordering a fold.

5. semigroupMonoidLaws.
   Several instances still write `mappend = (<>)` explicitly (Periodic.hs:52,
   Clamped.hs:40, Coord.hs:163). This bundle is exactly the check that the two
   agree, which is the only reason those lines are safe.

6. enumLaws and boundedEnumLaws -- the interesting one.
   Periodic's toEnum wraps with `mod` (Periodic.hs:28) and Periodic has NO
   Bounded instance, while Clamped, Reflective and Reflect101 all derive both.
   Running these either passes, or pins down precisely why a wrapping Enum
   cannot satisfy them. Both outcomes are worth having written down, and the
   answer decides the Bounded (Periodic n) line on sized-grid-90f.

7. genericLaws. GridOf derives stock Generic (Internal/Grid.hs:73).

== Conditional on sized-grid-90f

These become available only if the matching instance lands, and each is a
reason to trust that instance:

  ixLaws                              if Ix (Coord cs)
  storableLaws / primLaws / muvectorLaws   if Storable / Prim / Unbox
  monadZipLaws                        if MonadZip (pointwise) is added
  applyLaws                           if Apply is added

== Not applicable, for the record

alternativeLaws, monadPlusLaws, altLaws, plusLaws -- Grid has no empty.
bifunctorLaws, bifoldableLaws, bitraversableLaws -- nothing is bifunctorial.
numLaws, ringLaws, semiringLaws, integralLaws, euclideanLaws, gcdDomainLaws,
bitsLaws -- see the rejected Num/Ring line on sized-grid-90f.
isListLaws, showReadLaws -- no IsList and no Read instances.
idempotentSemigroupLaws, rectangularBandSemigroupLaws -- not idempotent.

== Note for whoever picks this up

The higher-kinded bundles want Arbitrary1 as well as Arbitrary; the
first-order ones above want only Arbitrary, which tests/Test/Arbitrary.hs
already supplies for the coord types. Landing items 1-5 should need no new
Arbitrary instances at all.
notes: All 7 items landed (see prior notes for 1-6). Item 7: genericLaws for GridOf's derived Generic, via a new Arbitrary (Rep a ()) instance in tests/Test/Arbitrary.hs routed through Grid's existing Arbitrary and GHC.Generics.from -- needed the type-variable+equality-constraint instance-head trick since Rep is a type family and can't appear in an instance head directly, plus OVERLAPPABLE since that head is maximally general. All 582 tests pass. Not landed: the sized-grid-90f-conditional bundles (ixLaws, storableLaws/primLaws/muvectorLaws, monadZipLaws, applyLaws) since their preconditions (Ix/Storable/Prim/Unbox/MonadZip/Apply instances) don't exist yet -- tracked by those issues already. Ready to close.
close_reason: Closed

title: stepsWithin folds the axis list with a helper that cannot unroll: the real neighbourhood cost
description:
Third instance of the defect sized-grid-czf and sized-grid-135 fixed, and this is the one the neighbourhood workloads actually run.

sized-grid-135 was filed on the premise that 'the neighbourhood path is what
gameOfLife, ising-example and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs and 2018/18.hs actually run'
and that the path went through offsetCoord. It does not. neighbours =
mooreNeighbours 1, and mooreNeighbours r c = [n | (s, n) <- stepsWithin r c, s > 0].
stepsWithin never calls offsetCoord.

What it calls is its own where-helper (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs):

    stepsWithin r (Coord cs) = fmap Coord <$> go cs
      where
        go :: IsCoordList xs => NP I xs -> [(Int, NP I xs)]
        go Nil = [(0, Nil)]
        go (I x :* xs) = do
            (d, v) <- axisSteps r x
            (s, rest) <- go xs
            return (d + s, I v :* rest)

Self-recursive and polymorphic in the axis list, so it cannot unroll and every
axis after the first peels the IsCoordList dictionary at run time. Exactly the
shape of the two folds already moved into class methods.

EVIDENCE. 'extend neighbourSum 50x50' is 2,500 cells x 8 Moore neighbours. It
measured 9.17 ms / 28 MB before sized-grid-czf, 9.18 ms / 28 MB after it, and
9.02 ms / 28 MB after sized-grid-135. Neither fold fix touched it, because
neither fold is on this path. That is what identifies this helper.

APPROACH. Same as the other two: an IsCoordList method. The per-axis step is
axisSteps, whose only obligation is IsCoordLifted x, which IsCoordList already
supplies per axis -- so like npOffset and unlike AffineCoordList, this needs no
new class and is not a breaking change. Note the step also carries the radius r,
so the method takes it as an argument.

axisSteps is worth a look in the same pass but is a separate cost: it builds a
'reachable' list per axis per call and filters it with 'any' over that same
list, which is quadratic in r.

VERIFY WITH 'extend neighbourSum 50x50' in bench/Main.hs, measuring both sides
now per that file's header. Do not read against the recorded CSV.
notes:
DONE in 7915bff. The fold is now npStepsWithin, an IsCoordList method; axisSteps
moved to SizedGrid.Coord.Class so the method could be stated there, and
SizedGrid.Coord re-exports it, so no import changes and no breaking change ---
the approach in the issue was right that IsCoordList already supplies the
per-axis obligation.

Core verified at '[Clamped 50, Clamped 50]: the fold unrolls to two per-axis
loops calling $waxisSteps directly, no axis-list dictionary, no recursion left.

MEASURED, both sides in one session, 'extend neighbourSum 50x50':
  25,709,079 B / 6.840 ms  ->  23,421,527 B / 6.544 ms   (-8.9% alloc, -4.3%)
Every other benchmark's allocation byte-identical. 334 tests, downstream and
readme pass.

THE FINDING, which is worth more than the fix: the issue's premise was half
wrong. The fold was real and is gone, but it was only 9% of the neighbourhood
cost. The rest is one function below it --- axisSteps rescans its whole
candidate list per candidate. Skipping that scan where it cannot fire measured
12 MB / 2.24 ms on the same benchmark, 67% under baseline. Filed as
sized-grid-knm with the experiment and the class-contract question it raises.

This closes out the fold defect the IsCoordList note describes: all three
instances (AffineCoordList, npOffset, npStepsWithin) are now class methods.
close_reason: Closed

title: WIP gridWindows: rows work, but 'mapLowerDim gridWindows' for columns/squares takes a cartesian product
description:
Applies to the uncommitted change in src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:258-266 and its use in
sudoko/src/Main.hs:50-59.

CONFIRMED with a 4x4 stand-in for the 9x9 board:

    rows    = gridWindows board                 -- 4 results, correct
    columns = mapLowerDim gridWindows board     -- 256 results, expected 4

The first six 'columns' produced were
    [1,5,9,13] [1,5,9,14] [1,5,9,15] [1,5,9,16] [1,5,10,13] [1,5,10,14]
i.e. every combination of one cell per row, not the four actual columns.

Cause: mapLowerDim (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:221-233) ends in

    traverse (fmap unGrid . f . Grid) (splitVectorBySize ... v)

With f = [] the list applicative is the cartesian product, so n sub-grids each
yielding n windows gives n^n results. For the real 9x9 sudoko board that is
9^9 = 387,420,489 grids -- sudoko/src/Main.hs:54 'columns' and :56 'squares' will
both hang.

Fix: the intent is a zip, not a product. Use ZipList:

    columns = getZipList $ mapLowerDim (ZipList . gridWindows) board

That yields exactly 4 (resp. 9). Worth checking 'squares' the same way -- it is
'gridWindows' then 'mapLowerDim gridWindows', so it has the same defect.

Separately, gridWindows' signature is weak:
  - 'small' and 'big' are only related by 'CoordNat big `Mod` CoordNat small ~ 0';
    nothing ties the element counts to 'rest', so a caller can ask for a shape that
    does not tile the source.
  - splitVectorBySize's final clause returns a short trailing chunk rather than
    failing, so a non-dividing size silently yields a malformed last Grid.
  - The name says 'windows' but the behaviour is non-overlapping tiles. Sliding
    windows and disjoint tiles are different operations; pick one and name it.

Suggest landing this as two functions -- 'gridTiles' (disjoint, what the code does)
and a real 'gridWindows' (overlapping, stride 1) -- with the ZipList variant for
the lower-dimension case.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 4767533 on worktree-examples-build-s25.

Root cause was as diagnosed: mapLowerDim combines per-sub-grid results with traverse, so f ~ [] is the list applicative and yields a cartesian product (4^4 = 256 at the 4x4 stand-in, 9^9 = 387,420,489 on the real board).

Landed:
  - zipLowerDim :: AllSizedKnown as => (Grid as x -> [Grid bs y]) -> Grid (c ': as) x -> [Grid (c ': bs) y], which is mapLowerDim in ZipList. 'zipLowerDim gridTiles' gives the 9 columns.
  - gridWindows renamed to gridTiles. It always cut disjoint tiles; the old name promised sliding windows. Safe rename -- sudoko was the only caller in this repo or ../aoc, and 0.3.0.0 is unpublished.
  - mapLowerDim's haddock now names the safe applicatives (Identity, Maybe) and the trap ([]), because the wrong choice is the obvious one.
  - splitVectorBySize rejects a chunk size of 0 instead of looping forever on empty prefixes.
  - tests/Test/Tiling.hs: 10 new tests covering gridTiles and zipLowerDim at 4x4 and 9x9, including a length assertion that would not have terminated before, plus one that pins mapLowerDim's cartesian-product behaviour so the two do not get folded back together. Suite is 90 tests, up from 80.
  - sudoko now prints all nine rows, columns and squares.

Two of the issue's sub-points resolved differently than suggested:
  - 'splitVectorBySize returns a short trailing chunk rather than failing' is unreachable from gridTiles: the Mod ~ 0 constraint plus the Grid length invariant means the chunk size always divides the source exactly. Documented rather than made total, since other callers in the module are equally protected.
  - The real (overlapping, stride 1) gridWindows was NOT added -- it is a new operation, not needed to fix the hang. Filed as sized-grid-3t6 (P3); shrinkGrid is already the primitive it would be built from.

Found while fixing: gameIsInvalid in the example ran allUnique over the Maybes, so two blank cells read as a duplicate and every partially-filled board was called invalid. Fixed to check the filled cells only.

title: _SplitHigherDim: an Iso with a y <= x side condition natnormalise must still discharge
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier A: a genuine Iso with a type-level
side condition.

  splitHigherDim :: (VG.Vector v a, KnownNat y, y <= x, AllSizedKnown as)
                 => GridOf v (c x ': as) a
                 -> (GridOf v (c y ': as) a, GridOf v (c (x - y) ': as) a)   Internal/Grid.hs:628

  combineHigherDim :: VG.Vector v x
                   => GridOf v (c n ': as) x
                   -> GridOf v (c m ': as) x
                   -> GridOf v (c (n + m) ': as) x                            Internal/Grid.hs:559

  _SplitHigherDim :: (VG.Vector v a, KnownNat y, y <= x, AllSizedKnown as)
                  => Iso' (GridOf v (c x ': as) a)
                          (GridOf v (c y ': as) a, GridOf v (c (x - y) ': as) a)
  _SplitHigherDim = iso splitHigherDim (uncurry combineHigherDim)

The two are inverse only where `y + (x - y) ~ x`, which over GHC's truncating
subtraction needs `y <= x` in scope -- exactly the constraint splitHigherDim
already carries and combineHigherDim does not. ghc-typelits-natnormalise
discharges it; check that it still does through the Iso newtype, since the
plugin has been sensitive to where the equality is demanded before (see the
sliceGrid comment at Internal/Grid.hs:600 for the precedent, where composing
takeGrid after dropGrid put the bound out of the solver's reach and the fix
was to restate it as linear arithmetic).

`y` is ambiguous and must be supplied at the call site either way. Every
other size in this API travels as a RequiredTypeArgument (`takeGrid 3 g`), so
the natural spelling is `_SplitHigherDim y :: forall y -> ...` rather than a
type application -- match the surrounding convention rather than lens's.

Worth confirming before writing: `splitHigherDim`'s Haddock records that its
second component used to be a free type variable and was pinned to `x - y`
deliberately. The Iso must not undo that.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.

title: Cube map: 6 charts glued by a D4 transition table, first non-identity atlas seam
description:
Follow-up to sized-grid-fh2's v1 (grid-atlas, the degenerate/tiled atlas,
merged this session). That slice deliberately only ever glues charts with an
identity transition -- same position on every axis but the one that was
tiled, no axis flip or swap, because a tiling never needs one.

A cube map is the smallest atlas where that stops being true: 6 same-shaped
charts (grid-sized `Grid '[Ordinal n, Ordinal n] a` each), and crossing an
edge of one face lands you on an edge of a neighbouring face rotated by some
element of D4 -- the local u/v axes get swapped and/or sign-flipped, not just
translated. That is an off-diagonal frame transform in sized-grid-1bm's
sense, the exact case grid-atlas v1's Atlas/atlasOffsetHead type deliberately
cannot express (atlasOffsetHead only ever moves the head axis of the SAME
Coord cs shape, never permutes axes or crosses into a differently-oriented
local frame).

WHAT THIS NEEDS THAT V1 DOES NOT HAVE

  * A real seam-transition representation: for a given chart and which edge
    was crossed, the destination chart plus a coordinate map Coord cs ->
    Coord cs (not just "same axis, adjacent chart") plus the frame transform
    for headings crossing it (sized-grid-o1n's Needle -> Needle, concretely a
    signed axis permutation now that there are exactly 2 axes per face).
  * The transition table for a cube: 6 faces x 4 edges = 24 entries, but by
    D4 symmetry there are only a handful of distinct rotation cases to get
    right (identity glue where faces already agree, and 90/180/270-degree
    rotations at the rest) -- worth deriving by hand first since the issue
    that spawned this (sized-grid-fh2) says the cube map is checkable by
    hand, that is the point of picking it first.
  * Decide where the transition table lives: grid-atlas (grid-specific), or
    does building this finally answer sized-grid-ts4 (is the seam/atlas
    layer actually a grid-independent manifold library)? This is the second
    concrete atlas ts4 says is the minimum evidence needed to answer that
    question -- do that comparison as part of this work, not before it.

NOT heterogeneous chart shapes (all 6 faces are the same Ordinal n x
Ordinal n shape) -- that is still out of scope here too.
close_reason:
Shipped: Data.Grid.Atlas.CubeMap (grid-atlas/src/Data/Grid/Atlas/CubeMap.hs). 6 faces (Face), each Grid '[Ordinal n, Ordinal n] a, glued by cubeSeam -- a 24-equation hand-transcribed transition table -- and cubeStep, which crosses a seam applying both the coordinate remap and a heading's frame transform. Also added Data.Grid.Atlas.atlasFromVector (checked smart constructor for an atlas that isn't a subdivision of one bigger grid) since cubeAtlas needed a way to build an Atlas from 6 explicit charts.

Table derived from each face's (u,v) basis (u x v = outward normal, consistent across all 6 faces), not guessed from a drawn net. That surfaced a real correction to the issue's own framing: some of the 24 seams are genuinely orientation-reversing in raw (u,v) coordinates (a reflection, not just a rotation) -- still always one of sized-grid-1bm's 8 D4 elements, just not only the 4-rotation subset the issue anticipated.

Verified two ways, both landed as regression tests (Test.CubeMap): cubeSeamPairsUp (all 24 half-edges pair with the one that names them back) and cubeStepBeltCloses (a walker following a fixed heading around any of the cube's 3 equatorial belts returns to its exact start after 4n steps, checked exhaustively over 600 starting configurations on n=5). The belt-closure check earned its keep during development: the first version of the heading sign formula passed the pairing check and looked right by hand-tracing one seam, but was wrong (double-applied the crossing direction's sign) and only the belt-closure property caught it.

Also merged worktree-sized-grid-fh2 into master first (it was closed but had never actually been merged) since this built directly on grid-atlas v1.

Builds, 100% haddock coverage on grid-atlas, hlint clean, all 481 grid-sized + 4 grid-atlas tests pass. Pushed to origin/master at 4f08e2d.

This is also sized-grid-ts4's second data point (two concrete atlases now exist: the degenerate/tiled one and this). Left a comment there; not resolving ts4 itself here.

title: Establish a property-test baseline that would have caught the confirmed bugs
description:
The existing suite passes 62 tests while three genuine bugs sit in the library. The
laws being tested are too weak.

Gaps found:
  - tests/Test/Utils.hs:98-110 affineSpaceLaws tests only 'a .+^ zeroV == a' and
    'a .-. a == zeroV'. Both hold under HardWrap's clamping. Add the round-trip law
    'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' -- it fails on HardWrap today.
  - aesonLaws (tests/Test/Utils.hs:41-48) only round-trips valid values. Add negative
    cases: decoding a too-short / too-long array must be Nothing.
  - No test asserts the core invariant 'V.length (unGrid g) == MaxCoordSize cs'.
    Make it a property over every Grid-producing operation: tabulate, gridFromList,
    takeGrid, dropGrid, splitHigherDim, combineHigherDim, shrinkGrid, mapLowerDim,
    fmap, <*>, and FromJSON. takeGrid and splitHigherDim fail it today.
  - No Comonad law tests for FocusedGrid (extract . duplicate == id, etc.).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid has exactly one example-based test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) and no
    properties.

Also: tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
which builds the entire domain for each sample -- fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.

Write these BEFORE fixing the bugs, so each fix has a failing test to turn green.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:

New: tests/Test/Invariant.hs (size invariant + negative JSON + take/split), and the round-trip law 'b .+^ (a .-. b) === a' added to affineSpaceLaws in tests/Test/Utils.hs.

Failing, each mapping to a filed defect:

  - Coord [HardWrap 10, Periodic 20]: same    -> sized-grid-0kf

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:

title: No test checks that coord operations produce in-range values
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while adding the asOrdinal Iso laws (sized-grid-6p4).

The new 'asOrdinal lands in [0, n)' property quantifies over 'arbitrary', and
Test.Arbitrary's genOrdinal draws through unsafeOrdinal at an already-reduced
index. So every coord the property sees is in range BEFORE asOrdinal is applied:
it cannot catch a coord that an operation built out of range.

The operations that build coords with unsafeOrdinal, each of which is asserting
its own precondition rather than checking it:

  Clamped  Semigroup   unsafeOrdinal (min (ordinalSize @n - 1) (a + b))
  Clamped  .+^         unsafeOrdinal (fromInteger (max 0 (min (size-1) (a + b))))
  Periodic Semigroup   unsafeOrdinal ((a + b) `mod` ordinalSize @n)
  Periodic toEnum      unsafeOrdinal (x `mod` ordinalSize @n)

unsafeOrdinal does check, with Control.Exception.assert -- but cabal builds the
test suite at -O1, where GHC compiles assertions away. So in the suite as it
runs today that check is not live, and a wrong mod or a wrong clamp would
produce an Ordinal outside [0, n) that nothing rejects. It would then index a
vector out of bounds, or silently read the wrong cell.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, not exclusive:
  1. Add 'ghc-options: -fno-ignore-asserts' to the tests component, which makes
     every existing property that exercises these operations into a range check
     for free. Cheapest by far.
  2. State it directly as a property: for arbitrary a, b, the results of (<>),
     (.+^) and toEnum all satisfy 0 <= ordinalToInt < ordinalSize.

Option 1 is the one with leverage -- the suite already generates a great deal of
Semigroup and AffineSpace traffic, and none of it is currently range-checked.
notes:
2026-08-19, sized-grid-adr.14 (537bca4). Option 1's premise is gone, in a good way. unsafeOrdinal's precondition is no longer an assert -- it is an ordinary guard in the source -- so the check is live in every component at every optimisation level, with no flag involved and no way for one to strip it. The specific hazard in this description ('cabal builds the test suite at -O1, where GHC compiles assertions away') can no longer happen, and it is faster than the assert was rather than slower.

So every property in the suite that exercises Clamped's Semigroup, Clamped's .+^, Periodic's Semigroup and Periodic's toEnum is now a range check for free, which is the leverage option 1 was after.

Kept open for option 2, which is still not done and is not the same thing. The guard proves the result of unsafeOrdinal is in [0, n) by failing loudly if it is not; it does not state, as a property anyone can read, that these four operations are total over arbitrary inputs. A test that says so directly also survives someone later reaching for the unchecked constructor. Option 2 is the whole of what is left here.

title: coordPosition still costs 320 bytes per call after specialisation
description:
Follow-up from sized-grid-0vl, which took coordPosition from 608 to 320 bytes per call by exposing its unfolding with INLINABLE so consumers specialise at a concrete cs.

320 bytes for what should be a couple of multiplies and adds is still 40 words, so something in the path is not melting away even when the All dictionary is statically known.

The measurement to work against is 'extract 50x50' in the benchmark suite: it is a single coordPosition call and nothing else, so its Allocated column IS the per-call cost, with no traversal or list machinery mixed in. It reads 320 bytes at the commit that closed sized-grid-0vl (was 608).

  cabal run bench:benchmarks -- -p '$0 ~ /extract 50x50/'

Options 3 and 4 from sized-grid-0vl are still on the table and were never tried,
because option 1 alone cleared that issue's acceptance criterion:

  3. Get ordinalSize off Integer. It is 'fromInteger $ natVal (Proxy @m)', and
     GHC.TypeNats.natVal returns a Natural, so naturalToWord avoids the Integer
     box. At a concrete size this should constant-fold anyway, which is a reason
     to check whether it is really what is left before changing it.
  4. Add a direct Int-level method to IsCoord so the per-axis read does not go
     through the asOrdinal Iso. Changes the class, so weigh it last.

Worth doing first: dump Core for a concrete two-axis call and find out what the
40 words actually are, rather than guessing. 'cabal build' will not re-dump on a
ghc-options change alone -- the module has to actually change for the dump to
regenerate.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (Core, not guesswork). coordPosition's fold was a where-helper, which makes it polymorphically recursive over the axis list: it calls itself at a shorter list. GHC specialises the outermost call and STOPS, leaving one shared worker $whelper that takes the All IsCoordLifted dictionary at run time. So the INLINABLE from sized-grid-0vl did work -- for axis one only, which constant-folded. Every axis after it paid, per axis: two thunks to peel the dictionary ($p1All, $p0CTuple2), integerFromNatural for ordinalSize, asOrdinal applied through $fProfunctorFUN/$fFunctorConst, and two boxed I#. That is the 40 words. The comment then at Coord.hs:324 named those exact costs but concluded INLINABLE removed them.

MEASURED OPTIONS (2-axis, coord-construction baseline subtracted; the 328 B here cross-validates the benchmark's 320 B):
  current                                    328 B
  option 3 alone (ordinalSize off Integer)   336 B  -- NO WIN, ruled out
  options 3+4 (+ direct Int read)            216 B  -- 34% off, option 4 does all the work
  class-based induction                       32 B  -- 90% off
  -fpolymorphic-specialisation -fspecialise-aggressively  328 B -- worker byte-for-byte identical

Also ruled out with Core: lifting the helper to a top-level INLINABLE function (identical), and routing the fold through generics-sop's cpara_SList (its cons is a function ARGUMENT, so the per-axis dictionary stays a run-time value). Only an instance method resolves it.

FIX SHIPPED: new class IsCoordList cs in SizedGrid.Coord.Class carrying the fold as method sizeAndPosition, with All IsCoordLifted cs as a superclass and a IsCoordListF type-family superclass so that IsCoordList (x ': xs) hands back IsCoordList xs (the shape generics-sop gives its own All, needed or every local induction over the axis list stops typechecking). Replaced All IsCoordLifted with IsCoordList throughout: a rename, not an added obligation.

RESULT: coordPosition at '[Clamped 50, Clamped 50] compiles to +# (*# x 50#) y, zero allocation.
  extract 50x50   320 B -> 0 B,     92.6 ns -> 11.0 ns
  index x90000     27 MB -> 38 B,   8.05 ms -> 753 us
  ifoldl' 300x300  30 MB -> 2.7 MB, 8.24 ms -> 1.03 ms
  imap 300x300     35 MB -> 7.6 MB, 15.1 ms -> 4.86 ms
  tabulate 300x300 47 MB -> 20 MB,  24.6 ms -> 14.1 ms
  extend neighbourSum 32 MB -> 26 MB
  Nothing regressed; pure/fmap/itraverse/collapseGrid/coord arithmetic all unchanged.

CONSUMER IMPACT: none. ../aoc works at '[Clamped n, Clamped n] with (KnownNat n, 1 <= n), and IsCoordList is discharged there by instance resolution exactly as All IsCoordLifted was; verified by typechecking aoc's verbatim signatures against the new API. (A full ../aoc build is blocked by a pre-existing unrelated failure: hmatrix needs blas/lapack C libs.)

FOLLOW-UP: sized-grid-92z, coordSpaceSize has the identical defect via sList induction.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the closing notes above, found while answering "is there a general fix to sList induction?".

The notes say cpara_SList does not unroll "because its cons is a function ARGUMENT, so the per-axis dictionary stays a run-time value". That explanation is WRONG. An eliminator whose step is a function argument unrolls fine; a clone of cpara_SList, and generics-sop's own, both constant-fold a coordSpaceSize-shaped fold to a literal (I# 7000#) at a concrete three-axis list.

What actually separated the two cases in the original experiment was INLINE vs INLINABLE on the WRAPPER. The failing test marked the wrapper INLINABLE, so GHC specialised it rather than inlining it, and specialisation lambda-lifts the higher-rank step into a shared worker that keeps the per-axis dictionary at run time. Flip that one pragma to INLINE and the identical code unrolls. Verified both directions, one variable at a time.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and is the real reason the class was the right fix:

1. The old where-helper was SELF-RECURSIVE, and that can never unroll -- GHC does not inline a self-recursive binding. Verified: the original body with INLINE instead of INLINABLE still leaves 'Rec { $whelper ... }' with the runtime dictionary. So the defect was real and no pragma could have fixed it.

2. cpara_SList + INLINE unrolls in isolation but is a REGRESSION in this library, measured on the real benchmarks:

     extract 50x50   320 B before -> 0 B (class) -> 584 B (cpara+INLINE)
     index x90000     27 MB before -> 34 B (class) -> 50 MB (cpara+INLINE)

   Because coordPosition is called from polymorphic instance methods (index on Representable, gridIndex on IsGrid), INLINE splices the eliminator into a body where cs is still a type variable and nothing can resolve, so it builds the closure chain per call. Unrolling through an eliminator needs INLINE all the way down to a concrete call site, and this library's call path does not provide one.

3. A class method has no such dependency on the inliner: the instance chain resolves whenever the DICTIONARY is known, which happens at specialisation, not only at inlining.

Source Haddock and ChangeLog have been corrected to say this. Consequence for sized-grid-92z: do NOT rewrite coordSpaceSize through cpara_SList; add a method to IsCoordList as that issue already proposes.

title: asOrdinal is IsCoord's only required method and its Iso laws are untested
description:
Found 2026-08-12 while working out whether Test.Utils.isCoordLaws should be rewritten as properties (see sized-grid-05b).

IsCoord has exactly one required method, and its haddock states the obligation outright:

    -- | As each coord represents a finite number of states, it must be
    --   isomorphic to an Ordinal
    class IsCoord (c :: Nat -> Type) where
      asOrdinal :: Iso' (c n) (Ordinal n)
      (src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:50-53)

Everything else in the class is derivable from it. So 'asOrdinal is an isomorphism' is the load-bearing law of the whole coordinate abstraction -- and nothing checks it.

WHAT COVERAGE ACTUALLY EXISTS. Across the entire suite 'asOrdinal' appears three times:

    tests/Test/Utils.hs:361   view asOrdinal (zeroPosition @c @n)   -- one fixed value
    tests/Test/Utils.hs:368   view (asOrdinal @c) (maxCoord :: c n) -- one fixed value
    tests/Test/Ordinal.hs:114 view (re asOrdinal) (toEnum 3)        -- one fixed value

Three ground facts about three distinguished values. The round trip is never exercised at an arbitrary coord in either direction.

THE MISSING LAWS, which are the standard Iso laws:

    view asOrdinal . review asOrdinal == id     -- on Ordinal n
    review asOrdinal . view asOrdinal == id     -- on c n

for arbitrary values, over Periodic, Clamped and Ordinal. An 'Iso' that is not one is precisely the failure that produces silently wrong reads rather than errors: every index, tabulate and neighbour calculation goes through this conversion, so a coord type whose two directions disagree corrupts results everywhere without ever throwing.

Worth stating alongside them, since they are the same obligation seen from other angles:

    ordinalToNum (view asOrdinal c) is in [0, CoordNat c)     -- the range half
    reifyCoord c (\m -> natVal (Proxy @m)) == ordinalToNum (view asOrdinal c)

The second is partially covered already -- Test.Ordinal checks it at every value of an Ordinal 5 and at one Periodic 5 -- but it is written as examples rather than as a law over arbitrary coords.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: isCoordLaws is an HUnit testCase asserting facts about zeroPosition and maxCoord. Those are single values, so there was nothing to quantify over and the shape of the test never invited the question 'what varies here'. Rewriting it as properties is what surfaced the gap.
close_reason:
Added the missing quantified laws.

Test.Utils gains 'isoLaws', a generic bundle for any AnIso' -- both round trips,
labelled from the iso's name. isCoordLaws is now a testGroup: the three original
HUnit assertions (kept, as 'distinguished values' -- zeroPosition and maxCoord
are single values with nothing to quantify over) plus isoLaws on asOrdinal, the
range property, and reifyCoord-agrees-with-asOrdinal quantified over the coord.

Main.hs gains 'Ordinal 10' as an isCoordLaws call site -- it had none, and it is
the instance that overrides asOrdinal, zeroPosition, maxCoord and reifyCoord all
at once. isoLaws also picks up _WrappedCoord, the library's other exported Iso'.

315 -> 330 tests; downstream and readme suites still pass; no new warnings.

WHAT THE MUTATION TESTING ESTABLISHED, which is the part worth carrying forward:
only two of these four properties can actually fail.

  review asOrdinal . view asOrdinal == id   HAS TEETH. A non-injective instance
                                            (extra field dropped on the way out,
                                            invented on the way back) falsifies
                                            it within a handful of cases.
  reifyCoord agrees with asOrdinal          HAS TEETH. Verified with an
                                            off-by-one reifyCoord override; also
                                            caught by 'distinguished values'.
  view asOrdinal . review asOrdinal == id   CANNOT FAIL.
  asOrdinal lands in [0, n)                 CANNOT FAIL.

The last two are unfalsifiable because asOrdinal carries no KnownNat n, so an
instance cannot build an Ordinal n at all -- unsafeOrdinal and numToOrdinal both
need the size -- and the only ordinal it can return is the one it was handed.
They are the law written down, not tests, and they become real only if asOrdinal
ever gains that constraint. Recorded in memory so nobody adds more round-trip
properties expecting them to catch something.

DISCOVERED: sized-grid-6os. The range property quantifies over 'arbitrary',
which draws in-range by construction, so a coord built out of range by an
OPERATION is not reached -- and unsafeOrdinal's assert does not catch it either,
because cabal builds the suite at -O1 where assertions are compiled away.

title: Enum and Bounded for Coord cs: the bijection already exists, only the standard names are missing
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey.

coordPosition (Coord.hs:288) and coordFromPosition (Coord.hs:297) are already
a bijection between Coord cs and [0, MaxCoordSize cs), and MaxCoordSize is
already a type family (Coord.hs:283). toEnum/fromEnum is that bijection under
the names the rest of the ecosystem uses.

  instance IsCoordList cs => Enum (Coord cs) where
    fromEnum = coordPosition
    toEnum p = case coordFromPosition p of
                 Just c  -> c
                 Nothing -> error "..."

coordFromPosition returns Maybe, so toEnum has to fail on out-of-range input.
Copy the error text style from Ordinal's toEnum (Ordinal.hs:120), which
already reports the offending value and the bound.

Override enumFrom / enumFromThen / enumFromTo / enumFromThenTo the way
Ordinal.hs:127-134 does. The default enumFrom counts up in Int past the last
coordinate and then calls the error above -- the same trap Ordinal already
sidestepped, and the same one Periodic fell into (see the enumFrom bug
issue). Do not leave them to the defaults.

  instance (All Bounded cs, ...) => Bounded (Coord cs) where
    minBound = Coord (hcpure (Proxy @Bounded) (pure minBound))
    maxBound = Coord (hcpure (Proxy @Bounded) (pure maxBound))

This needs Bounded on every axis, so it is blocked on Bounded (Periodic n):
without it, no Coord containing a periodic axis -- which is most of the
interesting ones -- can be Bounded.

== The property that makes this coherent, and that the test should pin

Ord (Coord cs) (Coord.hs:129) is lexicographic with the FIRST axis most
significant, and coordPosition is row-major with the first axis most
significant. So

  compare a b  ==  compare (fromEnum a) (fromEnum b)

and [minBound .. maxBound] == allCoord, in that order. Neither is forced by
the Enum class, both are true here, and both are things a consumer will
assume. Write them as properties, not as Haddock claims.
close_reason: Implemented finite Enum and axis-derived Bounded instances for Coord, with ordering and enumeration properties.

title: _CoordTuple and _DeltaTuple: coordFromTuple/coordToTuple are a genuine Iso
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier A: a genuine Iso.

  coordFromTuple :: (IsProductType t xs, IsCoordList xs) => t -> Coord xs      Coord.hs:345
  coordToTuple   :: (IsProductType t xs, IsCoordList xs) => Coord xs -> t      Coord.hs:348
  deltaFromTuple :: IsProductType t ds => t -> Delta ds                        Delta.hs:206
  deltaToTuple   :: IsProductType t ds => Delta ds -> t                        Delta.hs:209

Both directions are total and mutually inverse -- `IsProductType t xs` is
generics-sop's statement that `t` IS an `NP I xs` up to isomorphism, so there
is nothing partial anywhere in either pair. That makes these Isos and not
Prisms, unlike most of the other from/to pairs in this survey.

  _CoordTuple :: (IsProductType t xs, IsCoordList xs) => Iso' (Coord xs) t
  _CoordTuple = iso coordToTuple coordFromTuple

  _DeltaTuple :: IsProductType t ds => Iso' (Delta ds) t
  _DeltaTuple = iso deltaToTuple deltaFromTuple

What it buys beyond the two functions: composition. `c ^. _CoordTuple . _1`,
`over (_CoordTuple :: Iso' (Coord '[X 3, Y 3]) (Ordinal 3, Ordinal 3)) swap`,
and -- the real one -- using it as the pivot in a longer chain rather than
having to name an intermediate.

Note the annotation burden is real and is not the optic's fault: `t` is only
determined by the call site in either form, so a bare `_CoordTuple` is as
ambiguous as a bare `coordToTuple`. Keep both functions exported; the Iso is
an addition, not a replacement.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency (grid-sized.cabal:244).

title: SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is dead code containing an unsound axiom
description:
src/SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs is imported by nothing. Verified:

    grep -rn 'SizedGrid.Internal' src tests sudoko/src gameOfLife/src ising-example/src
    -> only its own module header and module declaration

It is also absent from both 'exposed-modules' and 'other-modules' in sized-grid.cabal,
so cabal does not know about it at all (it would be omitted from an sdist).

Its contents are worth deleting rather than wiring up:

  - takeAddIsId (line 52-53):
        takeAddIsId :: forall m . Dict (((m - 1) + 1) ~ m)
        takeAddIsId = unsafeCoerce (Dict :: Dict (a ~ a))
    This is false at m = 0. It is an unsound axiom obtained by unsafeCoerce, and if
    anything ever imported it, it could be used to derive nonsense.

  - sLessThan (line 41-49) fabricates an SBool (n <=? m) via unsafeCoerce off a
    runtime Integer comparison. Sound in practice but the comment on 'magic'
    (line 55, 58) literally says 'don't really understand it' / 'Also don't understand'.

  - SBool/SBoolI duplicate what singletons or Data.Type.Bool already provide.

ghc-typelits-natnormalise supplies it soundly (see the plugin issue).

else is missing.

title: ../aoc 2018/06 manhattan silently returns 0 after the HardWrap (.-.) fix
description:
BREAKING CONSUMER CHANGE, confirmed empirically against the fixed library.

sized-grid-0kf removed the 'max 0' clamp from HardWrap's (.-.) so it returns a true
signed displacement. ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:22-26 was relying on that clamp to compute
an absolute value:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum [dx1, dx2, dy1, dy2]
      where
        (dx1, dy1) = c1 .-. c2
        (dx2, dy2) = c2 .-. c1

OLD: dx1 = max 0 (x1-x2), dx2 = max 0 (x2-x1), so dx1 + dx2 = |x1-x2|. Correct.
NEW: dx1 = x1-x2, dx2 = x2-x1, so dx1 + dx2 = 0. Always.

Probe output against the fixed library (HardWrap 400 x HardWrap 400):
    (1,1) -> (8,3) = 0
    (8,3) -> (1,1) = 0
    (5,5) -> (5,5) = 0
    (3,4) -> (8,9) = 0

Every distance is 0, so 2018/06 produces a wrong answer rather than failing loudly.

FIX (in ../aoc, one line):

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

This is a defect in the consumer, not a reason to revert sized-grid-0kf: the old
behaviour violated the AffineSpace round-trip law and the clamp-as-abs trick only
worked by accident. But ../aoc must be patched in the same change set, or its 2018/06
answer regresses silently.

Also re-check the moorePoints call sites, which the 0kf fix was expected to IMPROVE:
  - ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 'filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1'
  - ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:51 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:67 (both commented out)
The nubOrd workarounds may now be removable; verify before deleting them.
close_reason: Fixed ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs manhattan to take abs of a single signed diff; verified against the day's own (17,90) doctest via a scratch replica run in cabal repl, since ../aoc cannot build here (hmatrix/blas). moorePoints follow-up recorded on sized-grid-7gs: nubOrd workarounds must stay.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED in ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs. manhattan is now:

    manhattan c1 c2 = fromIntegral $ sum $ map abs [dx, dy]
      where (dx, dy) = c1 .-. c2

hmatrix-0.20.2 fails to configure, 'Missing (or bad) C libraries: blas, lapack', and

    expected      : (17,90)   <- the doctest at ../aoc/src/2018/06.hs:42-43
    new manhattan : (17,90)   PASS
    old manhattan : *** Exception: Data.Foldable.maximum (for Data.IntMap): empty map

answer, it CRASHED. With every distance 0 the first target wins on 0 < maxBound and

title: HardWrap does not wrap, it clamps; the name has caused two bugs already
description:
'HardWrap n' clamps out-of-range values to the nearest edge. It does not wrap. 'Periodic n' is the one that wraps. The name says the opposite of what the type does, and it has been read the wrong way twice:

  sized-grid-0kf (P0)  HardWrap's (.-.) clamped negative differences to 0, breaking
                       the AffineSpace law b .+^ (a .-. b) == a for every a < b.
  sized-grid-7bp (P0)  ../aoc 2018/06 manhattan silently returned 0 as a result.

The README compounds it (README.md, coordinate-types section) by describing HardWrap
as 'like Ordinal ... but it allows a more permissive API by clamping', which is
accurate prose under an inaccurate name.

The clamping itself is not the bug and should stay: (.+^) has to be total to satisfy
AffineSpace, so clamping is its honest total approximation. sized-grid-7gs adds the
checked counterpart (offsetIsCoord, returning Nothing at the edge). What is left over
after 7gs is purely the name.

CANDIDATES
  Clamped      says exactly what (.+^) does
  Bounded      clashes with the Prelude class of that name; it also has a Bounded instance
  Clipped      fine, slightly graphics-flavoured
  Saturating   accurate and standard for arithmetic, a touch jargon-heavy

'Clamped' is the recommendation: it names the operation, has no Prelude clash, and
reads correctly at every use site ('Coord \'[Clamped 5, Clamped 5]').

Best done as part of sized-grid-85n, since that pass is already rewriting the README's
coordinate-types tutorial and is the moment breaking renames are cheapest. Filed
separately because it is a distinct decision and could be taken on its own.
acceptance_criteria: The clamping coord type has a name that describes clamping; no occurrence of 'HardWrap' remains in src, tests, examples, README or ../aoc; the suite passes.
close_reason: HardWrap renamed to Clamped throughout sized-grid (merged to master, 53b86cd) and ../aoc (7 files, 24 occurrences, uncommitted per user). Zero occurrences remain in src, tests, examples, README or ../aoc. sized-grid: library, 3 examples and benchmark build clean under -Wall; both test suites pass (172 tests + readme). aoc: 5 of 7 affected modules type-check clean; the other 2 fail on PRE-EXISTING breakages unrelated to this rename (sealed Grid constructor -> sized-grid-bb5, removed moorePoints -> sized-grid-niq), proven by checking session-start master where moorePoints survived only in a comment and Grid was already exported abstractly. ChangeLog and the dated docs/ design spec keep the old name where they are historical records.

title: Missing API: safe neighbour offset. Users emulate it with strengthenCoord/weakenCoord through a larger grid
description:
The most-wanted operation on a bounded grid is 'move by a delta, or fail if that leaves
the grid'. The library has no such function, so users build it out of parts.

../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:63-80 -- to walk three steps in a direction on an n x n grid the
user has to widen the coordinate type to n+1, offset there, then narrow back:

    i, j, k :: Coord '[Periodic (n + 1), Periodic (n + 1)]
    i = strengthenCoord c .+^ d
    j = i .+^ d
    k = j .+^ d
    ... mapMaybe (traverse weakenCoord) ...
        \\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1) \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

That is a lot of machinery to express 'neighbour, or Nothing'. It also only works
because Periodic's wrap-around at n+1 happens not to collide for small deltas -- it is
not actually a bounds check.

../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:64-66 and ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:78-80 give up on the library
entirely and hand-roll:

    neighborsOf = [ toEnum nr :| toEnum nc :| EmptyCoord | ... ]

../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 uses moorePoints but must repair the result:

    experiment (filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1) g

Proposed API:

    -- fails instead of clamping or wrapping
    offsetCoord  :: Coord cs -> Diff (Coord cs) -> Maybe (Coord cs)
    neighbours   :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- Moore, excludes centre, no duplicates
    neighbours4  :: Coord cs -> [Coord cs]   -- von Neumann, excludes centre

with the boundary behaviour driven by the coord type rather than by clamping:
Periodic wraps (total), and a new 'Bounded'/'Clipped' coord returns Nothing at the
edge. Note moorePoints/vonNeumanPoints currently INCLUDE the centre, which every
observed caller then filters out -- the default is wrong.

Blocked on the HardWrap AffineSpace fix, since that is what makes the current
neighbour story incorrect.
close_reason: Done on branch worktree-neighbour-offset-7gs. offsetIsCoord (IsCoord method, bounds-check default, Periodic wraps), offsetCoord, mooreNeighbours, vonNeumannNeighbours, neighbours. moorePoints/vonNeumanPoints deleted; all five in-repo consumers migrated. Constraints drop from eight to All IsCoordLifted, and Ordinal axes now work. Clean build zero warnings, 172 tests plus README suite pass. See the issue comment for the design decisions that differ from this issue as filed.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Empirical check of the moorePoints half of sized-grid-7bp: the nubOrd workarounds at
../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 (and the commented-out ones in 2015/18 and 2018/18) must STAY.
The 0kf fix did not help them.

0kf only desugared (.-.); HardWrap's (.+^) still clamps
(src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:62-65), and moorePoints is built out of (.+^)
(src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:250-257), so every off-grid offset folds back onto the edge
cell. Measured on HardWrap 5 x HardWrap 5:

    moorePoints 1 (0,0) -> 9 results, 4 distinct   <- 5 duplicates
    moorePoints 1 (2,2) -> 9 results, 9 distinct

This is the concrete argument for the 'no duplicates' clause in the proposed
'neighbours' API above: dedup cannot be the caller's job when the clamp is what
created the duplicates.

Note vonNeumanPoints (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:275-284) was silently repaired by 0kf:
its 'min (new .-. c) (c .-. new)' picked the componentwise minimum of the two signed
diffs, which under the old clamp was 0 for every pair, so the radius filter passed
everything. It now yields -|d| and the abs makes the filter real. It still inherits the
duplicate cells from moorePoints.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
DONE on branch worktree-neighbour-offset-7gs. Design recorded in
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-safe-neighbour-offset-design.md.

WHAT LANDED
  offsetIsCoord  -- new IsCoord method. Default is the bounds check; Periodic
                    overrides it to wrap and is total. (.+^) is untouched:
                    AffineSpace needs it total, and clamping is its honest
                    total form.
  offsetCoord    -- the same over a whole Coord, taking the same Diff as (.+^)
                    so it is a drop-in. Policy is read per axis.
  mooreNeighbours / vonNeumannNeighbours / neighbours (= mooreNeighbours 1)
  moorePoints and vonNeumanPoints DELETED, not deprecated.

DESIGN DECISIONS THAT DIFFER FROM THIS ISSUE AS FILED
1. No new 'Bounded'/'Clipped' coord type. HardWrap already denotes a bounded
   space; a fourth type for the same space with a different offset policy would
   be redundant. What HardWrap actually needs is a name that says 'clamps' --
   filed separately as sized-grid-7d1.
2. No 'neighbours4'. Von Neumann radius 1 is four cells in 2D but six in 3D, so
   the count is a fact about the dimension, not the operation. It is
   vonNeumannNeighbours 1.
3. Deleted rather than deprecated. The replacements change behaviour under an
   otherwise compatible signature, so the names had to go for the change to be
   a compile error instead of a silent one. Kevin confirmed breaking the API is
   fine, and raised claiming the fork as a distinct project (sized-grid-85n).

THE IMPLEMENTATION TRICK
Neighbourhoods are generated per axis, not by offsetting whole coordinates.
Each axis enumerates the values reachable within r steps and keeps each value
once, at its true step count. Consequences:
  - a cartesian product of per-axis-distinct sets is distinct, so NO duplicates
    without a nubOrd and without Ord (Coord cs);
  - the centre is the only entry whose total distance is zero, so excluding it
    needs no Eq (Coord cs);
  - on a torus the kept step count is the WRAPPED distance, which is what makes
    vonNeumannNeighbours correct on a small torus rather than accidentally
    right;
  - constraints drop from vonNeumanPoints' EIGHT to All IsCoordLifted alone,
    and they now work on Ordinal axes, which moorePoints never could (Ordinal
    has no AffineSpace instance, so All AffineSpace cs was unsatisfiable).

VERIFIED
  Clean build: library + sudoko + gameOfLife + ising-example, ZERO warnings.
  172 tests pass (up from 129) plus the README suite. sudoko still runs.
  Test-suite warnings 14 -> 6, all pre-existing; no new ones.
  Regression pinned: neighbours at a HardWrap 5 corner is exactly 3 distinct,
  where moorePoints 1 gave 9 with 4 distinct.

ALL FIVE in-repo consumers migrated, and every one had been hand-filtering the
centre back out: README tutorial, bench/Main.hs, gameOfLife, ising-example.
The benchmark now reads 8 cells not 9, so its recorded numbers move.

NOT DONE, deliberately: ../aoc migration belongs to sized-grid-bb5. Note
2024/04 must also change its grid from Periodic to the clamping coord type --
it is not a torus, it used Periodic only to make the n+1 trick work.

title: Periodic's Needle: shortest signed route, or non-negative residue?
description:
Surfaced by sized-grid-8nz. A real design question independent of whether we
take the manifolds-core dependency, because it is about what a displacement on
a cyclic axis means.

Periodic's AffineSpace instance (src/Data/Grid/Sized/Coord/Periodic.hs:86):

    Periodic a .-. Periodic b = (ordinalToInt a - ordinalToInt b) `mod` ordinalSize @n

always non-negative, in [0, n). On a 7-cycle, 6 .-. 0 is 6, never -1.

But axisDistanceIsCoord on the same type already takes the shorter way round,
and its Haddock argues for it: "on a 3-cycle every other cell really is one
step away".

manifolds-core's S1 -- the continuous type Periodic is the discrete image of --
resolves it the other way:

    S1Polar phi1 .-~. S1Polar phi0
      | dphi >  pi  = pure (dphi - tau)
      | dphi < -pi  = pure (dphi + tau)
      | otherwise   = pure dphi

i.e. shortest signed route, and its Needle doc is explicit about why: a needle
is "like a compass needle, but also with an actual length". A needle of length
6 where one of length -1 would do is the wrong needle.

Both satisfy p .+^ (q .-. p) == q, so no law distinguishes them and nothing is
currently broken. The question is which one the library should mean, given it
already has both notions in the same type.

Three ways out:
  a) leave .-. alone; if PseudoAffine is adopted, give it the shortest signed
     route so Needle /= Diff for Periodic. Costs a divergence between two
     operations that look like they should agree.
  b) change .-. to the shortest signed route, making it agree with
     axisDistanceIsCoord. A behaviour change to a public instance; needs a
     survey of ../aoc call sites first (see the sized-grid <-> aoc note).
  c) leave both, document the split deliberately: .-. is the canonical
     representative, axisDistanceIsCoord is the metric.

Blocked on nothing; worth deciding before sized-grid-8nz picks an
implementation, since option (a) only exists if 8nz goes ahead.
close_reason: Decided on option (c): keep (.-.) as the canonical non-negative residue and document axisDistanceIsCoord as the shortest-route metric. Added regression tests.

title: Grid is a leaky abstraction: constructor and unGrid are exported, no smart constructor
description:
src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:40-42

    newtype Grid (cs :: [Type]) a = Grid { unGrid :: V.Vector a }
      deriving (Eq, Show, Functor, Foldable, Traversable, Eq1, Show1, GHC.Generic)

Both Grid and unGrid are exported (the module has no export list at all -- every
module in the library uses an implicit 'module M where'). Anyone can build a Grid
whose vector length disagrees with MaxCoordSize cs, which is the one invariant the
library exists to enforce. The FromJSON bug and the takeGrid bug are both instances
of this.

Evidence users reach through it: ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs:31
    prefixSum1D = Grid . V.scanl1' (+) . unGrid
That is a legitimate need (prefix sums along an axis) with no API for it, so the
user bypasses the abstraction. Length-preserving uses like this are fine -- the
point is the type does not distinguish them from unsound ones.

Proposal:
  - Give every module an explicit export list.
  - Export the Grid type but not the constructor from SizedGrid.Grid.Grid.
  - Add SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe exposing UnsafeGrid/unGrid for the escape hatch,
    documented as 'you must preserve length'.
  - Add a safe 'gridFromVector :: ... => V.Vector a -> Maybe (Grid cs a)'.
  - Add the length-preserving combinators people actually want, so the escape hatch
    is rarely needed: mapAxis / scanAxis / prefix sums along a dimension
    (covers the ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs summed-area-table use directly).

Explicit export lists also let -Wmissing-export-lists be turned on, which ../aoc
already enables for its own code.
close_reason:
Grid is now abstract. Constructor and unGrid field are unexported; SizedGrid.Internal.Grid (hidden) holds the representation so SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe can be the only public route to it, and it is not re-exported by the SizedGrid umbrella.

Delivered: explicit export lists on every module, -Wmissing-export-lists on, gridVector (safe read), gridFromVector (checked build), unsafeGridFromVector (asserted build, own module), scanl1Grid (length-preserving scan).

Verified against the compiler, not by inspection: 'Grid v' -> illegal term-level use of the type constructor; 'unGrid' -> not in scope; 'g { unGrid = ... }' -> record field not in scope; unsafeGridFromVector via the umbrella import -> not in scope; via SizedGrid.Grid.Unsafe -> compiles with only -XDataKinds. Public API diff (:browse SizedGrid, before vs after) is exactly +gridFromVector +gridVector +scanl1Grid and Grid becoming abstract -- nothing dropped by accident. 89 tests pass (9 new), README suite passes, library builds warning-clean.

Design change from the proposal: the escape hatch is a function, not the 'UnsafeGrid' pattern synonym. A bidirectional synonym drags the safe direction (reading) through the unsafe import, and naming a pattern synonym in an import list requires the importing module to enable PatternSynonyms.

NOT delivered, split out to sized-grid-tw3: the mapAxis/scanAxis axis-selector bullet. scanl1Grid + mapLowerDim covers the ../aoc/src/2018/11.hs case that motivated it; a general type-level axis selector is unjustified by one 2D call site. aoc migration tracked as sized-grid-bb5.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick

title: Claim the fork: rename the package, re-own the metadata, state the design thesis
description:
The fork has diverged past any possible upstream merge, and the name it carries belongs to someone else.

FACTS
  - upstream github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid: last commit 2019-09-13
  - this fork (origin = github.com/beefyhalo/sized-grid): first Kevin commit 2025-05-09
  - 'sized-grid' on Hackage is edwardwas', maintainer ed@wastell.co.uk. This fork
    can never be released under that name.
  - divergence is not mergeable upstream anyway: GHC 9.10+ minimum,
    RequiredTypeArguments, sealed Grid constructor, Ordinal as a newtype over Int,
    gridWindows renamed to gridTiles, GHC2024.

STALE METADATA still pointing at upstream:
  sized-grid.cabal  maintainer: ed@wastell.co.uk
                    author: edwardwas
                    homepage: github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid
                    bug-reports: github.com/edwardwas/sized-grid/issues
  README.md         dead travis-ci.org/edwardwas badge (line 1)
                    Hackage badge resolving to upstream's version
                    tutorial predates the sealed Grid and RequiredTypeArguments;
                    still describes HardWrap as if the name were accurate

WORK
  1. Pick a package name.
  2. Rewrite cabal metadata to Kevin as maintainer/author, this repo as homepage
     and bug-reports. Reset version (0.1.0.0 under the new name).
  3. Decide whether the module prefix stays SizedGrid.* or follows the new name.
     Keeping it is defensible and much cheaper; renaming touches every module.
  4. README: drop both dead badges, rewrite the tutorial against the current API.
  5. Write down the design thesis, because that is what makes later API changes
     principled rather than merely permitted:
       'The coordinate type is the boundary policy. Any operation that can leave
        the space is either total because the type says how to come back, or it
        returns Maybe. Nothing clamps silently.'
     That thesis is what decides sized-grid-7gs and it is what condemns the name
     HardWrap.

Deliberately NOT blocking sized-grid-7gs: the neighbour API is designed against the
thesis either way, and 7gs should land whatever happens to the name.
acceptance_criteria: No file in the repo names edwardwas as maintainer/author/homepage/bug-reports; both dead README badges are gone; the design thesis is written down in the README; the package builds and the test suite passes under the new name.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
NAMING CANDIDATE: grid-sized (proposed 2026-08-13)

Availability checked against Hackage:
  grid-sized     -> 404  FREE
  sized-grid     -> 200  taken (edwardwas, unreleasable for this fork)
  grid           -> 200  TAKEN: mhwombat, 'Tools for working with regular
                         grids (graphs, lattices)', live at 7.8.15
  vector-sized   -> 200  the convention being matched
  matrix-sized   -> 200  precedent that X-sized need NOT wrap X

Cost of matching the convention all the way (module prefix follows the name,
since vector-sized ships Data.Vector.Sized, not VectorSized):
  library:  12 modules under src/SizedGrid/
  consumer: ../aoc, 9 imports across 8 files, plus 2 dep refs
            (aoc/cabal.project:3, aoc/aoc.cabal:66)

The one cost of grid-sized: mhwombat's 'grid' is live and in the SAME domain
(lattices, neighbours, distance, boundary behaviour). Readers who learned the
convention from vector-sized will read grid-sized as a size-indexed wrapper
over it. False lineage, not a false domain claim.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
NAMING, second pass: the neighbour that matters is 'grids', not 'grid'

grids (ChrisPenner, Hackage, BSD-3): "Arbitrary sized type-safe grids with
useful combinators". Modules Data.Grid, Data.Grid.Internal.Coord,
Data.Grid.Examples.Conway. Deps: comonad, adjunctions, distributive,
singletons, vector. Last upload 2019-03-10, at 0.5.0.1.

That is the same library concept as this one, by a different author, six
months before upstream sized-grid's last commit (2019-09-13). Both are dead.
The domain is a graveyard of 2019 attempts; this fork is the live one.

Two consequences:
  1. 'sized' does not differentiate. grids was ALREADY "arbitrary sized
     type-safe grids". The real differentiator is the thesis (boundary policy
     in the coordinate type, total-or-Maybe, sealed constructor), which no
     package name will carry. Accept that; name for discovery instead.
  2. RETRACTS the Data.Grid.Sized.* suggestion from the previous comment.
     grids owns Data.Grid. Nesting under another package's namespace implies
     a relationship that does not exist. Use Grid.Sized.* or keep SizedGrid.*.

Other names checked, all FREE: finite-grid, static-grid, fixed-grid,
bounded-grid, grid-comonad, mosaic, tessera, toroid, tiling, plane, lattice.
Three live Haskell conventions for size-in-the-type: '-sized' (vector-sized,
matrix-sized), 'fixed-' (fixed-vector), 'Static' (hmatrix, static-tensor).
'-sized' is the most modern and most searched.

Runner-up was finite-grid (matches finite-typelits, and Ordinal IS a Finite),
rejected because 'finite' reads as "not infinite" rather than "size in the
type", where 'sized' is unambiguous in Haskell.

VERDICT: grid-sized.

title: CI: cabal matrix fails to resolve on GHC 9.14.1 -- gloss stack pins containers <0.8
description:
`cabal build all` fails at dependency resolution (9s, before any compilation) on GHC 9.14.1.

Reproduced locally with nix ghc9141 + cabal 3.16.1.0:
