title: Adopt ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat to remove manual Nat proof plumbing
description:
The library currently discharges type-level arithmetic by hand with Data.Constraint.Nat
and, in places, unsafeCoerce.

Manual plumbing in the library:
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:61  '\\ plusNat @n @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:68  '\\ leTrans @(x + 1) @n @m'
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:79  '\\ plusMinusInverse3 @1 @m \\ minusNat @m @1'
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305  the whole AllSizedKnown class exists only to
    thread 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' through timesNat

And it leaks all the way into user code. ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:78-80 has to write:

    \\ plusNat @n @1
    \\ leTrans @1 @n @(n + 1)
    \\ plusMonotone2 @n @0 @1

and ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:96-97 the same again via withDict. That is the library's
proof obligations showing up in a puzzle solution.

../aoc already depends on ghc-typelits-natnormalise and ghc-typelits-knownnat.
sized-grid does not. Adding

    ghc-options: -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.Normalise -fplugin=GHC.TypeLits.KnownNat.Solver

discharges most 'KnownNat (n * m)', 'n <= n + 1' and 'n + 1 <= m' goals automatically.

Expected wins:
  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-305) likely disappears entirely, which
    simplifies the constraint on nearly every Grid function.
  - Callers stop needing KnownNat (n * n) in signatures -- cf. ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33
    'parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...'
  - The unsound axioms in SizedGrid/Internal/Type.hs become unnecessary.

Caveat: plugins are a build-time dependency for *users* too if the constraints appear
in exported signatures. Measure how much of the public API simplifies before
committing. Do this before the Ordinal representation change -- it will make that
refactor much less painful.
close_reason: Merged to master (387cde5..ecd572f). Plugins adopted; the two hand-written Nat axioms (timesNat in the AllSizedKnown instance, plusNat @k @1 in reifyOrdinal) and the Data.Constraint.Nat imports are gone. Verified: nix flake check passes on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1, 283 tests pass, the plugin-free example packages still build, and sized-grid builds under ../aoc's bare-ghc912 toolchain where cabal resolves natnormalise 0.9.6 / knownnat 0.8.4 / tcplugin-api 0.19.0.0 straight from Hackage. Public API unchanged: windowFits stays an asserted axiom (needs presburger) and AllSizedKnown stays (it is plugin-free induction, not plumbing). The predicted caller-side win is NOT achievable via plugins -- they are not transitive -- and is tracked as sized-grid-k6n.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
EVIDENCE AGAINST, from trying it during the wave-02 fixes (sized-grid-2h0 / sized-grid-px9).

Both plugins were added and then REMOVED again:

1. They did not solve the problem. The wanted was 'z <= y - n' from a given 'n + 1 <= x' plus 'x + z <= y + 1'. ghc-typelits-natnormalise does not use given <= premises to discharge wanted <= goals, so the error was unchanged ('Cannot satisfy: z <= y - m'). ghc-typelits-presburger is the plugin that does this, and it is marked BROKEN in nixpkgs.

2. They break GHC 9.14. ghc-typelits-natnormalise depends on ghc-tcplugins-extra, whose bound is 'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13'; with GHC 9.14.1 the nix build fails at configure with [Cabal-8010]. Since the flake checks both 9.12.3 and 9.14.1, adopting them would have cost 9.14 support outright.

What worked instead: restate constraints as additions rather than truncating Nat subtractions where possible ('x + z <= y + 1' not 'z <= y - x + 1'), and assert the residual existential facts in SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the pre-existing takeAddIsId.

Recommend this issue be reconsidered or closed unless presburger becomes usable AND ghc-tcplugins-extra gains a 9.14 bound. Retest before adopting.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
RETESTED 2026-08-09 as the previous comment asked. Both blockers still stand, and one
of them is worse than 'nixpkgs has not caught up'.

1. ghc-tcplugins-extra has NO GHC 9.14 release at all -- this is upstream, not a pin
   problem. Hackage's version list tops out at 0.5, whose bound is literally
   'ghc >=7.10 && <9.13', and whose tested-with stops at GHC 9.12.1. Reproduced the
   failure end to end by building the plugin against the 9.14 package set:

       Configuring ghc-tcplugins-extra-0.5...
       Error: [Cabal-8010]
       Encountered missing or private dependencies:
           ghc >=7.10 && <9.13 (installed: 9.14.1)

   ghc-typelits-natnormalise 0.7.12 and ghc-typelits-knownnat 0.7.13 both sit on top of
   it, so all three are unavailable on 9.14 together.

2. ghc-typelits-presburger 0.7.4.2 is still meta.broken = true in nixpkgs for both
   ghc912 and ghc914. It remains the only plugin that would discharge the actual wanted
   from the wave-02 work (a '<=' goal from '<=' givens); natnormalise does not do that.

Not a stale-pin excuse: flake.lock's nixpkgs is 2026-08-06, three days old.

Also ruling out the obvious workaround, so nobody spends time on it: adopting the
plugins only for GHC < 9.13 via 'if impl(ghc < 9.13)' in the cabal file does not work
for this library. The plugins do not simplify signatures by themselves -- they let us
WRITE simpler ones. Any signature written to depend on them would then fail to compile
on 9.14, so the public API would differ by compiler. That is not acceptable for a
library, and API simplification is the entire point of this issue.

Deferring rather than closing: the plan is sound the moment upstream moves. RETEST
CONDITION, both must hold:
  - a ghc-tcplugins-extra release accepting ghc >= 9.14 (check Hackage, not just
    nixpkgs), and
  - ghc-typelits-presburger no longer marked broken in nixpkgs.
Until then sized-grid-qh9 should proceed on its own option 2.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
RETESTED 2026-08-12. The deferral's blocker is gone -- it dissolved rather than being
fixed, so the stated retest condition never triggers as written.

The condition asked for "a ghc-tcplugins-extra release accepting ghc >= 9.14". That
will not happen and no longer matters: natnormalise 0.9 and knownnat 0.8 DROPPED
ghc-tcplugins-extra and moved to ghc-tcplugin-api. Current Hackage:

  ghc-typelits-natnormalise 0.9.6   ghc >=8.8.1 && <9.15   (was 0.7.12)
  ghc-typelits-knownnat     0.8.4   ghc >=8.0.1 && <9.17   (was 0.7.13)
  ghc-tcplugin-api          0.19.0.0

ghc-tcplugins-extra is still stuck at 0.5 / 'ghc <9.13', and presburger 0.7.4.2 is
still 'ghc <9.13' and still meta.broken in nixpkgs. Neither is on the path any more.

VERIFIED, not just read off Hackage: all three build against GHC 9.14.1, and the
library + tasty suite build and pass on 9.12.3 (283 tests) and 9.14.1. 'nix flake
check' covers both.

nixpkgs' hackage snapshot still ships the 0.7.x line for both compilers, so flake.nix
pins all three with callHackageDirect. Drop those overrides once nixpkgs ships
natnormalise >= 0.9.

DONE on branch worktree-natnormalise-h56 (commit 98b9a2c): plugins enabled in
'common lang', and the two hand-written axioms removed --
'timesNat' in the AllSizedKnown instance, 'plusNat @k @1' in 'reifyOrdinal' --
along with the Data.Constraint.Nat import in both modules. Library is warning-clean.

MEASURED, since this issue said to measure before committing: the public API
simplifies by nothing. One of the three predicted wins materialised, the smallest.

  1. AllSizedKnown does NOT disappear, and should not. Its instances are what derive
     'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' inductively from per-axis KnownNats WITHOUT a
     plugin. Replacing it with a bare 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' would push the
     plugin requirement onto every downstream package writing polymorphic grid code.
     The class is load-bearing, not plumbing.

  2. "Callers stop needing KnownNat (n * n)" is NOT achievable this way, at all.
     Type-checker plugins are not transitive: sized-grid enabling them affects only
     sized-grid's modules. ../aoc solves its own constraints and does NOT enable them
     (no 'typelits' in aoc.cabal, cabal.project or flake.nix -- the premise in this
     issue's description that it already depends on them is false). Filed
     sized-grid-k6n for the actual cause: AllGridSizeKnown is a type *family*, so it
     emits 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize ...)' at the call site instead of solving it.
     That fix needs no plugin.

  3. windowFits stays. Retested by deleting it: 'Cannot satisfy: z <= y - m' and
     'Cannot satisfy: m <= y', unchanged. Still presburger's job.

Also stale in the description: the '\\ plusNat @n @1 \\ leTrans ...' plumbing cited at
../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:78-80 is already gone -- the wave-02 work removed it.

RECOMMENDATION: merge is a judgment call, and a close one. For it: two hand-written
Nat axioms and a proof-axiom dependency surface go away, and future Nat work gets
easier. Against it: three hand-pinned Hackage overrides to carry until nixpkgs
catches up, in exchange for zero public-API simplification. The concrete pain this
issue was filed about is sized-grid-k6n, which is independent of the plugins.

title: Six benchmarks diverge from the checked-in laptop baseline on unmodified source; the baseline's numbers for them were never real work
description:
Found while measuring sized-grid-adr.14 on 2026-08-19. Not caused by that change: the divergence reproduces with adr.14's diff stashed out, and again on a full 'cabal clean' rebuild.

Running the suite at 689e9e8 -- the commit that recorded bench/baseline-ghc9.12.3-aarch64-darwin.csv, and the same source that recorded it -- six lines do not match the CSV. Allocation, which bench/README.md says does not drift:

                                                    baseline        today
  (.-.) x10000, Clamped 100x100 (coord list shared)       17 B     1.04 MB
  toEnum/fromEnum x300, Clamped 300                    31.2 KB     57.6 KB
  fmap 300x300 [no coord at all]                          32 B     4.32 MB
  index x90000, 300x300 (coord list shared)               48 B     7.92 MB
  mapGrid then sum 300x300   boxed                        32 B     4.32 MB
  mapGrid then sum 300x300 unboxed                        20 B    720.1 KB

Time moved with allocation on three of them and not on the others:

  fmap 300x300                     0.316 ms  ->  1.500 ms
  mapGrid then sum boxed           0.316 ms  ->  1.484 ms
  index x90000                     0.743 ms  ->  1.493 ms
  (.-.) x10000                     0.066 ms  ->  0.136 ms
  mapGrid then sum unboxed         0.092 ms  ->  0.088 ms   (same time, 20 B -> 720 KB)
  toEnum/fromEnum x300             0.006 ms  ->  0.007 ms

Which way is wrong is not in doubt. 'nf (fmap (+1)) bigGrid' over 90,000 boxed Ints cannot allocate 32 bytes. 4.32 MB is about 48 B a cell, which is what the work costs; 32 B is the signature of GHC floating the whole expression out of the benchmarked function and the harness timing a shared result. The baseline is the side that is not measuring anything, and today's numbers are the honest ones. bench/Main.hs already documents this exact hazard for the stencil radius benchmarks ('as a literal GHC floats mooreStencil 1 out ... and what gets measured is the step alone under a label claiming otherwise'), so it has bitten this suite before.

Two things to find out, in order:

1. What stopped the floating. The source is identical, so it is the environment: a GHC or dependency version different from the one that recorded the CSV, or the CSV having been recorded from a build with non-default flags. 'mapGrid then sum unboxed' is the clue -- its time did not change at all while its allocation went from 20 B to 720 KB, which reads like a measurement/accounting difference rather than a code one, while fmap's 4.7x says the opposite. Both patterns in one run need explaining.

2. Whether the five affected benchmarks should be rewritten so they cannot float in the first place, the way the stencil radius ones were (take the input as an argument the harness varies rather than a CAF). A benchmark whose recorded number is 32 B is not guarding anything.

Until this is settled, treat those six lines of the baseline as unusable. The rest of the CSV was reproduced exactly.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-19.

Part 1, what stopped the floating: bisected via git log on the CSV file.
689e9e8's checked-in baseline has the six small/fake numbers this issue
opened with (17 B, 32 B, 48 B, 20 B ...). The very next baseline
re-record, at 537bca4 (closes adr.14, "Make unsafeOrdinal's range check
free"), already has today's honest numbers. A fresh build of current
HEAD reproduces the checked-in CSV for all six lines to within 3%
(verified: cabal build + a --csv run against
bench/baseline-ghc9.12.3-aarch64-darwin.csv, all 57 benchmarks pass
--fail-if-slower 25). So the checked-in baseline is NOT stale -- the
divergence this issue found was specific to reproducing the OLD commit
689e9e8 against its OWN period CSV; current HEAD's CSV is trustworthy.

I could not pin the exact GHC mechanism further. Tried reintroducing
just unsafeOrdinal's old `assert`-based check (adr.14's own diagnosis:
assert desugars to opaque assertError, forcing boxing and blocking
inlining) in isolation, on top of today's tree, and rebuilt -- that did
NOT reproduce the float, so "assert vs guard" alone isn't the trigger;
whatever tipped GHC's decision at 537bca4 is more diffuse than that one
function. Not pursued further -- the cost of a real bisection (several
full -O2 library rebuilds per candidate commit) wasn't worth it once
part 1's actual question (is the current baseline usable) was answered
yes.

What IS certain, and is the actionable finding: tasty-bench's own
source documents this exact hazard class. From Test/Tasty/Bench.hs
(funcToBench, ~line 1359): "GHC ... does not notice that `f` and `x`
arguments are loop invariant and could be floated, and the whole `f x`
expression shared" -- UNLESS it does, which is exactly what happened
to these six. All six share one shape: `nf f x` (or `whnf f x`) where
both f and x are fully static (a top-level CAF grid, or a bare
integer/coord literal) -- structurally identical to the mooseStencil
radius hazard already documented and fixed elsewhere in bench/Main.hs,
just tripped by an unrelated inlining-threshold change instead of a
literal-vs-argument mistake.

Part 2, fix: wrapped all six in `env (pure <shared value>) $ \x -> ...`,
pushing the value through tasty-bench's withResource/unsafePerformIO
boundary, which GHC's simplifier does not see through -- this is
tasty-bench's own documented idiom for exactly this ("consider forcing
its evaluation separately, e.g. via env or withResource"). env doesn't
add a name segment, so --baseline matching by name is unaffected.
Verified: full `cabal test all` (589+ tests, all suites) passes, full
benchmark suite (57/57) passes --fail-if-slower 25 against the existing
checked-in CSV with no baseline re-record needed -- the six wrapped
lines report the same honest numbers as before wrapping, within noise.

This is a structural mitigation, not a proof: it removes the top-level-
CAF/literal shape that this hazard needs, using the mechanism
tasty-bench itself relies on to prevent it, but I can't produce a
GHC-internals guarantee that no future change could still tip some
other benchmark in this file the same way. Worth remembering as a
pattern for adr.5/adr.8 or any new benchmark that applies a function to
nothing but a shared grid and a literal.
close_reason: Closed

title: State the odd-extent precondition for windows, with the centre coordinate
description:
Window-shaped operations only make sense when every extent is odd: a window
with an even side has no centre cell, so there is no coordinate for the focus
to sit at. Today nothing states that. gridTiles and the neighbourhood
functions either work it out at the call site or quietly produce something
off-centre.

Prior art: Chris Penner's 'grids' states it as a class with the precondition
attached, in Data.Grid.Internal.Shapes:

  type Even n = Mod n 2 == 0
  type Odd  n = Not (Even n)
  type OddC n = Odd n ?! 'Text "Dimension '" ':<>: 'ShowType n
                      ':<>: 'Text " must be odd to use 'neighbouring' functions"

  class Centered (dims :: [Nat]) where
    centerCoord :: Coord dims

So the class both supplies the centre coordinate and refuses, with a sentence
rather than an unsolved Nat goal, to instantiate at an even extent.

Two things to keep and one to drop:
  KEEP the pairing of the precondition with the thing it guards. A standalone
       'isOdd' constraint that callers must remember is worth much less than
       a class you cannot obtain without it.
  KEEP the error text naming the offending dimension via ShowType.
  DROP the OVERLAPPING/OVERLAPPABLE instance pair. We have SList and the
       IsCoordList machinery and should fold over the axes the way the rest
       of the library does, which also keeps it consistent with the unrolling
       work in sized-grid-5uq.

Depends on sized-grid-0kq for the '?!' operator; the natural consumer is the
neighbourhood decomposition issue and sized-grid-7gs.
notes: Correction to the description's last line: sized-grid-7gs is CLOSED, not pending -- it delivered neighbours/mooreNeighbours/vonNeumannNeighbours already. So the odd-extent precondition is not blocking new work there; it is a precision upgrade to an API that already ships, and its live consumer is sized-grid-meg. Also relevant: sized-grid-3t6 (sliding windows, stride 1), which wants the same precondition.
close_reason: Landed: Odd/Even/OddC in Data.Grid.Sized.Coord.Class (via ?!), and centreCoord/CentredAxis in Data.Grid.Sized.Coord, folding over the axis list with the same hcpure/IsCoordLifted shape zeroCoord uses -- no OVERLAPPING/OVERLAPPABLE instances. Tests in tests/Test/Neighbours.hs (centredTests). Manually verified the readable compile error: centreCoord :: Coord '[Clamped 4] -> "Dimension '4' must be odd to have a centre coordinate". Unblocks sized-grid-meg.

title: Replace CoordDiff's per-arity tuple family with a manifolds-style Needle
description:
Inspiration: the `manifolds` package (Justus Sagemuller), `Semimanifold`'s associated
`Needle` type.

    class AdditiveGroup (Needle x) => Semimanifold x where
      type Needle x :: Type
      (.+~^) :: x -> Needle x -> x

`Needle` is an associated type, and products get theirs structurally:
`Needle (a,b) = (Needle a, Needle b)`, from the pair instance. There is no arity
ceiling and no per-arity boilerplate.

sized-grid does the opposite. src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:204-215 declares CoordDiff by hand,
one `type instance` per arity:

    type instance CoordDiff '[]              = ()
    type instance CoordDiff '[a]             = Identity (Diff a)
    type instance CoordDiff '[a, b]          = (Diff a, Diff b)
    ... up to ...
    type instance CoordDiff '[a, b, c, d, e, f] = (Diff a, ..., Diff f)

Seven instances, so six dimensions. THE CEILING IS REAL: a `Coord` of seven or more axes
has no `CoordDiff` instance, therefore `Diff (Coord cs)` is stuck, therefore no
`AffineSpace (Coord cs)` instance and no `offsetCoord`. The user can in principle add
their own `type instance` (these are open families) plus a 7-tuple, but that is an orphan
instance for something the library should supply.

The tuple encoding also forces `IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)` into the
context of everything that offsets --- see `offsetCoord` (Coord.hs:361-368) and the
`AffineSpace (Coord cs)` instance (Coord.hs:222-226) --- which is why generics-sop
appears in consumer signatures that have no other reason to mention it.

PROPOSAL

Make the displacement coord-shaped instead of tuple-shaped:

    type Needle (Coord cs) = Coord (MapDiff cs)

`MapDiff` (Coord.hs:218-220) is already a closed, recursive family, so it needs no new
per-arity code. The payoff:

  - no arity ceiling
  - `IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs)` disappears from every signature
  - the needle inherits `:|`, `EmptyCoord`, `Show`, `Eq`, `AdditiveGroup`, `Random`
    from the existing `Coord` instances for free
  - `CoordDiff` and its seven instances are deleted outright

The `AffineSpace` helper functions at Coord.hs:234-244 and the `offsetCoord` helper at
Coord.hs:375-382 already recurse structurally over `NP I (MapDiff xs)`; they get simpler,
because `productTypeTo` / `productTypeFrom` are no longer needed at either end.

COST

Tuple literals at call sites stop working. Today ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:98 writes
`c .+^ (-1, -1)` and ../aoc/src/2016/02.hs:45 writes `mempty .+^ (0, toInteger col)`;
both would become `(-1) :| (-1) :| EmptyCoord`. That is more uniform but more verbose in
two dimensions, which is the overwhelmingly common case.

Mitigation worth evaluating as part of this issue: keep a small `IsProductType`-based
conversion available as an explicit function (say `needleFromTuple`), or supply a pattern
synonym for the 2D needle, so the ergonomic case is one short call rather than a
structural literal. Do NOT keep it as an implicit coercion in the class --- that
reintroduces the constraint this issue exists to remove.
design: Follow manifolds: the displacement type is associated and products get theirs structurally. Reuse Coord itself as the needle (Needle (Coord cs) = Coord (MapDiff cs)) rather than introducing a new product type, so all existing Coord instances and patterns apply unchanged. Keep any tuple conversion as an explicit opt-in function, never as a class constraint.
acceptance_criteria: A Coord of seven or more axes has a working AffineSpace/offset API; IsProductType (CoordDiff cs) (MapDiff cs) appears in no exported signature; the seven CoordDiff type instances are deleted; ../aoc builds against the new needle.
close_reason: Closed

title: Benchmark "mapGrid then sum 300x300" does not sum
description:
The two benchmarks named `mapGrid then sum 300x300 {boxed,unboxed}` (bench/Main.hs:598 and :601) have the body `nf (mapGrid (+ 1)) g`. There is no sum: `nf` deep-forces the whole new 90,000-cell grid, so what is measured is a map plus a full NFData walk over the result.

The name misleads. sized-grid-adr.10 was filed partly on the strength of these numbers reading slower than `foldlGrid' 300x300`, and concluded from that that Foldable's `sum` built a thunk chain. It does not -- `sum` over that grid allocates 1,128 bytes, identical to `foldlGrid'`. The gap was map-and-force versus fold, which is not a comparison of anything.

Fixing it is not a free rename. The full benchmark name is the key both for the checked-in laptop baseline (bench/baseline-ghc9.12.3-aarch64-darwin.csv lines 46-47) and for the CI baseline in the Actions cache, and `--baseline` matches by full name. Renaming orphans both rows: the laptop CSV can be edited in the same commit, but the CI cache cannot, so the first PR after the rename compares against nothing for these two and the gate silently passes them.

Options, in preference order:
  1. Rename to what it measures (`mapGrid 300x300`) and edit the two baseline CSV rows in the same commit, accepting one CI run with no comparison for this pair.
  2. Keep the name and add the sum: `whnf (total . mapGrid (+ 1))`. Preserves both baselines' continuity but changes what the number means, which is worse -- a silently redefined baseline row is the thing the bench README exists to prevent.

Recommend (1).
close_reason: Closed

title: Test suite and README have warnings that only appear on a cold build
description:
'cabal build all --enable-tests --ghc-options=-fforce-recomp' on master (c697f1b) reports 8 warnings that a normal incremental build never shows, because GHC only emits warnings when it actually recompiles:

  README.lhs:104:8   -Wredundant-constraints
  README.lhs:129:16  -Wredundant-constraints
  tests/Main.hs:85:8    -Wredundant-constraints
  tests/Main.hs:101:11  -Wunused-matches
  tests/Main.hs:101:16  -Wunused-matches
  tests/Main.hs:145:8   -Wredundant-constraints
  tests/Main.hs:213:20  -Wunused-matches
  tests/Main.hs:213:25  -Wunused-matches

src/ is clean; this is test and README code only.

Found while working sized-grid-wrc, where a cached 'Up to date' build made a
before/after warning comparison look clean when it had simply not recompiled
anything. That is the more general trap: any check of the form 'did my change
add a warning' is worthless unless the build actually ran, so use
-fforce-recomp or compare against a forced baseline.

Two things worth doing:
 - fix the eight warnings
 - decide whether CI should build with -Werror on a cold cache, which is what
   would have caught these when they were introduced (relates to sized-grid-rt9,
   the GitHub Actions issue)
close_reason: Both parts resolved. (1) The 8 warnings (README.lhs, tests/Main.hs) are already gone -- verified via a clean 'rm -rf dist-newstyle && cabal build all --enable-tests --ghc-options=-fforce-recomp': zero warnings on a genuinely cold build, all 485+4 tests pass. Fixed incidentally by later refactors (likely sized-grid-4xh's AllSizedKnown/AllGridSizeKnown merge touching the same signatures). No code change needed. (2) The -Werror-on-CI decision is: yes, do it -- filed as sized-grid-dvm with the two pre-existing example-package warnings (sudoko missing-export-lists, ising-example unused-top-binds) that currently block turning it on repo-wide.

title: fromJust in Ordinal construction: seven call sites total only by an unchecked invariant
description:
Split out of sized-grid-0vq part (b); part (a), the four unreachable 'error' calls, is done.

'fromJust . numToOrdinal' appears in arithmetic that is total only because a mod or a
clamp happened just beforehand, which nothing checks:

  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Periodic.hs:42, 54, 65, 74
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/HardWrap.hs:44, 61
  - src/SizedGrid/Ordinal.hs:82        toEnum = fromJust . numToOrdinal
  - src/SizedGrid/Coord/Class.hs:83    maxCoord

Each is correct today, but the invariant lives in the reader's head, and every one of
them turns a future off-by-one into 'Maybe.fromJust: Nothing' with no indication of
which coordinate or which operation produced it.

This is deliberately NOT fixed by sprinkling error messages on the existing code. The
right fix arrives with sized-grid-upo: once Ordinal is a newtype over Int, all of these
collapse into a single 'unsafeOrdinalFromInt' whose precondition is stated once, checked
with an assert in a debug build, and free in a release build. Doing it before upo means
writing the same defensive code twice.
acceptance_criteria: No fromJust remains in src/; the single unchecked construction point documents its precondition and is assert-checked when compiled with -fno-ignore-asserts.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 'Make Ordinal a newtype over Int' on branch worktree-ordinal-int; 100 tests pass, zero warnings

title: Hashable for Ordinal, the four axis types and Coord
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey. Promoted out of "Tier 2: one small
dependency" -- hashable is not a new dependency, see Cost.

== Why

HashMap (Coord cs) v is an obvious thing for a consumer to want -- a sparse
overlay on a dense grid, a memo table keyed by coordinate, a visited set --
and it is currently unreachable without an orphan instance. Ord (Coord cs)
exists (Coord.hs:129) so Data.Map works today; that is the reason this is a
gap worth closing rather than a hole in the type's usability.

== The design question, which is not just "derive it"

Two honest implementations:

  a) hashWithSalt s = hashWithSalt s . coordPosition
     Needs only IsCoordList. One Int hashed, whatever the dimension.
     coordPosition is injective on Coord cs, so this is collision-free within
     a shape, and it is the cheapest possible.

  b) fold hashWithSalt over the NP, componentwise.
     Needs All Hashable cs. Matches what a tuple instance does.

Prefer (a), and say why in the Haddock: the coordinate space is a dense
prefix of the naturals by construction, so the position IS the perfect hash,
and (b) would pay per-axis for a worse distribution. The one thing (a) gives
up is that two Coords of DIFFERENT shapes with the same position hash the
same -- which is not observable, because they are different types.

Ordinal and the four axis types get the same treatment through
ordinalToInt.

== Cost

None. hashable is already in the build plan, pulled in by aeson and lens,
both already direct dependencies.
close_reason: Added Hashable instances for Ordinal, all four axis types, and Coord using their dense positions; added hashable to direct library dependencies. cabal build succeeds.

title: Keep chart/seam machinery in grid-atlas; do not extract a grid-independent manifold library yet
description:
## Decision

Do not extract Data.Grid.Atlas / Data.Grid.Atlas.CubeMap's chart/seam machinery into a separate grid-independent package (e.g. 'manifold' or 'atlas-topology') at this time, despite sized-grid-ts4's evidence bar (two concrete atlases) now being met.

## Rationale

sized-grid-ts4 asked for two concrete atlases before revisiting extraction. Both now exist: the tiled atlas (fh2, identity seams) and the cube map (68j, a hand-derived D4 transition table). Comparing them does show a real seam: Face/Axis/Extremum/Heading and cubeSeam's shape -- (Face, Axis, Extremum) -> (Face, Axis, Extremum, Bool) -- never mention Grid or cell contents anywhere load-bearing. AtlasCoord's only grid-specific half is the `Coord cs` component; the chart-index half is bare Ordinal k.

But both data points come from inside the same package, with the same author guessing at what a non-grid consumer would want. There is still zero actual non-grid (or even second-grid-package) consumer: `../aoc`, the fork's real external consumer (see memory sized-grid-aoc-relationship), has no call site touching grid-atlas at all. Extracting now would mean fixing an API boundary -- what a chart interface looks like, whether a bare-coordinate/no-payload atlas is representable, what a portable 'Seam' type looks like -- against zero outside pressure. That is exactly the speculation Data.Grid.Atlas's own haddock warns against when justifying why it deferred a general seam-transition table until the cube map existed, applied one level up: a second internal example is not the same evidence as one real external pull.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Extract now into a new package with no grid-sized dependency**: rejected -- no real non-grid consumer exists to drive the cut; the resulting API would be shaped by guesswork, not by a call site.
- **Extract only the clearly grid-independent leaf types (Face, Axis, Extremum, Heading) while leaving Atlas/AtlasCoord/cubeSeam in grid-atlas**: rejected for now -- splitting small helper types into their own package with zero consumers is pure churn; revisit alongside the fuller cut if/when the trigger below fires.
- **Close the question permanently / never revisit**: rejected -- the tension is real and documented (cubeSeam's shape is already payload-agnostic), so it should stay visible as a decision rather than be dropped silently.

## Trigger to revisit

When a concrete non-grid consumer actually wants Face/Axis/Extremum/Heading/cubeSeam-shaped chart/seam machinery without depending on Grid -- e.g. a pathfinding/graph problem in ../aoc, or a bare-coordinate topology (Mobius strip, arbitrary graph) elsewhere in this repo -- extract then, with that consumer's real call sites driving the API, not before.

## Affects

- sized-grid-ts4 (the issue this decision resolves)
- sized-grid-fh2 (tiled atlas)
- sized-grid-68j (cube map)
close_reason: Superseded by sized-grid-1av

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text: Superseded by sized-grid-1av: the 'wait for a non-grid consumer' gate was the wrong criterion. The seam-table half of cubeSeam (chart id + boundary label + involution) is already payload-agnostic and evidenced by existing tests, not a guess -- that part gets designed now (target: atlas-topology package) even with zero outside consumers. Only the coordinate-stepping half (cubeStep) stays gated on more evidence.

title: Each for Grid: each = traverse, so generic 'over each' code works on grids
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey.

  instance IsCoordList cs => Each (Grid cs a) (Grid cs b) a b where
    each = traverse

Two lines. Grid is Traversable already (Internal/Grid.hs:92 gives
Traversable (GridOf v cs) for Traversable v), so this is the class default
under another name; lens ships no blanket Traversable-implies-Each instance,
so it has to be written.

Value is modest and deliberately recorded as such: it buys nothing traverse
does not already buy, except that code written against 'each' -- which is a
fair amount of lens-idiomatic code -- starts working on grids.

Boxed Grid only. The unboxed GridOf cannot be Traversable, so 'each' there
would need a hand-written round trip; that is not worth it, and Ixed
(see the companion issue) already covers unboxed element access.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Added the boxed Grid Each instance as each = traverse in Internal/Grid.hs. Validated with nix develop --command cabal test grid-sized:test:tests; compilation and Grid traversal tests passed. The suite still has two unrelated existing Periodic Enum law failures.

title: Replace the AllGridSizeKnown type family with a class, so callers stop writing KnownNat (n * n)
description:
AllGridSizeKnown is a type family, so it emits 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize ...)' goals
at the call site instead of solving them. That is what makes puzzle code in ../aoc
write type-level arithmetic by hand:

    ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33
    parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => String -> Maybe (Grid '[Clamped n, Clamped n] Cell)

'gridFromList' asks for 'AllGridSizeKnown cs' (src/SizedGrid/Internal/Grid.hs:253).
Being a *family* (Internal/Grid.hs:213-219) it expands to a conjunction --

    AllGridSizeKnown cs = ( KnownNat (CoordNat (Head cs))
                          , KnownNat (MaxCoordSize (Tail cs))
                          , KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)
                          , AllGridSizeKnown (Tail cs) )

-- and then does no solving at all: the raw 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' goal lands
on the caller. For cs ~ '[Clamped n, Clamped n] that is 'KnownNat (n * (n * 1))',
which GHC cannot get from 'KnownNat n', so the caller states it by hand.

Contrast the AllSizedKnown *class* (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:783-791): its instances
derive 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)' inductively from the per-axis KnownNats, so a
caller with 'KnownNat n' needs nothing else. Same obligation, discharged by
instance resolution rather than dumped on the caller.

Proposed: give the structural-recursion classes the same treatment -- replace the
AllGridSizeKnown family with a class carrying the evidence it currently demands
(gridFromList, collapseGrid, and the ToJSON/FromJSON instances at
Internal/Grid.hs:265,283 are the users), so the induction happens during instance
resolution.

Expected: '../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33' loses 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' and reads
'parse :: KnownNat n => ...'.

WHY THIS AND NOT sized-grid-h56: h56 predicted the plugins would fix this. They
cannot -- type-checker plugins are not transitive. sized-grid enabling them affects
only sized-grid's own modules; ../aoc solves its own constraints and does not enable
them (verified: no 'typelits' in aoc.cabal, cabal.project or flake.nix). So this
leak is fixable only by an API change, and needs no plugin.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Done. AllGridSizeKnown is now a class with a GridSizeProof GADT method carrying the tail's dictionary; gridFromList, collapseGrid and the ToJSON/FromJSON instances case on it and no longer ask for SListI cs either.

VERIFIED, and verified the way this issue actually needed: a new plugin-free test suite. sized-grid.cabal's 'common lang' is split into 'lang-base' (language + warnings) and 'lang' (that plus the two solvers); the new 'downstream' test-suite imports lang-base only, because -fplugin is not transitive and a consumer therefore compiles without them. tests-downstream/Main.hs is ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs's signature with the leak deleted:

    parseSquare :: KnownNat n => String -> Maybe (Grid '[Clamped n, Clamped n] Char)
    renderSquare :: KnownNat n => Grid '[Clamped n, Clamped n] Char -> [String]
    roundTripJSON :: KnownNat n => Grid '[Clamped n, Clamped n] Char -> Maybe (...)

Negative control: reverting only the three source files and rebuilding that suite fails at exactly three sites --

    tests-downstream/Main.hs:41 Could not deduce KnownNat ... from the context: KnownNat n  (gridFromList)
    tests-downstream/Main.hs:48 ... (collapseGrid)
    tests-downstream/Main.hs:56 ... (decode)

so the suite is a real regression test and not a tautology.

Green: library builds with no warnings, 283 tests pass, downstream 3/3, readme test-suite and all three example executables build. Test warning count in tests/Main.hs is 6 before and after (pre-existing -Wunused-matches / -Wredundant-constraints, unrelated).

Head and Tail are now unused by the library but still exported -- see the follow-up.

title: Grid.Sized.Grid.* repeats 'Grid' twice in the module path
description:
The rename in sized-grid-85n mapped SizedGrid.* to Grid.Sized.* mechanically, preserving the existing tree. That is correct for a rename but leaves four modules whose paths stutter:

  Grid.Sized.Grid.Class
  Grid.Sized.Grid.Focused
  Grid.Sized.Grid.Grid     <- worst offender
  Grid.Sized.Grid.Unsafe
  Grid.Sized.Internal.Grid

Under the old prefix 'SizedGrid.Grid.Grid' read as one stutter; now it is two.

Options: flatten the Grid.* layer (Grid.Sized.Class, Grid.Sized.Focused,
Grid.Sized.Unsafe) since Grid.Sized is already the subject; or leave it, since
Coord.* has the same shape and the symmetry is worth something.

Deliberately not done as part of the rename: a rename that also reorganises the
tree is two changes wearing one commit message, and this one is not forced.
close_reason: Done in commit 96cfd54 on worktree-rename-grid-sized. src/Grid/Sized/Grid/Grid.hs -> src/Data/Grid/Sized/Grid.hs, so the module is Data.Grid.Sized.Grid with Class, Focused and Unsafe still beneath it -- the same shape Coord already had. One file moved, not four: the corrected analysis in the comments showed this restores symmetry with Coord rather than breaking it. Build clean, 334 tests still passing. The residual repetition (Grid at positions 2 and 4) is NOT fixed here and is filed as sized-grid-zxz, because that one needs the head module to absorb the type's export list rather than just a file move.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Correction to the description's "Options" paragraph, which framed this wrong.

I wrote it as "flatten the Grid.* layer, OR leave it for symmetry with Coord.*".
That is a false trade. Look at what Coord actually does:

  Grid.Sized.Coord            <- the module for the type
  Grid.Sized.Coord.Class
  Grid.Sized.Coord.Clamped
  Grid.Sized.Coord.Periodic

A module 'A.B' and modules beneath 'A.B.*' coexist perfectly well -- this is the
Data.Vector / Data.Vector.Mutable shape and it is thoroughly idiomatic. Coord
already has it. Grid does not, because the type's module is 'Grid.Sized.Grid.Grid'
and there is no 'Grid.Sized.Grid' at all:

  src/Grid/Sized/Coord.hs        EXISTS
  src/Grid/Sized/Grid.hs         DOES NOT EXIST
  src/Grid/Sized/Grid/Grid.hs    the type lives here instead

So collapsing Grid.Sized.Grid.Grid -> Grid.Sized.Grid does not BREAK symmetry
with Coord, it RESTORES it. Grid is currently the odd one out. The fix is a
single file move, src/Grid/Sized/Grid/Grid.hs -> src/Grid/Sized/Grid.hs, with
Class, Focused and Unsafe staying exactly where they are beneath it.

That also makes this smaller than filed: one module renamed, not four, and the
"leave it alone" option loses the argument that was supporting it.

Independent of the Data.* prefix question: adding or removing a 'Data.' at the
front does not touch this, since Data.Grid.Sized.Grid.Grid stutters identically.

title: axisSteps rescans its candidate list per candidate: the real neighbourhood cost, 67% of it
description:
sized-grid-5uq moved the stepsWithin fold into an IsCoordList method, which is
correct and unrolls, and it was worth 9% of the allocation. The remaining cost
is one function below it, in axisSteps, and it is most of the benchmark.

MEASURED, both sides in one session, on 'extend neighbourSum 50x50':

  HEAD before 5uq                      6.84 ms / 25.71 MB
  after 5uq (the fold as a method)     6.46 ms / 23.42 MB
  with the dedup scan skipped          2.24 ms / 12 MB     (67% less than HEAD)

So the fold was ~9% and this is the rest.

WHAT IT IS. axisSteps builds 'reachable' and then, per element, scans that whole
list again with 'any (beats (d, v)) reachable' --- quadratic in the number of
candidates, with a closure allocated per element. The scan exists to drop
duplicates: on a torus axis with 2*r >= n two offsets reach the same value, and
the one that took fewer steps has to win so that the recorded distance is the
true distance.

THE EXPERIMENT that produced the 2.24 ms was a guard skipping the scan when it
cannot fire:

    axisSteps r c
        | 2 * r + 1 <= ordinalSize @(CoordNat x) = [(abs d, v) | (d, v) <- reachable]
        | otherwise = <the scan as it is now>

Sound for the library's own axes. On a bounded axis the surviving values are at
position i + d and so are distinct for distinct d whatever r is; on Periodic
they are (i + d) mod n, distinct exactly when 2*r + 1 <= n. When every key is
distinct no element beats another --- 'beats' requires key equality, and an
element never beats itself --- so the fast path is elementwise equal to the
scan, order included.

THE DECISION TO MAKE, and why this was not landed with 5uq. The argument above
is about what offsetIsCoord does, not about what the class promises. A
third-party IsCoord with a reflecting boundary --- offset +1 from the top edge
coming back to n-2 --- would satisfy the stated law relating offsetIsCoord to
(.+^) and still produce duplicates under the guard. Either the guard is right
and IsCoord should say that offsetIsCoord is injective in d where it is Just,
or the dedup has to stay unconditional and get cheaper another way (scan the
candidates in (abs d, d) order keeping the first per key, which is the same
answer without the per-element rescan). That is a call about the class contract,
so it is filed rather than assumed.

VERIFY WITH 'extend neighbourSum 50x50' in bench/Main.hs, measuring both sides
now per that file's header. Do not read against the recorded CSV. The 334 tests
in tests/Test/Neighbours.hs already cover the torus cases the scan is for ---
'vonNeumannNeighbours 2' on a 3-cycle, 'mooreNeighbours 2' on a 4-torus --- so
they are the check on whatever replaces it.
notes:
RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY THE DECISION THIS ISSUE ASKED FOR.

The premise was wrong. The cost was not the quadratic dedup scan; it was that
axisSteps is out of line and so folds nothing it calls. One INLINE pragma:

  extend neighbourSum 50x50   6.51 ms / 22 MB  ->  2.12 ms / 9.9 MB  (67% less)

Every other benchmark in the suite unmoved, measured both sides in one session.
All 334 tests plus the downstream and readme suites pass.

WHY THE SCAN WAS NOT THE CAUSE. The neighbourhood functions run at r = 1, so
reachable has three elements and the scan is nine comparisons. Out of line each
one paid a dictionary. Before-Core of $waxisSteps:

  offsetIsCoord $dIsCoord $dKnownNat irred (eta `cast` ...) ds

per candidate, boxing a fresh ds = I# x1, and per inner element of the scan:

  asOrdinal $dIsCoord $fProfunctorFUN $fFunctorConst (lvl10 `cast` ...) (v' `cast` ...)

After-Core at '[Clamped 50, Clamped 50]: reachable is a go loop over Int# whose
body is ># x (-# 49# y) and <# x (negateInt# y), the bounds check against a
literal with no Natural anywhere; the scan is a joinrec, so no closure per
element; key is case v `cast` ... of I# x, asOrdinal reduced to a coercion; and
the (abs d', d') < (abs d, d) tuple comparison is branches on Int# with no
tuples built. No axisSteps, offsetIsCoord, npStepsWithin, integerFromNatural or
dictionary argument survives in the benchmark's Core.

THE CONTRACT DECISION IS DECLINED, and does not need making. The guard measured
2.24 ms / 12 MB -- slower than the INLINE -- so the injectivity law would have
bought nothing. It would also have cost: a reflecting boundary reaches the same
value from +d and -d at an edge, satisfies every law IsCoord currently states,
and is precisely what the fork's thesis (the coordinate type is the boundary
policy, sized-grid-85n) exists to admit. Narrowing the class to buy speed the
compiler gives away for free is the wrong trade.

Commit 66d50ee. Doc note added at axisSteps; the stale claim in the
offsetByPosition note that the residue was the fold above it is corrected.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add the separable policies that fit today: Reflective and Reflect101
description:
Three boundary policies from the transcript catalogue are separable, so they
are ordinary `IsCoord` instances with no new machinery -- the same shape as
Clamped.hs, which is 93 lines including its Haddock.

REFLECTIVE (billiard bounce)
    Stepping past an edge reflects back inside. Index -1 becomes 0, -2 becomes
    1; past the top, size-1 becomes size-1, size becomes size-2.

    bounceAxis size x dx = go (x + dx) where
      go i | i < 0     = go (negate i - 1)
           | i >= size = go (2 * size - 1 - i)
           | otherwise = i

    Note `go` recurses: a displacement larger than 2*size bounces repeatedly.
    Worth doing in closed form (divMod by 2*size, then a conditional mirror) so
    it is O(1) and matches the no-allocation standard the other axis types now
    meet -- see the measured notes on Clamped's (.+^).

REFLECT101 (mirror without edge duplication)
    The image-processing variant: reflects AROUND the boundary cell rather than
    across the wall, so -1 becomes 1, not 0. Standard for Sobel/Laplacian
    kernels, where Reflective double-weights the edge cell. Distinct enough
    from Reflective to be its own type.

CONSTANT / padding
    Out of range yields a fixed value. This one does NOT fit `IsCoord`: the
    policy needs a VALUE, and a coordinate type has no place to put one. It is
    a property of a lookup, not of an axis. Probably belongs as a function over
    the existing `Ordinal` axis (`indexOr :: a -> Grid cs a -> ... -> a`)
    rather than a coord type at all. Filed here to record that it was
    considered and why it is different.

FIT WITH THE THESIS

Reflective and Reflect101 are total, like Clamped, and they destroy information
the same way -- so, like Clamped, they are honest only because the caller named
them. `offsetIsCoord` should still report leaving the axis; the reflection
belongs in (.+^) alone. That is exactly the split Clamped documents at
Coord/Clamped.hs:19-22 and the new types should copy it verbatim.

ONE INTERACTION worth flagging: a bouncing walker has REVERSED VELOCITY after
the bounce, which is a frame transform, which is the seam rule. So Reflective
is the cheapest possible motivation for that work -- a separable policy that
still wants the frame to change. Build it, and the seam-rule question becomes
concrete instead of speculative.

ALSO: `axisDistanceIsCoord` must be overridden. The default measures straight,
which is right; but check whether a reflective axis wants reflected distance
(it probably does not -- distance is a property of the space, and the space is
still bounded). Decide deliberately and test it, the way Periodic's override is
tested.
close_reason: Reflective and Reflect101 IsCoord instances implemented, tested (closed-form vs. issue's own recursive reference, offsetIsCoord/axisDistance/axisBoundary default-preservation, AffineSpace/IsCoord/Aeson laws), and wired into the public API. CONSTANT/padding confirmed not an IsCoord fit, as the issue predicted.

title: Export the coordinate distance axisSteps already computes
description:
Inspiration: `Data.Manifold.Riemannian`'s `Geodesic` class, which asks a manifold for the
path between two points rather than leaving the caller to reconstruct it.

But the real point of this issue is smaller and cheaper than that: SIZED-GRID ALREADY
COMPUTES THE DISTANCE AND THEN THROWS IT AWAY.

    src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:398  axisSteps   :: IsCoordLifted x => Int -> x -> [(Int, x)]
    src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:423  stepsWithin :: All IsCoordLifted cs
                                            => Int -> Coord cs -> [(Int, Coord cs)]

`axisSteps` computes the TRUE per-axis distance, and its own documentation
(Coord.hs:386-397) explains that this is the hard part:

    "Where two offsets reach the same value --- which a torus axis does as soon as
     2 * r >= n --- the one that took fewer steps wins, so the recorded distance is the
     true distance on that axis rather than whichever offset the enumeration happened to
     try first."

`stepsWithin` sums that across axes. And then both consumers discard the `Int`:

    mooreNeighbours      r c = [n | (s, n) <- stepsWithin r c, s > 0]           -- :454
    vonNeumannNeighbours r c = [n | (s, n) <- stepsWithin r c, s > 0, s <= r]   -- :471

Neither `axisSteps` nor `stepsWithin` is exported --- check the export list at
Coord.hs:6-39. So the library contains a correct, wrap-aware, mixed-boundary-policy
distance function that no caller can reach.

PROPOSAL

1. Export the distance directly. Both metrics fall out of the same per-axis numbers:

     coordDistance     :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Coord cs -> Coord cs -> Int  -- L-infinity
     coordManhattan    :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Coord cs -> Coord cs -> Int  -- L-1

   Note these must NOT be built on `stepsWithin`, which is radius-bounded and enumerates
   the whole neighbourhood --- that would be O(r^d) to answer a question that is O(d).
   Factor the per-axis "shorter route wins" rule out of `axisSteps` into a scalar
   `axisDistance :: IsCoordLifted x => x -> x -> Int` and build all three on it.

2. Export `stepsWithin` itself. It is the general primitive (every coord within radius r,
   paired with its true distance), both neighbourhood functions are one-liners over it,
   and BFS-shaped consumers want the distances.

WHY THIS IS THE CHEAPEST ITEM IN THE SET

The semantics are already written, reviewed and covered by the neighbourhood tests. The
work is factoring a scalar out of a list comprehension and adding names to an export
list. No type-level machinery, no breaking change --- purely additive.

CORRECTNESS NOTE

`coordDistance` on a mixed `'[HardWrap 5, Periodic 5]` coord must use each axis's own
policy: the bounded axis measures straight, the torus axis takes the shorter way round.
That is the behaviour `axisSteps` already has and is exactly what a caller cannot easily
write by hand, which is the argument for exporting it.
design: Factor the per-axis 'shorter route wins' rule out of axisSteps into a scalar axisDistance, then build coordDistance, coordManhattan and axisSteps on it. Do NOT implement distance via stepsWithin: that is radius-bounded and O(r^d) for an O(d) question.
acceptance_criteria: coordDistance and coordManhattan are exported and correct on mixed '[HardWrap 5, Periodic 5] coords (torus axis takes the shorter way round); stepsWithin is exported; mooreNeighbours and vonNeumannNeighbours are unchanged in behaviour.
notes:
DONE in df9575d.

DESIGN DEVIATION from this issue, deliberate: the issue said to build all three
on axisDistance, INCLUDING axisSteps. I left axisSteps alone. Rebuilding it on
axisDistance would have to enumerate allCoordLike to find what is within r,
which is two regressions at once:
  - cost goes from O(r) to O(n) per axis regardless of r. 'neighbours' (r=1) on
    a 300-wide axis would go from 3 offsets to 300, in the hot loop of every
    cellular-automaton consumer.
  - ordering changes. axisSteps is documented to order 'by the surviving
    offset, ascending, so the centre sits in the middle'; enumerating values
    would order by value, which on a Periodic axis is a DIFFERENT order and
    would break the 'a torus axis is ordered by offset, not by value' test.
That collides with this issue's own acceptance criterion that moore/vonNeumann
be unchanged in behaviour. So axisDistance is a SECOND implementation of the
'shorter route wins' rule, and the drift risk is handled by a test instead --
see below.

SHIPPED
  axisDistanceIsCoord   new IsCoord method, bounded default, Periodic override
  axisDistance          lifted scalar
  axisDistances         per-axis breakdown (the honest primitive)
  coordDistance         Chebyshev / L-inf
  coordManhattan        L-1
  axisSteps, stepsWithin  now exported
  ChangeLog entry.

Periodic's override needed an InstanceSig to bring n into scope for ordinalSize
(the instance head is 'IsCoord Periodic', so n lives only in the method's
forall). It drops the class's '1 <= n', which the body does not use.

TESTS (24 new, in tests/Test/Neighbours.hs)
  - axisDistance == the distance axisSteps records, checked EXHAUSTIVELY over
    Clamped 5, Periodic 5, Ordinal 5, Periodic 4, Periodic 3. Exhaustive rather
    than QuickCheck because the axes are 5 wide and because Ordinal has no
    Arbitrary instance. This is the anti-drift test.
  - mooreNeighbours r is exactly the coordDistance ball, vonNeumannNeighbours r
    exactly the coordManhattan ball, each on bounded / torus / MIXED axes.
    Strongest available evidence, since the neighbourhoods were already covered.
  - metric laws: identity, symmetry, triangle inequality, Chebyshev <= Manhattan.
  - the mixed-policy acceptance case explicitly:
      axisDistances (mixc 0 0) (mixc 4 4) == [4, 1]   bounded straight, torus wraps
      coordDistance  == 4, coordManhattan == 5

MUTATION-CHECKED: replacing Periodic's 'min d (size - d)' with the naive
straight-line distance fails 12 of the new tests across every group, so they are
not vacuous.

VERIFIED: cabal test -- all 201 pass, both suites. Build clean, no new warnings.
All 8 ../aoc SizedGrid modules still type-check, confirming 'purely additive'.

SPUN OUT: sized-grid-b8f (ChangeLog claims GHC 9.8; base >=4.20 and tested-with
both say 9.10). Noticed because the new code uses Prelude's foldl', which is
base 4.20+ -- fine under the real bound, not under the claimed one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ixed and a 'cell' Lens' for GridOf: the one element access the class hierarchy is missing
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey. Verified against the tree, not guessed.

== Why

Grid already carries FunctorWithIndex, FoldableWithIndex and
TraversableWithIndex at Coord cs (Internal/Grid.hs:234-246) and is
Representable with Rep = Coord cs (Internal/Grid.hs:217). The one thing a
consumer cannot do is focus a single cell. There is no single-cell update
function anywhere in the public API either: the export list of
Data.Grid.Sized has gridFromVector, mapGrid, imapGrid, zipWithGrid and so on,
but nothing that writes one coordinate. Today that costs an imap over the
whole grid with an equality test per cell.

== What to add

  type instance Index   (GridOf v cs a) = Coord cs
  type instance IxValue (GridOf v cs a) = a
  instance (VG.Vector v a, IsCoordList cs) => Ixed (GridOf v cs a)

Note the instance head: GridOf, not Grid. indexGrid is already written at
GridOf with a VG.Vector constraint (Internal/Grid.hs:138), so the unboxed
grids in Data.Grid.Sized.Unboxed get this for the same code. Do not narrow it
to the boxed Grid.

Alongside it, export the honest optic:

  cell :: (VG.Vector v a, IsCoordList cs) => Coord cs -> Lens' (GridOf v cs a) a

lens fixes ix :: Index m -> Traversal' m (IxValue m) (confirmed in
lens-5.3.6, Control.Lens.At), which throws away the fact that here it can
never miss: every Coord cs indexes a cell by construction, so this is a
genuine Lens'. 'ix' is what the class demands and what generic code calls;
'cell' is what a consumer should reach for, and only the exported Lens' lets
them use it as a getter without a Monoid.

== Do NOT add At, and do not add Contains

At implies insert and delete, which a fixed shape cannot do. lens's own
Haddock for At says it outright: "Map-like containers form a reasonable
instance, but not Array-like ones, where you cannot satisfy the Lens laws."

Contains is the same mistake in the other direction: contains :: Index m ->
Lens' m Bool would have to be a constant-True getter with no lawful setter.

== Cost

None. lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Implemented Ixed and cell Lens' for GridOf, with focused getter/setter tests; full grid-sized test suite passes.

title: Neighbourhood decomposition: split a window into focus and neighbours
description:
Prior art: Chris Penner's 'grids' has

  partitionFocus :: (Centered window, IsGrid window)
                 => Grid window a -> (a, Grid window (Maybe a))

splitting a window into its centre value and the same window with a hole where
the centre was. That is the shape Conway actually wants -- the rule is a
function of the cell AND its neighbours, and today a caller of 'neighbours'
has to carry the centre separately or re-index for it.

WHAT IT IS, precisely. Not a comonad. Grid window is Representable over
Coord window, and 'Centered window' names a basepoint c0, so the honest
statement is the splitting of a representable functor over a pointed index:

  (I -> a)  ~=  a * (I \ {i0} -> a)

The Maybe encodes the puncture in place rather than in the index type.

It IS the shape of a cofree-comonad step, though. For any comonad w,
'extract &&& duplicate' has type 'w a -> (a, w (w a))', which is one unfolding
of 'Cofree w a = a :< w (Cofree w a)'. partitionFocus is that shape with the
recursive position truncated to 'Maybe a': it keeps the values and marks the
hole instead of recursing. So it is a shadow of Store, which this library
already has via FocusedGrid's ComonadStore instance -- worth knowing so we do
not reinvent a comonad we already own.

DESIGN NOTE, and the reason not to copy it verbatim. The codomain
'(a, Grid window (Maybe a))' is strictly larger than the thing it represents:
it admits Nothing at any cell and Just at the centre, neither of which the
function can produce. The type does not say where the hole is. That is the
same species of imprecision the boundary thesis rejects -- the type should
say it, not the documentation.

Options for our version, to be decided when this is picked up:
  (a) a punctured coordinate type, so the hole lives in the index and the
      Maybe disappears;
  (b) return the neighbours as a sized vector of length 'Size window - 1',
      which is precise and cheap but discards the window's shape;
  (c) keep the shape and accept the Maybe, documenting the invariant --
      cheapest, and the option the thesis argues against.

Wants the odd-extent precondition to be expressible with a readable error,
which is sized-grid-0kq.
close_reason: Implemented as option (a), PuncturedCoord cs: a newtype over Ordinal (MaxCoordSize cs - 1), the punctured-coordinate index type. puncturedToCoord :: PuncturedCoord cs -> Coord cs is total (skips centreCoord's flat position). allPunctured enumerates them in allCoord order minus the centre. partitionFocus :: Grid cs a -> (a, PuncturedCoord cs -> a) in Focused.hs, per user's choice of the function-returning form. The 1<=MaxCoordSize cs proof needed for KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs - 1) is recovered at runtime via cmpNat, mirroring reifyOrdinal's own pattern, kept private (coordSpaceNonEmpty, unexported). Tests added in Test/Neighbours.hs and Test/Focused.hs; full suite (424 tests) and gameOfLife/ising-example/sudoko all build clean.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Follow-on from the comonad question, and a trap to avoid.

There IS a comonad structure available on Grid window without asking for it.
Grid window is Representable over Coord window, and for any MONOID m the
functor (m -> a) is the Traced comonad:

  extract f   = f mempty
  duplicate f = \i j -> f (i <> j)

Coord cs is a Monoid whenever every axis is, and both Clamped and Periodic are.
So the instance would typecheck today.

Do not add it blind. On Periodic axes it is sound: Periodic is a group, (<>) is
modular addition, and the comonad laws hold on the nose. On Clamped axes (<>)
is SATURATING addition, so duplicate composes offsets by clamping -- meaning
'move right 3, then right 3' and 'move right 6' agree near an edge when they
should not, and the comonad's own associativity is doing the silent clamping
the boundary thesis exists to forbid. The structure would be well-typed and
quietly wrong, which is the worst failure mode this library has.

If a Traced-style instance is ever wanted, it belongs behind a constraint that
admits only axes whose monoid is a group -- i.e. Periodic, and whatever later
axis types satisfy it -- not 'All Monoid cs'. Ordinal has no Monoid at all and
is fine by construction.

Recorded here rather than as its own issue because it is a decision not to
build something; promote it if someone proposes the instance.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Precision fix to the previous comment, which understated the problem.

Saturating addition on [0, n-1] IS associative, so Clamped's Monoid is lawful,
and the Traced comonad laws that follow from it hold on the nose. Nothing would
fail. A law-checking test suite would pass.

That makes the case against the instance stronger, not weaker: it would be
lawful AND semantically wrong for this library. duplicate composes displacements
by clamping, so near an edge 'right 3 then right 3' equals 'right 6' -- the
distinction between a move that fit and one that did not is erased by the
comonad's own composition, and no law says otherwise.

This is the sharpest example so far of why the thesis is stated in terms of what
the library refuses rather than what it proves: lawfulness does not imply the
boundary is being respected. Worth putting in the README if the thesis section
is ever expanded with a worked example.

title: FromJSON (Grid cs a) does not validate length, silently builds a Grid whose vector is the wrong size
description:
CONFIRMED empirically.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:145-151

    instance (All IsCoordLifted cs, FromJSON a) => FromJSON (Grid cs a) where
      parseJSON v = case (shape :: Shape cs) of
        ShapeNil -> Grid . V.singleton <$> parseJSON v
        ShapeCons _ -> do
          a :: [Grid (Tail cs) a] <- parseJSON v
          return $ Grid $ foldMap unGrid a

Nothing checks that the outer list has exactly CoordNat (Head cs) elements.

Probe result:
    decode "[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]" :: Maybe (Grid '[Ordinal 3, Ordinal 3] Int)
    => Just, with unGrid length 6 (type promises 9)

The whole point of the library is that the type pins the size. A decoded Grid that
breaks the invariant makes every downstream operation unsound:
  - index/gridIndex do 'v V.! coordPosition c' -> out-of-bounds exception at runtime
  - Applicative (<*>) is V.zipWith -> silently truncates
  - collapseGrid produces a ragged result

Contrast with gridFromList (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:121-132), which DOES check
'length cg == natVal (Proxy @(CoordNat (Head cs)))' and returns Nothing. FromJSON
should reuse exactly that logic.

Note the constraints are also asymmetric: ToJSON needs AllGridSizeKnown + SListI,
FromJSON needs All IsCoordLifted. FromJSON needs the KnownNat evidence to validate,
so aligning them on AllGridSizeKnown is part of the fix.

Why the test suite misses it: aesonLaws only round-trips well-formed values.
Add a negative test decoding a short/long array and asserting Nothing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED. FromJSON now validates the length at every dimension and 'fail's otherwise, so a decoded Grid always satisfies the size invariant. Constraints aligned with ToJSON (AllGridSizeKnown cs, SListI cs), which is what supplies the KnownNat evidence needed to check.

Ragged input is rejected by the recursion: the outer list length is checked at each level. All three negative tests (too few rows / too many rows / ragged rows) now pass.

title: _FocusedGrid Iso and a focus Lens: the ComonadStore methods do not compose
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier A: an Iso, plus the field lenses
that should come with it.

  data FocusedGrid cs a = FocusedGrid
      { focusedGrid         :: Grid cs a
      , focusedGridPosition :: Coord cs
      }                                                  Focused.hs:26

A product of exactly two fields, both public, no invariant relating them --
every `Coord cs` is a valid focus by construction. So:

  _FocusedGrid :: Iso' (FocusedGrid cs a) (Grid cs a, Coord cs)
  _FocusedGrid = iso (\(FocusedGrid g p) -> (g, p)) (uncurry FocusedGrid)

  focus     :: Lens' (FocusedGrid cs a) (Coord cs)
  unfocused :: Lens (FocusedGrid cs a) (FocusedGrid cs b) (Grid cs a) (Grid cs b)

The two record accessors are already exported (`FocusedGrid(..)`,
Focused.hs:3), so the getters are free; the lenses add the setters, which
today have to be written as a record update.

`focus` is the interesting one. `ComonadStore` gives `pos`/`seek`/`seeks`
(Focused.hs:52-58) which is get/set/modify on exactly this field under three
names -- `focus` is the fourth, but it is the one that COMPOSES: `focus . _1`
moves along the first axis of the focus (Field1 for Coord already exists,
Coord.hs:351), and `over focus (.+^ d)` is a step. Neither is expressible
through the ComonadStore methods without naming an intermediate.

Do this issue together with the asFocusedGrid law bug, which is about the
same type and whose honest fix probably IS this Iso: a `Grid` has no focus to
store, so the conversion between the two cannot be a `Lens'` in that
direction, but it can be an Iso to a pair.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Fixed together: dropped the unlawful asFocusedGrid Lens from IsGrid, added _FocusedGrid/focus/unfocused to FocusedGrid, wired law tests. See commit c0bc2df.

title: ../aoc 2025/04 calls moorePoints, removed in 0.3.0.0
description:
../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:62 does not compile against sized-grid 0.3.0.0:

    neighs = experiment (filter (/= coord) . nubOrd . moorePoints 1) g

    src/2025/04.hs:62:55: error: [GHC-88464]
        Variable not in scope:
          moorePoints :: t0 -> Coord [Clamped n, Clamped n] -> [Coord [Clamped n, Clamped n]]

'moorePoints' was REMOVED in the 0.3.0.0 neighbourhood replacement (see ChangeLog).
Removal rather than deprecation was deliberate: the behaviour changed under an
otherwise compatible signature.

This call site is the exact idiom the ChangeLog migration note predicts -- it
works around both of the old API's defects at once, including the centre
('filter (/= coord)') and the duplicates the clamping '(.+^)' produced
('nubOrd'). The replacement does neither.

MIGRATION

    neighs = experiment neighbours g

'neighbours' is the Moore neighbourhood at radius one, already excluding the
centre and already duplicate-free. Both the 'filter' and the 'nubOrd' go. Check
whether 'nubOrd' (Data.Containers.ListUtils) is still used elsewhere in the file;
if not, drop the import or -Wall will flag it.

DISCOVERED how: type-checking aoc during sized-grid-7d1 (HardWrap -> Clamped).
This is NOT caused by that rename -- the rename diff to this file is purely the
type name, and the error names 'moorePoints'. Note the error text shows
'Coord [Clamped n, Clamped n]' resolving correctly.

SIBLING of sized-grid-bb5, which covers the OTHER pre-existing aoc breakage
(the sealed-Grid reach-through at 2018/11.hs:31). aoc needs both before it builds.

CANNOT BE VERIFIED BY 'cabal build' in this environment: aoc depends on
hmatrix-0.20.2, whose configure step fails with 'Missing (or bad) C libraries:
blas, lapack'. Type-check individual modules instead -- see the
sized-grid-aoc-cannot-be-cabal-built memory for the exact recipe.
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs type-checks against sized-grid 0.3.0.0 with no reference to moorePoints, and no unused-import warning.
notes:
RESOLVED, but NOT by the migration this issue prescribed. The prescribed 'experiment neighbours g' is behaviour-preserving -- verified -- but it preserves a BUG.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG

experiment f w = fmap (peek w) (f (pos w)), so the neighbourhood is centred on
'pos g', NOT on 'coord'. In forklift, 'pos g' is the parse-time focus (0,0) and
never moves, while 'coord' varies over every cell. So forklift inspected the
corner's neighbourhood for all 100 cells. On the example that region is
{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)} holding 2 Paper, so 'papers < 4' was always True and
forklift was degenerately constant.

Sibling call sites confirm the intended idiom: 2015/18.hs:51 and 2018/18.hs:67
both wrote 'filter (/= pos fg)', excluding the point experiment actually centres
on. 2025/04 wrote 'filter (/= coord)' -- a mis-adaptation.

PROVENANCE: it is a regression, with the original in git.
  d050263 (first commit): neighs = filter (/= coord) (nubOrd $ moorePoints 1 coord)
                          peek p g over that list -- centred on coord, CORRECT
                          doctest: '>>> solve example' == 13
  3278a32 ('2025 day 6'): refactored to experiment (...) g, which silently
                          re-centred on pos g, AND updated the doctest 13 -> 71
                          to match the newly-broken output. partTwo's 43 was
                          left alone and has been failing ever since.

MEASURED (probe against live 0.3.0.0, all four variants):
  doctest expects      solve=71  partTwo=43
  A current aoc code   solve=71  partTwo=71   <- partTwo already failing
  B this issue's fix   solve=71  partTwo=71   <- identical to A, bug preserved
  C centred on coord   solve=13  partTwo=43   <- both match d050263's originals

APPLIED (variant C):
  neighs = experiment neighbours (seek coord g)
