title: Retune the benchmark gate threshold once CI has run history
description:
sized-grid-adr.11 shipped the gate at --fail-if-slower 25, the value that issue proposed, with no CI data to set it from.

The one measurement taken is not reassuring. Same machine, same binary, same baseline CSV, aarch64-darwin/9.12.3: with an unrelated build running alongside, 17 of 48 benchmarks failed at 26-71% slower and the suite took 405s. Once the machine was quiet, none failed and it took 132s. The failures were not a property of the code -- they clustered in time and hit the small benchmarks hardest, where 'extract 50x50' is 10ns and one rescheduled thread is the whole measurement.

A GitHub shared runner is permanently in something like the first condition. If PRs start going red for reasons nobody can reproduce, the gate gets switched off, which is the failure mode sized-grid-adr.11 was explicitly trying to avoid.

After a few weeks of runs, look at the bench job's history and either tighten 25 (if the runner turns out steadier than feared) or raise it. The per-run CSVs are uploaded as artifacts on every run, pass or fail, so the spread is recoverable. If loosening the single global threshold would blunt it too much, note that tasty-bench takes FailIfSlower via localOption/adjustOption per benchmark or bgroup -- the nanosecond-scale ones could carry a looser bound than the millisecond-scale ones instead of everything moving together.

title: Seam rule: boundary resolution returns a coordinate AND a frame transform
description:
The unifying shape for every non-separable policy, from the Gemini transcript
and worth keeping because it is correct:

    type Policy = Coord -> (Coord, Needle -> Needle)

Resolving an out-of-range position returns the canonical in-range coordinate
AND a transform to apply to the walker's own direction. That second component
is the seam rule, and it is the whole content of the idea.

On a Mobius strip, crossing the seam an odd number of times flips the y axis.
The coordinate lands somewhere legal either way; what distinguishes Mobius from
a plain torus is that your notion of "up" is now different. A policy that
returns only a coordinate cannot express that.

WHAT THIS SUBSUMES

  Torus       -> (wrap c, id)
  Reflective  -> (bounce c, negate on the reflected axis)   <- note: bounce is
                 the one separable policy that STILL wants a frame transform,
                 because a billiard that hits a wall has reversed its velocity.
                 Today a caller re-decides that inline.
  Mobius      -> (wrap c, flip axis 1 when the x-wrap count is odd)
  Klein       -> same, both axes
  Projective  -> (antipode c, negate all axes)
  Atlas       -> (new tile + local coord, rotate the frame by a D4 element)

So the seam rule is the single generalisation that covers reflection, the
non-separable twists, and the multi-chart case. It is a better organising idea
than "another boundary policy".

RELATION TO EXISTING WORK

This is the same question sized-grid-448 (coord + heading) is blocked on, seen
from the other side. 448 asks "what happens to a heading at an edge"; this
asks "what does the edge do to the frame". They are one question, and the seam
rule is the answer: the policy returns the transform, and a walker carrying a
heading applies it.

That means 448 is not blocked on inventing a heading type. It is blocked on
this, plus the Needle-vs-Path representation question in the sibling issue.

OPEN QUESTIONS

  * Where does the transform live? An honest `Needle -> Needle` is a closure
    per step, which is exactly the kind of thing this library has spent five
    issues removing from the offset path. The integer affine matrix form the
    transcript suggests (`T(x) = Ax + b`, A unimodular) is closed under
    composition and finite, so a small enumerated type of frame elements --
    the signed-permutation group on n axes -- may be representable as a value
    with no closure at all. That is the design question.
  * Does the seam rule belong on the coord type at all, or only on the new
    atlas layer? Reflective suggests the former; Mobius forces the latter.
notes:
CORRECTION to this issue's policy table, found while building sized-grid-aqa (Klein) -- two of the six rows name the wrong surface:

  Klein -> 'same, both axes' is not a Klein bottle. Reflecting the sibling
  axis on BOTH edge-pairs is the projective plane's identification. A Klein
  bottle reflects exactly ONE pair: square model (x,0)~(x,1) together with
  (0,y)~(1,1-y). The Mobius row above it is right; Klein is Mobius plus a
  SECOND seam that glues straight through, not a second twisted one.

  Projective -> '(antipode c, negate all axes)' reads as an opposite-CORNER
  gluing, and sized-grid-aqa deferred the projective case on that reading.
  RP^2 as a square is the antipodal identification of the square's BOUNDARY,
  which is the both-edges-reversed table -- the one the Klein row was
  reaching for. Built as sized-grid-4nl.

The rest of the table stands, and the issue's actual thesis -- that a policy
must return a frame transform and not just a coordinate -- is unaffected;
both corrected rows still need one. Recording here because a closed issue
with a wrong table is what a later reader trusts.
close_reason: Axis-local case resolved and implemented: axisFrameFlipsIsCoord on IsCoord (Coord/Class.hs), lifted as axisFrameFlips (Coord.hs), wired into Reflective and Reflect101. Both open questions answered for this case (Bool representation at one axis; fits on IsCoord within the separable ceiling). Cross-axis case remains fh2/1bm's territory. Commit 07e7da0 on worktree-sized-grid-o1n.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
sized-grid-kvs landed: Reflective and Reflect101 are real code now
(src/Data/Grid/Sized/Coord/Reflective.hs, Coord/Reflect101.hs), not
transcript sketches. That makes the "bounce is the one separable policy
that STILL wants a frame transform" note above concrete rather than
speculative, exactly as kvs's closing note anticipated.

Concretely: Reflective's (.+^) (Reflective.hs, the AffineSpace instance)
computes the bounced position via the closed-form triangle wave and
returns only a Reflective n. Nothing in it reports whether a bounce off
a wall actually happened on this step, let alone which wall. A caller
simulating a billiard walker today has to re-derive that by comparing
axisBoundary before and after, or by re-implementing the reflection
predicate by hand -- exactly the "caller re-decides that inline" this
issue already flags.

This is now the concrete, non-hypothetical motivating case for the
Policy = Coord -> (Coord, Needle -> Needle) shape: Reflective 5 .+^ d
should be able to hand back (bounced coord, negate-on-this-axis) in one
call, with the frame half a no-op for every other axis type in the
library today (Clamped, Periodic, Reflect101 all only ever return id).

Not implemented as part of kvs -- that issue was scoped to the two
separable IsCoord instances alone, per its own "fit with the thesis"
section, and this issue's own open questions (where the transform lives,
closure vs. enumerated D4/signed-permutation representation) are still
unresolved. Filing this comment so the next pass at o1n has Reflective's
actual shape to design the seam rule against instead of the sketch.

title: Apply and Bind for Grid: not 'low value' -- they work where Applicative and Monad cannot
description:
From the sized-grid-90f survey, which listed these "for completeness" and
called them low value. That undersells them, and the reason is in the
constraints.

  instance AllSizedKnown cs                  => Applicative (Grid cs)  -- :203
  instance (AllSizedKnown cs, IsCoordList cs) => Monad (Grid cs)       -- :208

Applicative carries AllSizedKnown only because of pure, which has to
materialise a vector of the right length out of nothing. (<*>) is a zipWith
and needs none of it. Monad carries it only because its body goes through
Representable's index, whose instance context has it; indexGrid itself needs
only IsCoordList (Internal/Grid.hs:138).

So:

  instance IsCoordList cs => Apply (Grid cs) where (<.>) = zipWithGrid ($)
  instance IsCoordList cs => Bind (Grid cs) where
    g >>- f = imap (\p a -> indexGrid (f a) p) g

Both drop AllSizedKnown. That is a real capability, not a synonym: code that
is polymorphic in cs without KnownNat evidence on every axis can apply and
bind grids, and cannot use (<*>) or (>>=).

Write the Monad instance's (>>=) in terms of (>>-) afterwards so the two
cannot drift.

== Cost

None. semigroupoids is already in the build plan, pulled in by adjunctions and
lens, both already direct dependencies.
close_reason: Apply/Bind instances added for Grid, dropping AllSizedKnown; Monad's (>>=) defined via (>>-); semigroupoids added as a direct dependency; bindLaws hand-rolled test added (quickcheck-classes has applyLaws but no bindLaws); README and ChangeLog updated. All 650 tests pass.

title: aoc: drop KnownNat (n * n) from the five parse signatures
description:
sized-grid-k6n removed the constraint leak at the source. The five downstream signatures that were written around it can now lose it, but they are in ../aoc and were not touched by that change, so they still say it:

    ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:32  parse  :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31  parse  :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2024/04.hs:48  parser :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2017/19.hs:35  parse  :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2018/18.hs:36  parse  :: (KnownNat n, 1 <= n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...

Each should become 'KnownNat n' alone (2018/18 keeps its '1 <= n', which comes from IsCoordList and not from this leak). Some also import GHC.TypeLits qualified as GHC only for the '*'; that import goes too.

aoc's cabal.project has 'packages: . ../sized-grid', so it builds against the working tree -- the change has to land in sized-grid first, which it has. Expect -Wredundant-constraints to point at each one once it does.
close_reason: Already fixed in ../aoc commit d8e97e4 ('cleanup'), which dropped the KnownNat (n GHC.* n) constraint and the qualified GHC.TypeLits/TypeNats import from all five signatures (2025/04.hs, 2015/18.hs, 2024/04.hs, 2017/19.hs, 2018/18.hs). 2018/18.hs correctly kept its '1 <= n'. Verified: grep for 'n GHC.*' / 'KnownNat (n' across the five files returns nothing, and 4 of 5 executables build clean under nix develop -c cabal build with no redundant-constraints warnings. aoc-2017-19 fails to build for an unrelated reason -- a new exported Path type from sized-grid's Coord module collides with aoc's own local Path -- filed as sized-grid-vpr, out of scope here since the diff in that file is textually identical to the other four. Also confirmed sized-grid-0ao (corners hoist) is committed as d38cf1b on aoc main, main is FF-equal with origin/main, working tree clean.

title: [minBound ..] on an Ordinal throws Maybe.fromJust: Nothing
description:
Ordinal's Enum instance defined only toEnum and fromEnum, inheriting the class
defaults for enumFrom and enumFromThen. Those defaults count up from
'fromEnum x' with no upper bound and call toEnum on each element, and Ordinal's
toEnum was 'fromJust . numToOrdinal'. So the list walked one past maxBound and
died:

    [minBound ..]        :: [Ordinal 5]   -- Maybe.fromJust: Nothing
    [maxBound, toEnum 3 ..] :: [Ordinal 5]   -- likewise, past minBound

HardWrap derives Enum from Ordinal, so it inherited the crash. The bounded
enumFromTo used everywhere in the library ('allCoordLike' uses
[minBound .. maxBound]) was never affected, which is why it went unnoticed.

The fix is the standard Bounded/Enum idiom: enumFrom stops at maxBound, and
enumFromThen picks maxBound or minBound depending on the direction of travel.
Both were defined directly over Int in the same change, which also skips the
per-element range check.

Found while rewriting Ordinal for sized-grid-upo.
acceptance_criteria: [minBound ..] and [minBound, x ..] terminate at the bound for Ordinal and HardWrap. Regression test in tests/Test/Ordinal.hs.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 'Make Ordinal a newtype over Int' on branch worktree-ordinal-int; 100 tests pass, zero warnings

title: GH Actions nix store cache never restores (tar permission errors against /nix/store)
description: flake-check's nix-community/cache-nix-action@v6 restore step fails every run with tar errors against /nix/store: 'Cannot open: Permission denied' on an existing .drv, 'Cannot utime: Operation not permitted' and 'Cannot change mode to rwxr-xr-t: Operation not permitted' on /nix/store itself. Cache restore aborts and flake-check falls back to a full rebuild every time (29m44s observed), which is presumably why the cache never appears to help. Observed on run 32308245970 (and repeats on other recent runs). Both actions are pinned well behind current: cachix/install-nix-action@v27 (latest is v31.11.1) and nix-community/cache-nix-action@v6 (latest is v7.0.2). First attempt: bump both to current majors and watch the next run -- not verified locally, this is a GH-runner-only failure mode.

Next real push's flake-check run is the actual restore test; watch for a fast (cached) run rather than another ~30min full rebuild.

title: ShrinkableGrid window constraint had x and y transposed
description:
Found while fixing sized-grid-2h0, and fixed in the same change.

src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs, instance ShrinkableGrid (c x ': cs) (c y ': as) (c z ': bs)
carried the constraint:

    z <= (x - y + 1)

where x is the number of window positions, y the source size and z the window size.
The correct relation is that a window of z at any of the x offsets must fit in y:

    (x - 1) + z <= y     i.e.   x + z <= y + 1     i.e.   z <= y - x + 1

so x and y were the wrong way round.

Why it was never noticed: the only test (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) uses x == y == 3, where
both readings collapse to 'z <= 1'. The honest case of windowing a 5-grid into three
positions of 3 (x=3, y=5, z=3) was REJECTED by the old constraint: 3 - 5 truncates to 0
in Nat, giving 'z <= 1'.

FIXED: constraint restated as 'x + z <= y + 1'. Stating it as an addition rather than a
truncating Nat subtraction also keeps it in reach of the solver.

The two remaining obligations inside 'helper' (n <= y and z <= y - n, where n is the
existential offset from asSizeProxy with n + 1 <= x) follow by linear arithmetic but
mention a truncating subtraction over an existential, which GHC cannot discharge.
ghc-typelits-natnormalise was tried and did NOT help (it does not use given <= premises
to discharge wanted <= goals), and its ghc-tcplugins-extra dependency caps at GHC <9.13,
which broke the 9.14 build. So the plugins were dropped and the facts are asserted in
SizedGrid.Internal.Type.windowFits, in the same style as the existing takeAddIsId.
Soundness rests on the instance constraint, which IS checked at every call site.

FOLLOW-UP: tests/Test/Shrink.hs still only covers x == y == 3. Add a discriminating
case (x=3, y=5, z=3) that would have caught the transposition.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
FIXED in the same change as sized-grid-2h0. Constraint restated as 'x + z <= y + 1'.

The follow-up named in the description is DONE: tests/Test/Shrink.hs now has the discriminating case (x=3 positions, y=5 source, z=3 window) at all three offsets, which the old transposed constraint rejected at compile time. Suite is 80 tests, all passing on GHC 9.12.3 and 9.14.1.

title: _GridVector: gridVector/gridFromVector as a type-changing Prism
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier B: a genuine Prism, and one of
the few places the whole safe-construction story is currently two functions
the consumer has to know to pair up.

  gridVector     :: GridOf v cs a -> v a                          Internal/Grid.hs:109
  gridFromVector :: (VG.Vector v a, AllSizedKnown cs)
                 => v a -> Maybe (GridOf v cs a)                  Internal/Grid.hs:113

`gridFromVector` checks `VG.length v == MaxCoordSize cs` and nothing else, so
this is exactly a refinement of `v a` and the pair is a lawful Prism:

  _GridVector :: (VG.Vector v a, AllSizedKnown cs)
              => Prism' (v a) (GridOf v cs a)
  _GridVector = prism' gridVector gridFromVector

Laws: `gridFromVector (gridVector g) = Just g` holds by GridOf's own size
invariant; the other direction is `Just (Grid v)` on the nose.

Consider the type-changing version instead, which is strictly more useful and
costs nothing:

  _GridVector :: (VG.Vector v a, VG.Vector v b, AllSizedKnown cs)
              => Prism (v a) (v b) (GridOf v cs a) (GridOf v cs b)

That gives `over _GridVector (mapGrid f)` on a raw vector, which is the
shape most consumers reaching for this actually want.

Do NOT build the Prism on `unsafeGridFromVector` (Internal/Grid.hs:104). It
lives in Data.Grid.Sized.Unsafe for a reason and a Prism made from it would
be unlawful in the interesting direction (it would accept the wrong length
and produce a grid whose `indexGrid` reads past the end).

The unboxed wrapper `ugridFromVector` (Unboxed.hs:44) is `gridFromVector` at
`U.Vector`, so it gets the Prism for free at that instantiation and needs no
separate optic -- but the Unboxed module's export list should say so, since
its whole premise is that the shared operations come from Data.Grid.Sized.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Implemented the requested lawful optics, renamed _WrappedCoord to _CoordAxes, and validated tests.

title: The torus displacement group: Coord cs is a torsor over a finite abelian group when every axis is Boundaryless
description:
Fell out of the sized-grid-adr.16 design discussion, where the displacement type is being split out of Coord.

When every axis is Boundaryless (today: every axis Periodic), Coord cs is a
torsor over a genuine finite abelian group -- Z/n1 x ... x Z/nk. That group is
bounded, shape-dependent, and the library has no type for it.

Diff (Coord cs) deliberately does NOT become that group. adr.16 settled that
the difference space is shared and shape-free: Coord '[Clamped 3, Clamped 3]
and Coord '[Clamped 5, Clamped 5] have the same difference space, Z^2, and
Delta is indexed by the diff list to say so. The reason it cannot be the
quotient is Clamped: from position 0 on Clamped 5, +100 and +5 both land at 4,
but that is not a subgroup kernel -- it depends on the origin -- so there is no
uniform normal form across a mixed-policy coord like '[Clamped 5, Periodic 3],
and mixed policies are the library's thesis.

Restricted to All Boundaryless cs, though, the quotient IS well defined and is
exactly what the axis types already compute: Periodic's AdditiveGroup reduces
mod n and its (.-.) returns (a - b) `mod` n. So the group exists in the
arithmetic already; what is missing is a type that names it.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY

  * Extensional equality. Today d2 1 0 and d2 6 0 are distinct Delta values
    that act identically on a Periodic 5 axis, so pathOffset p == pathOffset q
    can be False for observationally equal paths. In the quotient they are
    equal.
  * A finite type. Like PuncturedCoord and unlike Delta, it is bounded, so it
    can be a flat position -- and after adr.16 so is Coord, which makes the
    action close to free.
  * Bounded/Enum/Finitary. Directly relevant to sized-grid-8ni, which wants
    Finitary (Coord cs) and is already blocked on adr.16; the same instance
    story covers this group.

SHAPE, roughly: its own type alongside PuncturedCoord rather than a change to
Diff, carrying the All Boundaryless cs constraint, with the torsor action
(.+^)-shaped and a conversion to and from Delta. Whether it is a flat Int (the
adr.16 representation, since it is bounded by MaxCoordSize cs) or an NP of
per-axis Ordinals is the first thing to settle -- flat is the obvious answer if
the action is to be free.

DO NOT START before adr.16 lands: it depends on both the Delta split and the
flat Coord representation.
close_reason: Closed

title: AllGridSizeKnown is a type family, so KnownNat (n*n) leaks into every consumer signature
description:
Split out of sized-grid-cpw bullet 4, with the mechanism now identified.

The library has two ways of saying 'the sizes are known' and they behave very
differently for users:

  - AllSizedKnown (src/SizedGrid/Coord.hs:294-302) is a CLASS whose instance chain is
    '(KnownNat n, AllSizedKnown as) => AllSizedKnown (c n ': as)'. GHC discharges it by
    instance resolution from 'KnownNat n' alone, and the total-size fact is handed back
    at the value level as 'sizeProof :: Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))'. Callers pay
    nothing: ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:38 gets Comonad on a FocusedGrid with only
    '(KnownNat n, 1 <= n)'.

  - AllGridSizeKnown (src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs:92-97) is a TYPE FAMILY that expands to
    a conjunction of KnownNat constraints, including 'KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs)'. A type
    family cannot be discharged by instance resolution, so the whole expansion lands in
    the user's context.

That is the direct cause of the impact measured in cpw:

    ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs:33  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...
    ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs:31  parse :: (KnownNat n, KnownNat (n GHC.* n)) => ...

Both signatures carry 'KnownNat (n * n)' purely because gridFromList is constrained by
AllGridSizeKnown rather than by AllSizedKnown. Compare the FocusedGrid signatures a few
lines below in the same files, which need nothing of the sort.

Affected API: collapseGrid, gridFromList, and the ToJSON/FromJSON instances for Grid
(Grid.hs:109, :123, :135, :153).

TWO POSSIBLE FIXES, and they should be evaluated in this order:

1. Do sized-grid-h56 first. ghc-typelits-knownnat derives 'KnownNat (n * m)' from
   'KnownNat n, KnownNat m' automatically, which makes the leaked constraint solvable
   at the call site and may make this issue disappear without touching the API.

2. If it does not, convert AllGridSizeKnown from a type family to a class in the shape
   of AllSizedKnown. The obstacle is that the four call sites recurse structurally over
   'Shape cs', and from a dictionary for 'AllGridSizeKnown (x ': xs)' there is no way to
   recover 'AllGridSizeKnown xs' -- a class dictionary cannot be run backwards through
   its own instance context. So the class would need to carry the tail's evidence
   explicitly, e.g. a method returning 'Dict (AllGridSizeKnown (Tail cs))' alongside the
   KnownNat proof. Note 'All IsCoordLifted cs' already supplies
   'KnownNat (CoordNat (Head cs))' via IsCoordLifted's superclasses, so only the
   MaxCoordSize half actually needs new machinery.
design: Prefer waiting on sized-grid-h56: a plugin fix costs one cabal line and no API churn, while the class conversion changes four exported signatures and needs new Dict plumbing. Only take option 2 if the plugins are rejected or turn out not to discharge KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs).
acceptance_criteria: ../aoc/src/2025/04.hs and ../aoc/src/2015/18.hs can drop 'KnownNat (n GHC.* n)' from their parse signatures and still compile.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:

Hackage at all (0.5 is capped at 'ghc < 9.13'), so natnormalise and knownnat cannot be

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text: Related: sized-grid-4xh proposes dissolving AllSizedKnown into a function (sizeProof :: All IsCoordLifted cs => Dict (KnownNat (MaxCoordSize cs))), on the grounds that All IsCoordLifted already determines the total size. That is in tension with option 2 above, which proposes converting AllGridSizeKnown INTO the shape of AllSizedKnown. Decide the direction once, for both classes, before implementing either. Not filed as a blocking dependency because option 1 (the plugin route) may still resolve this issue without touching either class.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Superseded by sized-grid-k6n, which is closed. Same defect, filed twice: qh9 (2026-08-10) diagnosed it against src/SizedGrid/Grid/Grid.hs before that code moved to Internal/Grid.hs; k6n (2026-08-12) re-filed it after establishing that option 1 here -- 'do sized-grid-h56 first, the plugins may make it disappear' -- cannot work, because -fplugin is not transitive.

qh9's option 2 is what was built, including its prediction of the obstacle: the class carries the tail's evidence explicitly, since a dictionary cannot be run backwards through its own instance context. It carries it as a GridSizeProof GADT rather than a Dict, which also subsumes the SListI/Shape nil-or-cons match, so those four signatures lost that constraint too.

qh9's acceptance criterion is met in substance and checked more strictly than it asked: a plugin-free 'downstream' test suite in this repo compiles the same signatures at the same axis list with KnownNat n alone, and fails to compile against the old family. The literal edit to ../aoc's five signatures is sized-grid-oxb.

title: _WrappedCoord's name has lied since adr.16; and the Wrapped-class decision
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Naming hygiene, with a decision
attached.

== _WrappedCoord's name has lied since adr.16

  _WrappedCoord :: forall cs. IsCoordList cs => Iso' (Coord cs) (NP I cs)
  _WrappedCoord = iso unCoord (Coord . npToPosition @cs)        Coord.hs:233

The name says "Coord is a wrapper around an NP I cs". It was, once. After
sized-grid-adr.16 a `Coord` is a flat `Int` and `unCoord` is no longer a
field accessor -- its own Haddock says so: "Was a field accessor. It costs
one quotRem per axis now" (Coord.hs:170-175).

So `_WrappedCoord` is a genuine Iso between two things of different shapes
and different costs, presented under a name whose whole connotation is that
it is free. A caller who reads `_WrappedCoord` as a coerce will put it in a
loop.

Rename to something that says what it is -- `_CoordAxes`, `axiswise`,
`_Unpacked` -- and say in the Haddock what it costs, pointing at the same
adr.16 measurement `unCoord` already cites. Keep the old name as a deprecated
alias for one release if the package has any external users yet; it is
pre-1.0 and unreleased under this name, so it may not need one.

`_WrappedDelta :: Iso' (Delta ds) (NP I ds)` (Delta.hs:113) is NOT affected:
`Delta` really is `newtype Delta ds = Delta { unDelta :: NP I ds }`
(Delta.hs:87), the Iso really is a coerce, and the name is accurate. Leave
it. (It is also spelled `dimap unDelta (fmap Delta)` rather than `iso`, which
is the same thing; unify the spelling with `_WrappedCoord`'s while touching
these.)

== The decision: do NOT instantiate lens's `Wrapped` class for Coord

`Wrapped s` with `Unwrapped (Coord cs) = NP I cs` would be a lawful Iso --
the class's stated law is only that `_Wrapped'` is an Iso. But the class's
entire convention, and what every consumer assumes on seeing it, is that it
is the newtype's own coercion. Instantiating it for a type that stopped being
that newtype is how the cost gets hidden again under a different name.

DO consider `Wrapped` for the types where it is honest and currently missing:
`Delta` (newtype over `NP I ds`), `Path` (newtype over
`[Diff (Coord cs)]`, Coord.hs:579), `Ordinal` (newtype over `Int`, but see
the caveat below), and the four axis types.

`Ordinal` needs care: `Wrapped (Ordinal m)` with `Unwrapped = Int` hands out
`review _Wrapped' :: Int -> Ordinal m` with no range check -- i.e. it
re-exports `unsafeOrdinalUnchecked` (Ordinal.hs:138) under a safe-looking
name, defeating the `type role Ordinal nominal` annotation that exists
specifically to stop `coerce` forging one (Ordinal.hs:40-41). Either skip
`Ordinal` or accept that and say why. The safe optic for Ordinal already
exists and is `_Ordinal :: Prism' a (Ordinal n)` (Ordinal.hs:205).
close_reason: Implemented the requested lawful optics, renamed _WrappedCoord to _CoordAxes, and validated tests.

title: gridTiles is a lawful Traversal; gridWindows is a Fold and must never be a Traversal
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier C, and the sharpest correctness
point in it: these two functions have the same type and CANNOT have the same
optic.

  gridTiles   :: (VG.Vector v a, KnownNat (MaxCoordSize (small ': rest)),
                  CoordNat big `Mod` CoordNat small ~ 0)
              => GridOf v (big ': rest) a -> [GridOf v (small ': rest) a]   Internal/Grid.hs:891

  gridWindows :: (VG.Vector v a, AllSizedKnown rest, KnownNat (CoordNat small),
                  CoordNat small <= CoordNat big)
              => GridOf v (big ': rest) a -> [GridOf v (small ': rest) a]   Internal/Grid.hs:931

== gridTiles is a lawful Traversal'

The `Mod ~ 0` constraint is exactly the statement that the tiles are disjoint
and exactly partition the grid -- the body is `map Grid . splitVectorBySize`
(Internal/Grid.hs:901) with no overlap and no remainder. Disjoint, covering
foci is the precondition for a lawful Traversal, so:

  tiles :: (...) => Traversal' (GridOf v (big ': rest) a) (GridOf v (small ': rest) a)

Needs the write-back half written -- concat the modified tiles in order --
which is `mapLowerDim`-shaped and should share its implementation if the
sizes let it.

== gridWindows is a Fold and MUST NOT be a Traversal

Its own Haddock (Internal/Grid.hs:904-907) says it: an `Ordinal 9` axis
windowed by `Ordinal 3` gives seven OVERLAPPING windows, 0..2, 1..3, ..., 6..8.
Cell 2 is in three of them.

A Traversal's foci must be disjoint. Setting through overlapping foci is not
well defined -- `over windows f` would have to decide which of the three
writes to cell 2 wins, and whichever it picked, the Traversal composition law
would fail (`over l f . over l g /= over l (f . g)`). So the only lawful
optic here is read-only:

  windows :: (...) => Fold (GridOf v (big ': rest) a) (GridOf v (small ': rest) a)
  windows = folding gridWindows

This asymmetry is the whole value of doing the two together: shipping them as
`Traversal'` and `Fold` states in the types the difference the Haddock
currently has to explain in prose, and makes the unlawful thing unwritable
rather than merely discouraged.

Do NOT be tempted by a Traversal for windows on the grounds that "the caller
knows what they mean". The failure is silent -- wrong values, not a type
error -- which is the one failure mode this library's whole thesis is
organised against.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Added tiles :: Traversal' and windows :: Fold as lawful optics over gridTiles/gridWindows; shared chunking engine with mapLowerDim via traverseChunks; added property tests for the Traversal laws and Fold agreement

title: Remaining property-test gaps: Comonad/Representable/Distributive laws and O(n^2) Arbitrary
description:
Split out of sized-grid-6jd so the baseline issue can close. The baseline's blocking purpose -- write failing tests before the fixes -- is done: the three defects it gated (sized-grid-0kf, sized-grid-miz, sized-grid-2h0) each had a red test first and are now green.

Still outstanding from the original gap analysis:

    fmap extract . duplicate == id, duplicate . duplicate == fmap duplicate . duplicate).
  - No Representable law test (tabulate . index == id) beyond the 2D case in
    tests/Main.hs:81-82.
  - No Distributive law test.
  - shrinkGrid now has four example-based tests (tests/Test/Shrink.hs) but still no
    properties -- e.g. 'shrinkGrid at offset n == the n-th window' over arbitrary
    offsets and sizes.
  - tests/Main.hs:34-38 defines Arbitrary via 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])',
    which builds the entire domain for each sample: fine at size 10, quadratic at 300.

Also worth adding now that the size invariant is enforced: extend the Test.Invariant

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text:
Done on branch worktree-ryy-property-tests. 283 -> 315 tests, all passing; 'cabal build all --enable-tests --enable-benchmarks' exits 0 and both test suites (tests, readme) pass.

Every bullet is covered:

  - Comonad laws for FocusedGrid: all three, in Test.Utils.comonadLaws, run over
    '[Periodic 3, Periodic 3]' and '[Clamped 2, Periodic 3]'. Coassociativity builds a
    grid of grids of grids, so the sizes are deliberately small -- cubed cell count.
  - Representable: 'tabulate . index == id' (the direction with the payload in it; the
    existing 'index (tabulate id) c == c' compares coordinates, so a tabulate that filled
    the vector in the wrong order still passed it), plus 'index . tabulate == id' and an
    fmap/representation coherence law. Run at 2D and at 3D.
  - Distributive: four laws, incl. 'distribute . distribute == id' (a transpose done
    twice) and 'collect f == distribute . fmap f'. Run at 2D and 3D.
  - shrinkGrid properties: a 1D 'window at offset n == take 3 . drop n' and a 2D
    'window at (i,j) == the 2x2 submatrix'. The 2D one uses a 4x4 source, 2x2 window and
    3x3 offsets so the axes carry different numbers and a transposed index cannot pass by
    coincidence -- the shape the old 'z <= x - y + 1' constraint was wrong for.
  - Arbitrary: 'oneof (map pure [minBound .. maxBound])' is gone. Test.Arbitrary.genOrdinal
    is 'unsafeOrdinal <$> chooseInt (0, ordinalToNum maxBound)' -- constant time, same
    uniform distribution. Deviation from the issue text: unsafeOrdinal rather than
    numToOrdinal, because chooseInt has already established the precondition and
    unsafeOrdinal's assert re-checks it in unoptimised builds anyway; it avoids a Maybe
    that cannot be Nothing. Suite still runs in 0.35s (was 0.23s).
  - Size invariant extended to the whole shape-changing API: splitGrid (outer and
    sub-grids), combineGrid, combineHigherDim, splitHigherDim, mapLowerDim, gridTiles,
    zipLowerDim, transposeGrid, shrinkGrid.

ENABLING LIBRARY CHANGE: FocusedGrid had neither Eq nor Show, so its Comonad laws could
not be written down at all. Added both as derived instances (equality is on grid AND
focus -- an Eq that ignored the focus would pass the laws without checking it) and
recorded in ChangeLog 0.3.0.0. 'comonad' and 'distributive' added to the tests stanza.

THE TESTS WERE MUTATION-CHECKED, not just observed green:
  1. duplicate := 'FocusedGrid (tabulate (const (FocusedGrid g p))) p'
     -> ONLY 'fmap extract . duplicate == id' failed. Nothing else in the suite caught it,
        which is the gap this issue was about.
  2. combineHigherDim := 'Grid v1' (drop the second operand)
     -> the new 'combineHigherDim sums the outer axis' failed, alongside two pre-existing.
  3. axes swapped in the 2D window property
     -> that property failed alone, confirming it is genuinely orientation-sensitive.
Each mutation was reverted and the suite re-run green.

comments.author: Kevin Horlick
comments.text: Follow-up filed: sized-grid-05b, the quickcheck-classes evaluation. Short version for anyone reading this issue later -- quickcheck-classes ships no Comonad, Representable or Distributive laws, so nothing in this issue was reinventable. What it would add is the base-class coverage Grid never had (Functor, Foldable, Traversable, Monad), prototyped at +32 passing laws for three new dependencies.

title: _Position: coordPosition/coordFromPosition is a Prism, not the Iso the premise assumed
description:
From the sized-grid-31z optics survey. Tier B, and the direct answer to the
question the survey started from.

The premise was "npToPosition <-> npFromPosition can just be a lens Iso". At
`Coord` that Iso already exists -- `_WrappedCoord = iso unCoord (Coord .
npToPosition)` (Coord.hs:233-234). At `Int` it is NOT an Iso, and that is
what is missing:

  npFromPosition :: Int -> NP I cs                       Coord/Class.hs:343

is unchecked. An out-of-range `Int` is decoded through `unsafeFromAxisIndex`
(Coord/Class.hs:441) and produces an out-of-range axis value -- a forged
coordinate, the same class of hole `unsafeCoordFromPosition` documents at
Coord.hs:524. `Int` is strictly larger than `[0, MaxCoordSize cs)`, so the
honest optic is a Prism, and both halves already exist checked:

  coordPosition     :: Coord cs -> Int                       Coord.hs:288
  coordFromPosition :: IsCoordList cs => Int -> Maybe (Coord cs)  Coord.hs:498

  _Position :: IsCoordList cs => Prism' Int (Coord cs)
  _Position = prism' coordPosition coordFromPosition

Laws, checked by hand:
  * `coordFromPosition (coordPosition c) = Just c` -- holds, coordPosition is
    the identity on the representation after adr.16 and the range check
    cannot fail on a real Coord.
  * `coordFromPosition p = Just c  ==>  coordPosition c = p` -- holds, the
    successful branch is `Just (Coord p)`.

This is deliberately the same shape as `_Ordinal :: Prism' a (Ordinal n)`
(Ordinal.hs:205), which is `prism' ordinalToNum numToOrdinal` -- the
coordinate-level analogue of an optic the library already ships. Follow that
precedent including the `Integral a` generalisation if it costs nothing:
`Prism' a (Coord cs)` for `Integral a` needs the same via-Integer care
numToOrdinal takes (Ordinal.hs:145) to stop a wrapping conversion turning an
out-of-range input into an in-range one.

What it buys a consumer: `v ^? ix i . _Position` style chains from a raw
index out of a vector or a parser, without the `maybe` plumbing.

Cost: none, lens is already a direct dependency.
close_reason: Implemented the requested lawful optics, renamed _WrappedCoord to _CoordAxes, and validated tests.

title: flake-check nix cache GCs away GHC toolchain, defeating the cache
description:
ci.yml's flake-check job caches the nix store via nix-community/cache-nix-action@v6 with gc-max-store-size-linux: 6G. Observed in run 32211552551 (job 95945073977, 2026-08-19T03:16-03:46Z): the post-job GC step ran `nix store gc --max 3545285184` -- that's ~3.3 GiB, not 6 GiB -- and deleted 1084 store paths (4196.55 MiB freed) to get under it, including /nix/store/p1z5mbyw9a5wm65f5b90qkp1hkbi90ml-ghc-9.12.3 (the compiler itself) and the whole haskell-language-server/devShell closure (hls, ormolu, hlint, stylish-haskell, etc).

The cache save afterward (875MB compressed, uploaded fine) therefore does not include GHC. The very next run that restores this cache (32213722072, started 03:53) shows the cache-nix-action restore step taking ~27s (vs <1s on a genuine cache-miss), i.e. it does find and restore something, but `nix flake check` is still rebuilding practically everything -- consistent with GHC having been evicted from what got cached.

Net effect: the cache exists and "works" (restores, saves, no errors) but doesn't actually save time, because the GC step throws away the one thing (the compiler) that makes the rest of the closure reusable.

Likely fix: gc-max-store-size-linux's unit/interpretation doesn't match the "6G" intent (check whether the action wants bytes, KB, or a different multiplier -- 3545285184 bytes is neither 6*1024^3 nor 6e9). Either correct the value so GHC + the checked components' closure actually fits, or split what's kept (e.g. don't cache the full devShell/HLS closure, which is large and not needed for `nix flake check`, and reserve the space for GHC + the build/check closure).

Evidence lives in job logs 95945073977 (save+gc) and 95951213881 (next restore, still rebuilding).
notes: Follow-up (still 2026-08-19): first fix attempt (00e6a2e) broke CI outright -- nix flake check --no-build fails on callCabal2nix's IFD before even reaching devShells. Fixed in 28418c3 by building the checks derivations first (realizes the IFD) then running --no-build after. Run 32215689822's flake-check job passed (30m44s, cold rebuild) but hit the *same broken pre-fix cache* (nix-Linux-fda31e3e..., created 03:46:20, 835MB, no GHC) because the cache key is flake.lock/flake.nix-hash-only and purge-primary-key:never means a primary-key hit never re-saves. Manually deleted both stale nix-Linux-fda31e3e... cache entries (ids 6770608855, 6767730733) via gh cache delete so the next run treats it as a genuine miss and saves a corrected cache. Next master push should confirm restore time drops on the run after that.
close_reason: Fixed in 00e6a2e: nix flake check now uses --no-build (eval only, validates devShells without building HLS) plus an explicit nix build of just the checks derivations. Keeps HLS/devShell closure out of the store so the existing 6G GC cap fits both GHC toolchains without evicting the compiler. Confirm cache effectiveness on next CI run.
